job.title: Art Manager
job.description:
Manage process, traffic and materials for large multi-part projects, based on the overall direction of the Senior Creative Director, in service of business needs. Oversee daily hands-on design and production within the FCP Creative Development Department and ensure smooth transitions of information and files between project team partners and colleagues. Track jobs and monitor progress on projects and identify potential scheduling issues, using workflow/traffic management systems. Provide technical counsel and answer questions on production issues. Proof interim versions of specs sheets for accuracy before final approval round and oversee accuracy of final materials sent to vendors. Assist Senior Creative Director with review of Licensing and Global Partnership materials (revisions to submissions for Licensing and to environment and product mockups for GP). Provide backup support for Senior Creative Director during travel/absence. Assist in the writing and preparation of reports and documents such as RFPs and presentation materials. 

Research, design and produce graphic solutions for specific special projects (such as development of new products and processes); however, position is not primarily for design.

job.title: Senior Manager, Digital Marketing
job.description:
Feld Entertainment is seeking a strategic, hands-on Senior Digital Marketing Manager to lead the evolution and optimization of the company’s portfolio of consumer-facing digital experiences, including brand websites, mobile applications, campaign landing pages, and other owned digital platforms.

Supporting Monster Jam, SMX, Disney On Ice, Ringling, and other Feld Entertainment brands, this position will lead major digital initiatives from discovery and requirements gathering through design, development, launch, and ongoing optimization. The role will focus on creating intuitive, personalized, and high-performing experiences that connect fans with Feld’s brands, content, events, and ticketing opportunities.

Serving as the business and product owner for Feld’s digital platforms, the Senior Digital Marketing Manager will translate business objectives and user needs into technical requirements, functional specifications, platform roadmaps, and actionable development priorities. The role will partner closely with internal teams and external development partners to manage execution, project timelines, budgets, platform standards, and the customer journey.

Success in this role requires digital product leadership, marketing strategy, technical fluency, strong project management, and the ability to build alignment across Brand Marketing, IT, Ticketing, Ecommerce, Analytics, Creative Services, Legal, Operations, and external agencies.

job.title: Supercross Operations Manager
job.description: The Operations Manager leads on-site Registration and Will Call for Supercross events, including hiring, scheduling, and supervising seasonal staff and handling registration documents and Will Call funds. The role also manages credentials, tour hotel contracts and rooming lists, unit-level travel and accommodations, budget accounting support, team and crew packets, event supplies and apparel, summary reports, and summit presentations. The ideal candidate is organized, able to manage multiple priorities and deadlines, and comfortable working both independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced touring environment.

job.title: Transportation Manager - CDL
job.description: The CDL Class A Semi Truck Driver is responsible for safely operating and transporting a full-size tractor-trailer and specialized Red Plate Mobile Medical Services trailer throughout the United States for all 31 rounds of the SuperMotocross (SMX) season, including Monster Energy Supercross, Pro Motocross, and the SMX Playoffs. This is a high-travel, season-long position requiring extended periods on the road. The driver remains with the truck and trailer at race locations throughout each event weekend to support security, readiness, setup, breakdown, and event logistics.

job.title: 2027 Graduate Programme - Asia
job.description:
Pave your career path with FGS Global

We are the best at what we do because we hire people who are open-minded, collaborative and bring diverse perspectives to the table.  

If you’re looking to be challenged, want to learn and progress in a fast-paced environment, and have excellent written and verbal communication skills, we want to get to know you.  

We work for some of the world’s most successful and interesting businesses, institutions and individuals helping to tell their stories to multiple stakeholders including investors, media, employees and government. The exceptional quality of our people is crucial to our success as a company and how we serve our clients.

We help our clients navigate today’s fast-moving and interconnected world to win support from the people who are interested in them. The knowledge, creativity, and passion our people bring to this work is why we are a leader in our field.

Do you want to join a world-leading strategic communications consultancy?

We’re now welcoming applications for our 2027 Asia Graduate Programme

With five offices across the Asia region, you will be applying to join our brilliant team in one of the following locations: Beijing, Hong Kong, Shanghai or Singapore.

During the graduate programme you will get the opportunity to work on high-stakes, business-critical projects that span some of the world’s largest companies and most complex situations faced by organisations. You’ll encounter issues that make up the global news agenda of the time.

If you are interested in other opportunities, please visit our Join Us page. Candidates who are interested in applying to our graduate programme in the UK or Middle East must submit a separate application for these markets and adhere to the respective application processes.

What the programme will involve

Successful applicants will be enrolled on in a 2-year structured programme, learning both on-the-job and through formal trainings to help develop your knowledge and skillset across key areas of strategic communications and capital markets advisory. You will have the chance to put these skills to use across a variety of exciting and impactful client mandates.

You will be based in one of our Asia offices but working in close collaboration with clients and colleagues across the Asia region and our international offices. We are a global business, and we work collaboratively across time zones.

Our people love the work they do, and the people they do it with, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to get to know your local and global colleagues both socially and professionally.

Through the application process, we select individuals for this programme who we believe will pioneer the future of FGS Global. The intention is for us to invest in your development, and you to receive a truly immersive learning experience that challenges you and allows you to demonstrate your own entrepreneurial flare, growing with the firm. The expectation is that you will continue with us after the programme ends as a full-time Senior Associate.

Who are we looking for?

  • We are looking for motivated and proactive graduates who welcome a steep learning curve and the chance to collaborate with a wide range of people.
  • The role requires individuals who are interested and engaged in how different stakeholders communicate – be it through news outlets, investor presentations, social media, keynote events, or face-to-face conversations.
  • We want applicants who are interested in the news agenda, and track emerging issues and current challenges facing society today.
  • In doing so we want people who will bring their own dynamism and knowledge of how companies and organisations communicate, for example the changing world of digital and social media communications.
  • Successful candidates will be able to demonstrate that they embody the values our people live by: being ambitious together, working hard while keeping energy levels high, striving for excellence and taking responsibility in all they do.
  • We care for and uplift those around us, and expect anyone who joins our team to do their part.

What we offer you in return

  • We are a diverse, dynamic and caring group of people. We motivate each other, strive to deliver to a brilliant standard and we take the time to celebrate together and learn lessons to improve.
  • You will have the opportunity to work with leading communications professionals, learning from the brightest minds in the industry who come from a diverse background.
  • You will be working on a diverse mix of clients, across industries, sectors and geographies.
  • You will have continuous training and development throughout the programme, with dedicated mentors.
  • You will be given the platform to innovate and trusted to demonstrate your entrepreneurial flare.
  • You will have access to a range of office perks, location-dependent, including regular team socials, flexible and remote working policies, gym and wellness allowances, and private health and dental care.
  • A competitive salary benchmarked against others in the industry and reviewed regularly, on an annual basis.
  • Candidates applying from abroad will receive relocation support, including flights and assistance with accommodation and visa applications.
  • At the beginning of the programme, we require you to be in the office full time. After this, we expect all colleagues to be in the office the majority of the working week, however we do offer flexibility to work from home at least one day a week.

Visa, language and relocation requirements

Asia

  • Exceptional English language skills (written and verbal) are essential and proficiency in a relevant Asian language is preferable.
  • For candidates looking to join our Hong Kong, Shanghai or Beijing offices, it is necessary to have a high-level of proficiency in Chinese (written and verbal)
  • We will support candidates with their visa application; for those candidates looking to join our offices in Beijing, Shanghai and Singapore, it is important that you have the right to work in these markets.
  • Candidates must be able to relocate by start of August 2027 to begin work by the middle of August

How the application process works

Step 1. We will ask you to fill out a short form and send us your CV and we will also ask you to address an FGS Global-specific case study analysis task that is designed to highlight the brightest, most creative graduates. This task is an opportunity for you to demonstrate your research skills, creative thinking and ability to communicate complex ideas in a simple way.

For the instructions for the task please click here.

Your completed case study analysis should be structured as a 1–2-page summary in English, providing a focused, well-organized overview of your findings.

We appreciate that this task takes a lot of work, but it gives us the opportunity to assess in a completely objective way based on your abilities and talents.

Your case study analysis and CV must be submitted in PDF format. This application must be completed by Friday 19th March 2027 at 23:59 HKT – late applications will not be accepted.

Step 2. Shortlisted candidates will be sent an online written assessment, and if you are applying for a position in one of our locations where Asian language skills are required, we will ask you to complete an assessment in this language

Step 3. We will host a series of assessments including group tasks, problem solving exercises and interviews the week of 19th April 2027. Further details of the final assessment phase will be announced in due course.

Successful applicants will start full-time on 9th August 2027.

 

For more in depth information please refer to our Grad Programme Website.

job.title: 2027 Graduate Programme - United Kingdom
job.description:
UK Graduate Programme 2027

Pave your career path with FGS Global

We are the best at what we do because we hire people who are open-minded, collaborative and bring diverse perspectives to the table.

If you’re looking to be challenged, want to learn and progress in a fast-paced environment, and have excellent written and verbal communication skills, we want to get to know you.

2027 UK Graduate Programme

We work for some of the world’s most successful and interesting businesses, institutions and individuals helping them to shape and safeguard reputations, and succeed in critical moments. We help leaders engage with multiple stakeholders including investors, media, employees and government. We do this in a range of ways, crafting communication strategies encompassing everything from traditional media through to the latest digital channels and content creation.

What sets us apart has always been clear in the work: the ability to anticipate what's next, influence what matters, and orchestrate outcomes that hold. The knowledge, creativity and passion our people is crucial to our success as a company and why we are a leader in our field.

Do you want to join a world-leading strategic leadership advisory firm?

We’re now welcoming applications for our 2027 UK Graduate Programme

You will be applying for the UK office in London, where you will join one of our brilliant teams

During the graduate programme you will get the opportunity to work on high-stakes, business-critical projects that span some of the world’s largest companies and most complex situations faced by organisations. You’ll encounter issues that make up the global news agenda of the time.

If you are interested in other opportunities, please visit our Join Us page. 

What the programme will involve

The UK graduate programme is based in London but offers our graduates the opportunity to work with colleagues and clients around our international offices. We are a global business, and we work collaboratively across time zones.

Throughout your application for the UK Graduate programme, you will have the opportunity to indicate a preference for one of three pathways:

  • Core consulting – most of FGS Global’s UK activity takes place on this pathway, including Transaction & Financial Communications, Strategy & Reputation and Crisis and Issues Management practices.
  • Digital & creative – This pathway is an opportunity to join the Edmonds Elder by FGS Global team, which offer world leading digital and creative content strategies. This pathway will either mean working very closely with Edmonds Elder or potentially directly as part of their team, depending on your skillset.
  • UK Public Affairs, Policy & Intelligence – This pathway is to work as part of our specialist public affairs and policy offering, which helps clients engage with the UK political environment, and working closely with our colleagues in Brussels, Washington D.C. and all over the world.  

The graduate programme will begin with two joint-training weeks for all participants to truly immerse you in our culture and the type of work we do. Following this, you’ll spend six-months in a structured training and mentorship programme along one of our three pathways, learning both on-the-job and through formal trainings to help develop your knowledge and skillset across communications. This will be across a range of audiences including those involved in public affairs, the media, investors, employees and government.

Our people love the work they do, and the people they do it with, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to get to know your local and global colleagues both socially and professionally.

Through the application process, we select individuals for this programme that we believe will pioneer the future of FGS Global. The intention is for us to invest in your development, and for you to receive a truly immersive learning experience that challenges you and allows you to demonstrate your own entrepreneurial flare. The expectation is that you continue with us after the programme ends as a full-time Associate without any further interviews or assessment.  

Who are we looking for?

  • We are looking for motivated and proactive graduates who welcome a steep learning curve and the chance to collaborate with a wide range of people
  • All roles require individuals who are interested and engaged in how different stakeholders communicate – be it through news outlets, investor presentations, social media, keynote events, or face-to-face conversations
  • We want applicants who are interested in the news agenda, and track emerging issues and current challenges facing society today
  • We want people who will bring their own dynamism and knowledge of how companies and organisations communicate, for example the changing world of digital and social media communications
  • Our core pathway is suited to a wide range of backgrounds and skillsets in line with the criteria above, while the Creative & Digital pathway is best suited to those with a flair for content production and design. While not explicitly required, UK Public Affairs pathway applicants will benefit from a strong understanding of the Westminster system and UK political dynamics
  • Successful candidates will be able to demonstrate that they embody the values our people live by: being ambitious together, working hard while keeping energy levels high, striving for excellence and taking responsibility in all they do
  • We care for and uplift those around us, and expect anyone who joins our team to do their part

 

What we offer you in return

  • We are a diverse, dynamic and caring group of people. We motivate each other, strive to deliver to a brilliant standard and we take the time to celebrate together and learn lessons to improve
  • You will have the opportunity to work with leading communications professionals, learning from the brightest minds in the industry who come from a diverse background
  • You will be working on a diverse mix of clients, across industries, sectors and geographies
  • You will have continuous training and development throughout the programme, with dedicated mentors
  • You will be given the platform to innovate and trusted to demonstrate your entrepreneurial flare
  • You will have access to a range of office perks including regular team socials, free tickets to exhibitions, company discounts, and flexible working policies
  • A competitive salary benchmarked against others in the industry, and we review Associate salaries every six months in line with formal appraisals. We also offer a number of other benefits including gym membership and private health and dental care
  • At the beginning of the programme, we require you to be in the office full time. After this, we expect all colleagues to be in the office the majority of the working week, however we do offer flexibility to work from home at least one day a week

 

Visa, language and relocation requirements

UK

  • Fluent and native-standard English is essential
  • Candidates must have a right to work in the UK
  • Candidates must be able to relocate by the end of August 2027 to begin work on 6th September 2027

 

How the application process works

Step 1. We have developed an FGS Global-specific task that is designed to highlight the brightest, most creative graduates. It will be an opportunity for you to demonstrate your research skills, creative thinking and ability to communicate complex ideas in a simple way. This must be completed in a presentation.

We will also ask you to fill out a short form and send us your CV, as well as specifying which pathway you are most interested in (don’t worry – you can specify interest in more than one). We appreciate the task takes a lot of work, but it gives us the opportunity to assess in a completely blind way based on your abilities and talents.

Presentations and CV’s must be submitted in PDF format. This application must be completed by Friday 15th January 2027 at 23:59 GMT – late applications will not be accepted.  

Our Step 1 review process is entirely anonymous. All application tasks and CVs are assessed blindly with personal identifying information removed prior to review.

Step 2. Successful candidates will be interviewed virtually between 8th and 26th February 2027 and told whether they are through to the final shortlist for our assessment day. You will also take an online scenario test simulating tasks we undertake.

Step 3. We will host an in-person assessment day at our London office on 23rd  April 2027. Further details of the assessment day will be announced in due course.

Successful applicants will start full time in on 6th September 2027.

Apply now

If you’re ready to launch your career and start your journey in strategic communications, apply before Friday 15th January.

job.title: Account Payable Accountant
job.description:
Account Payable Accountant 

 

Overview of the Firm   

FGS Global helps the world's most influential leaders move minds and markets. Working where business, government, and public opinion intersect, we advise CEOs, boards, and leadership teams at the most consequential moments.  

We work as one team across geographies and disciplines - bringing together specialists with backgrounds in communications, finance, law, government, journalism, data science, and digital. Whatever the moment demands, we combine multidimensional perspectives to help leaders anticipate what's next, engage the stakeholders who matter, and drive meaningful outcomes. 

Across 31 global offices, we draw on the full depth of the firm so clients can operate with clarity, act with confidence, and lead with trust. This collaborative approach has established FGS as a market leader: we are consistently ranked Band 1 for Crisis & Risk Management and Litigation Support by Chambers and Partners, and were ranked the #1 Global M&A PR firm by deal value and deal count for four consecutive years (Mergermarket, 2025). 

 

The Role  

You will play a pivotal role in facilitating daily accounting and payment operations across the firm in Hong Kong. 

You will collaborate closely with consultants, client teams, and finance colleagues to ensure the seamless and accurate processing of financial transactions. 

 

Responsibilities 

  • Process accounts payable transactions, including office expenses, client project payments, staff reimbursements, corporate card expenses, and travel-related invoices 
  • Handle banking activities, including cheque deposits and collections, telegraphic transfers, and other payment arrangements 
  • Perform daily bank reconciliations and ensure the accuracy of financial records 
  • Assist in preparing accounting schedules, reconciliations, and ad hoc finance reports 
  • Support month-end closing activities and maintain proper documentation for audit and compliance purposes 
  • Liaise with internal stakeholders regarding payment requests, invoice enquiries, and expense claims 
  • Assist with administrative duties and contribute to ongoing process improvement initiatives within the finance team 
  • Provide cross-functional support to team members when required 

Desired Skills & Qualities 

  • Minimum 5 years of accounting experience gained from a professional services firm or multinational corporate environment 
  • Exposure to accounts payable, expense processing, and bank reconciliations 
  • Experience using NetSuite is an advantage 
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications to run reports and do analysis 
  • Strong attention to detail with good organisational and analytical skills 
  • Effective communication skills in English and Cantonese 
  • A proactive team player with a positive and professional attitude

job.title: Accounting Manager / Senior Accounting Manager
job.description:
Overview of the Firm 

FGS Global helps the world's most influential leaders move minds and markets. Working where business, government, and public opinion intersect, we advise CEOs, boards, and leadership teams at the most consequential moments.

We work as one team across geographies and disciplines - bringing together specialists with backgrounds in communications, finance, law, government, journalism, data science, and digital. Whatever the moment demands, we combine multidimensional perspectives to help leaders anticipate what's next, engage the stakeholders who matter, and drive meaningful outcomes.

Across 31 global offices, we draw on the full depth of the firm so clients can operate with clarity, act with confidence, and lead with trust. This collaborative approach has established FGS as a market leader: we are consistently ranked Band 1 for Crisis & Risk Management and Litigation Support by Chambers and Partners, and were ranked the #1 Global M&A PR firm by deal value and deal count for four consecutive years (Mergermarket, 2025).

 

The Role

We are seeking an experienced and hands-on Accounting Manager to join our Asia finance team in Hong Kong. Reporting to the Head of Finance, Asia, and working closely with the Finance Operations Senior Manager, this role plays a key part in the accounting operations of the firm across the Hong Kong, Singapore, and China entities, with key responsibility for the month-end close, financial reporting, and tax compliance, as well as supporting the statutory and group audits. The role places a strong focus on income statement analysis to provide insight into revenue and cost performance.

The ideal candidate will be a qualified accountant who combines strong technical knowledge with a hands-on approach, takes accountability for their deliverables, and communicates clearly with senior internal and external stakeholders. They will be comfortable operating in a fast-paced professional services environment and contributing to continuous improvement in processes and controls. Experience with VAT/GST filing across Singapore and China jurisdictions will be highly regarded.

 

Responsibilities

  • Reporting to Head of Finance, this role is a key Act as a key member to perform the month-end closing, including revenue recognition, accruals, balance sheet reconciliations and variance analysis.
  • Work closely with Global Accounting Team to drive alignment and compliance with Group Policy and Accounting Standards and to support audits and tax filings.
  • Perform detailed monthly income statement analysis, explaining revenue and cost movements against prior periods, budget and forecast, and identifying trends, anomalies and risks.
  • Ensure departmental costs are accurately recorded, coded, and allocated to the correct cost centres, reviewing cost reports and resolving variances with budget holders on a timely basis.
  • Review and deliver monthly, quarterly, and annual financial and management reports, providing analysis and commentary on key variances to the Head of Finance and regional leadership.
  • Support the statutory and group audit processes together with Senior Manager, Finance Operations .
  • Manage tax filing obligations across Hong Kong, Singapore, and China, including GST/VAT compliance, corporate income tax, and withholding tax matters, and liaise with external tax advisers.
  • Partner with operational teams on cost budgeting and reforecasting to support business to drive cost control.
  • Proactively identify opportunities to drive cost optimisation, analysing spending trends and recommending practical cost-saving initiatives to the Head of Finance and business leaders.
  • Partner with global finance teams and external service providers on group reporting, intercompany, and consolidation matters.
  • Maintain and strengthen internal controls and accounting policies, and drive process and system improvements to enhance efficiency in the Asia finance function.
  • Support ad hoc finance projects as required.

 

Desired Skills & Qualities

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or a related discipline from a recognised university.
  • A recognised professional accounting qualification (e.g. HKICPA, ACCA, CPA) is required.
  • 10-15 years of relevant accounting experience, preferably in a professional services or multinational environment. Audit firm experience is an advantage.
  • Solid technical accounting knowledge, with experience applying US GAAP and/or IFRS/HKFRS.
  • Strong analytical skills with a proven track record in income statement analysis, able to translate financial results into clear, actionable insights for business leaders.
  • Proven experience supporting statutory audits and managing tax filings across multiple jurisdictions; familiarity with Singapore GST and China VAT filing will be highly considered.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel; experience with ERP or accounting systems such as NetSuite is strongly preferred.
  • Strong team player, with the ability to guide and support junior team members.
  • Hands-on, highly organised, and able to manage competing priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced and dynamic working environment.
  • Treasury experience is a plus but it is NOT a must.
  • Proactive, with excellent interpersonal and communication skills and the confidence to engage senior stakeholders, auditors, and advisers.
  • Fluency in written and spoken English and Cantonese is preferred and be ready to join global calls

job.title: Director, Media Planning and Placement
job.description:

FGS is seeking a Director to join our Media Planning & Placement team in our Washington, DC office. The Director will manage day-to-day execution of client advertising campaigns and lead the development of media plans, campaign performance reports and other client-ready deliverables.

Responsibilities

  • Work with clients and internal teams to devise advertising campaign strategy and campaign plans
  • Independently run paid media accounts, managing the day-to-day operations while anticipating client issues and concerns proactively
  • Support new business pitches and draft paid media proposals for existing and prospective clients
  • Interact with external vendors to ensure on-time delivery of plans, creative and performance data
  • Analyze campaign performance, prepare clear client reports and develop actionable recommendations
  • Coordinate with FGS Global Creative teams on campaign production, ad specs and delivery deadlines
  • Assist ad operations in campaign set up, including trafficking, pixel creation, QA/testing and other functions as needed
  • Day-to-day management of media buys, including making regular optimizations based on performance
  • Work with FGS Global finance staff to track and record invoices and vendor bills
  • Mentor junior Media Planning and Placement staff
  • Act as a subject matter expert on advertising, helping educate clients and internal teams on paid media opportunities and best practices
  • Conduct research and develop written materials to support advertising campaign strategy, media planning and client reporting

Attributes

  • A BA/BS degree in a related field, plus 6-10 years of relevant work experience (previous agency and/or public affairs experience preferred, but not required)
  • Experience working in one or more self-serve ad platforms (Meta, X, LinkedIn, Reddit, Google search, etc.) and experience working with an ad server (Campaign Manager 360 preferred)
  • Strong interest in all aspects of digital media and advertising
  • Detail-oriented with exceptional critical thinking and problem-solving abilities  
  • Strong quantitative and analytical skills  
  • Ability to combine strategic thinking with creative problem-solving
  • Ability to prioritize, multi-task, work successfully with teams, and work under pressure

  • Comfort working in a fast-paced and ever-changing environment

The salary range for this role in Washington, DC is $130,000-$170,000.

job.title: Intern Strategic Corporate & Transaction Communication
job.description:
Intern Strategic Corporate & Transaction Communication

FGS Global helps the world's most influential leaders move minds and markets. Working where business, government, and public opinion intersect, we advise CEOs, boards, and leadership teams at the most consequential moments. 

We work as one team across geographies and disciplines - bringing together specialists with backgrounds in communications, finance, law, government, journalism, data science, and digital. Whatever the moment demands, we combine multidimensional perspectives to help leaders anticipate what's next, engage the stakeholders who matter, and drive meaningful outcomes.

Across 31 global offices, we draw on the full depth of the firm so clients can operate with clarity, act with confidence, and lead with trust. This collaborative approach has established FGS as a market leader: we are consistently ranked Band 1 for Crisis & Risk Management and Litigation Support by Chambers and Partners, and were ranked the #1 Global M&A PR firm by deal value and deal count for four consecutive years (Mergermarket, 2025).

 

Join our team in Amsterdam as Intern Strategic Corporate & Transaction Communication starting February 1st 2027.

 

What tasks can you look forward to?

  • As an intern, you will be part of the team from day one and experience everyday life as a communications consultant at first hand.
  • You will support the project teams in the development and implementation of communication strategies for national and international clients in matters of strategic corporate communication and positioning.
  • The topics range from M&A transactions, IPOs and strategic realignments to the communication of digitalization and transformation strategies.
  • Together with our team, you will design compelling communications materials for internal and external stakeholders (e.g., communications plans, press releases, corporate presentations).
  • You follow, monitor and understand Dutch and European media.
  • You help with ad-hoc requests and questions from other offices about the media, economy, and society in the Netherlands.
  • For research and analysis, you will dig deep into relevant topics, exciting companies, media coverage and trends.
  • You bring in fresh, inspiring ideas and innovative communications formats.

 

What should you bring along?

  • You are at the end of your undergraduate or master's degree - the subject is less important than your enthusiasm for communication.
  • Ideally, you have already gained practical experience during your studies, for example in communications, finance, journalism, politics and/or strategy consulting.
  • You are a quick learner and it is recommended that you communicate fluently in Dutch and very well in English.
  • You have a good understanding of the Dutch media landscape.
  • You love variety and new challenges and really thrive when working in a team.

 

What we can offer you

  • The opportunity to get to know strategic communications consulting
  • Insights into the activities of a leading strategic communications consultancy as well as into various industries and areas of expertise as part of our integrated project teams
  • Exciting and varied tasks in an international and inspiring working environment
  • The opportunity to benefit from training & development opportunities
  • Induction and individual support as well as detailed feedback from an experienced consultant
  • A committed, collegial and constantly growing team in which mutual appreciation and team spirit are paramount
  • A company culture that combines excellence with team spirit
  • The opportunity to work flexibly both in our offices and from home
  • Our beautiful office in the heart of Amsterdam- Zuid

 

Don’t meet every single requirement? Please don’t worry! Studies have shown that some groups like women or people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single requirement. At FGS Global, we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. So, if you’re excited about this role and our company but your previous professional experience doesn’t match perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we would like to encourage you to apply anyway. You may just be the right candidate for this or another role.

We look forward to your complete application (incl. all relevant academic and professional certificates and/or reference letters). Feel free to contact us by email via careers-eu@fgsglobal.com.

 More information: FGS Global

Our Washington, DC office, located a few blocks from the National Mall, is seeking a highly motivated, organized, and detail-oriented student for a part-time winter/spring internship within our Research & Insights division. As an intern in our office, you will have the opportunity to work gain hands-on experience working alongside our teams of dedicated and talented communications professionals.

RESPONSIBILITIES

While intern tasks vary, a typical workload consists of short- and long-term research projects, including assisting with qualitative research such as focus groups and in-depth interviews, quantitative research such as online surveys, and synthetic research. The intern is also tasked with keeping up to date on current public polling trends and topics and assisting with public opinion PowerPoint decks that are published on the FGS Global website. In addition, the intern provides general assistance (proofing, number-checking, etc.) and note-taking on research projects as needed to the Insights team. 

REQUIREMENTS

  • An in-progress BA/BS in a related field, with a preference for third and fourth year students
  • Ability to devote 2-3 full office days to the internship
  • Research experience not required, but preferred
  • Strong analytic, writing, attention to detail and editing skills are required 
  • Problem-solver and strong communicator 
  • A demonstrated capacity for communication, teamwork and collegiality within a tight-knit team

job.title: Acting Commissioning Editor, Arts
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

 

Our commitment to inclusion and fairness

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

 

The role

The FT’s arts desk is looking for a commissioning editor to work across the team’s print and digital content on a three-day a week basis to cover a period of parental leave.

The successful applicant will have had several years experience in arts journalism and relish working across a broad range of content, from film and television to music, theatre, visual art, dance, opera and gaming.

 

Your skills

  • Excellent editing skills, with the ability to turn around copy speedily and accurately
  • The ability to conjure up grabby headlines and standfirsts
  • A wide-ranging knowledge of and deep interest in the arts. A passion for pop culture would be a particular asset
  • A willingness to take on tasks big or small, including fact-checking and scheduling
  • A hard-working, ambitious journalist with an eye for detail
  • The ability to collaborate effectively with freelance and staff writers
  • Adept social media skills
  • A creative thinker with a strong teamwork ethic

 

The arts desk produces a wealth of articles online and in print, working to both long and short lead times. This position is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment.

 

Key responsibilities

  • Edit regular reviews that need to be speedily published
  • Fact-check articles
  • Keep in touch with arts and entertainment publicists to maintain a schedule of upcoming events that we may want to feature
  • Manage our digital publishing schedule
  • Maintain schedules with freelance writers
  • Commission features
  • Work with the picture editor on all aspects of story presentation across print, mobile and digital platforms

 

Please submit your application by the end of the day, Monday 30th November 2026.

 

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not by default use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

 

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

FT Newsroom staff are expected to work onsite a minimum of three days per week, subject to role requirements and regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for Editorial roles.

 

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

*LI-RS1

The FT's B2B division licenses content and information solutions to organisations worldwide. We're looking for a driven Business Development Manager to grow our corporate licensing business across the Banking and Financial Services sector in North America.

You'll develop and implement a strategic sales plan, build relationships with senior decision-makers and win new business.   • Develop and implement a strategic sales plan to drive growth across the North American Banking and Financial Services sector.
  • Take ownership of achieving annual new business revenue targets.
  • Handle the assigned travel budget efficiently, prioritising face-to-face meetings with prospective clients.
  • Collaborate with the marketing team to identify and deliver activities that support new business acquisition.
  • Work closely with customer success colleagues to find opportunities and coordinate activities that drive new business.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with senior decision-makers and key collaborators at prospective client organisations.

  • Experience in solution-based sales, ideally within the online information or subscription services industry.

  • Well-developed influencing and negotiation skills, with the ability to secure commitment from prospective clients and internal collaborators.

While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for all roles. We believe this balanced approach supports flexibility and protects our culture, making collaboration and communication easier, building stronger relationships and team cohesion, and supporting peer learning. We reserve discretion on reasonable notice to change this approach either generally or for specific individuals or teams.

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

Further information

A reasonable estimate of the salary range for this role is 90,000-95,000, along with a commission package. To ensure pay fairness, the successful candidate will be offered a salary within the estimated salary range based on a number of considerations including but not limited to: skills; experience and training; certifications; and other business and organisational needs. The disclosed range estimate is for our NYC office and has not been adjusted for other locations.

At the FT, we embrace innovation and the use of technology and appreciate that individuals may use AI tools as part of their job application process. Whilst we are happy for you to use AI to assist with your application, it is essential that all information provided is authentic and accurately represents your skills, experience, and qualifications.

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process may be monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

Please beware of fraudulent job postings and offers claiming to be from the Financial Times. All legitimate opportunities will direct you to apply through the official Financial Times careers site, and the FT will never ask for financial information, payments, or referrals to third parties during the hiring process. If you have any concerns about the legitimacy of a job posting or suspect any scam activity, please contact talent@ft.com.

The Reader Revenue Group (RRG) unites the subscription and licensing businesses of the Financial Times. This allows crafting opportunities for broader, deeper, and longer-term relationships globally.

Within RRG, Corporate Licensing provides FT content to organisations worldwide through solutions ranging from group and enterprise subscriptions to customised data feeds. Our Americas team works collaboratively to strengthen customer relationships and drive sustainable commercial growth.

We are looking for an experienced Client Relationship Manager to lead and grow a portfolio of Corporate and Government customers throughout the Americas.

In this role, you will take charge of customer retention, revenue growth, and renewal strategy. You will build diligent connections with senior partners and see opportunities to grow accounts over time.

This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys handling sophisticated customer relationships, navigating commercial discussions and delivering long-term value to clients.

Key responsibilities

  • Deliver agreed retention and revenue growth targets, taking ownership of portfolio performance, account strategy and forecasting.
  • Develop strategic account plans to protect existing revenue, identify renewal risks and pursue opportunities for growth.

  • Analyse customer engagement, account performance and market developments to find opportunities for retention and growth.
  • Partner with Customer Success and other internal teams to coordinate account activity, resolve customer issues and deliver a consistent customer experience.
  • Stay informed about relevant market and competitor developments and confidently communicate the value of FT products and services.
  • Maintain accurate account records, commercial activity and pipeline forecasts in Salesforce.
  • Proactively plan renewal activity, handle contending priorities and ensure timely follow-up across a varied portfolio.
  • Collaborate with colleagues across the business to achieve shared customer and commercial objectives.

Required skills / experience

  • At least 2 years of experience handling B2B customer relationships or a revenue-generating portfolio, with a focus on retention and account growth.
  • Strong commercial judgment, with the confidence to lead renewal, negotiation and expansion discussions.
  • Shown ability to run multiple accounts, prioritize effectively and deliver against deadlines and commercial targets.
  • Excellent relationship-building and influencing skills, including experience engaging senior customer partners.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to understand customer needs and articulate a compelling value proposition.
  • A collaborative, customer-focused attitude, combined with the initiative to take ownership of work and follow through on commitments.
  • Experience using CRM systems to handle customer activity, pipeline information and forecasts.

Please submit your application by December 1st.

Desirable skills / experience

  • Experience working with Corporate or Government customers, including familiarity with formal procurement processes.
  • Experience using Salesforce and Google Workspace.
  • Knowledge of Corporate and Government sectors across the Americas.

A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

The role 

The Credit Controller is responsible for managing assigned customer accounts, ensuring timely collection of outstanding receivables, minimising overdue debt, and maintaining strong customer relationships. The role supports the achievement of cash collection targets, Debt Within Terms (DWT), and other key Accounts Receivable (AR) performance indicators.

Key responsibilities

Credit Control & Collections

  • Proactively manage assigned customer accounts and follow up on outstanding invoices.
  • Ensure timely collection of payments in line with agreed credit terms.
  • Monitor aged receivables and prioritise high-value and overdue accounts.
  • Obtain payment commitments and follow through until settlement.
  • Escalate overdue balances and payment risks when necessary.

Account Reconciliation & Dispute Resolution

  • Perform customer account reconciliations and resolve outstanding discrepancies.
  • Investigate invoice disputes, missing purchase orders (POs), and payment delays.
  • Coordinate with Sales, Billing, Accounts Receivable, and other stakeholders to resolve issues.
  • Ensure unapplied payments, credit notes, and account adjustments are addressed promptly.

Customer & Stakeholder Management

  • Maintain professional relationships with customers and internal stakeholders.
  • Respond promptly to customer enquiries and payment-related concerns.
  • Work closely with Sales and Commercial teams to resolve collection challenges.
  • Support customer meetings and account reviews when required.

Reporting & Performance Management

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date collection notes and customer account records.
  • Monitor and contribute to key performance indicators, including Debt Within Terms (DWT), aged debt, and cash collections.
  • Provide regular updates on overdue accounts, payment commitments, and collection risks.
  • Support weekly and monthly debt reviews and cash forecasting.

Process Compliance & Continuous Improvement

  • Follow established credit management policies, procedures, and internal controls.
  • Ensure accurate documentation and compliance with audit and SOX requirements.
  • Identify opportunities to improve collection efficiency and reduce overdue debt.
  • Support month-end closing activities and other AR operational requirements.

Required skills and experience 

  • Previous experience in Credit Control, Accounts Receivable, Collections, or Finance.
  • Strong communication, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple customer accounts and prioritise workloads effectively.
  • Strong attention to detail and analytical skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and financial systems, preferably Oracle Fusion.
  • Experience with customer payment portals and invoicing platforms is an advantage.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Debt Within Terms (DWT) performance.
  • Reduction of overdue and aged receivables.
  • Achievement of monthly cash collection targets.
  • Timely resolution of customer disputes and payment issues.
  • Accuracy of collection notes and account reconciliations.
  • Compliance with internal controls and operational deadlines

job.title: Engineering Lead – ERP Services
job.description:
About Us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Together, we help audiences stay better informed and deepen their understanding of the world around them.

Our Product & Tech teams drive us forward in an ever-evolving digital landscape, delivering cutting-edge products to over one million digital subscribers daily. Our growth relies on a diverse, dedicated and dynamic group of product, tech, delivery and data specialists.

With a supportive culture, entrepreneurial spirit and opportunities at every turn, there are no limits to where your FT career can take you.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

About you

You are an experienced engineering leader with strong knowledge of ERP or similarly complex enterprise platforms and a track record of leading teams responsible for business-critical technology.

You combine people leadership with credible technical judgement. You are comfortable setting direction, making engineering decisions and working with your team on complex technical problems, while creating the ownership and autonomy for engineers to succeed.

You understand that enterprise platform engineering goes beyond implementing configuration or coordinating vendors. You think about the entire technology capability: the core platform, integrations, data flows, extensions, operational processes, security, resilience and how the platform evolves over time.

You are comfortable working closely with Finance and other business stakeholders, translating priorities and requirements into sustainable technology solutions and constructively challenging approaches that create unnecessary complexity or risk.

You are also interested in building capability. You can identify gaps in skills and knowledge, develop engineers and create a team that understands and genuinely owns its technology rather than relying disproportionately on individual specialists or external partners.

About the team

ERP Services sits within Corporate Technology, part of Internal Products, and owns the engineering capabilities supporting critical Finance and enterprise business processes across the FT.

The team is responsible for the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of our ERP technology estate, including Oracle Fusion and the integrations, data flows and supporting capabilities that connect it to the wider FT technology landscape.

ERP Services works closely with Finance, Product, Architecture, Integration & Engineering Services, Security and other Corporate Technology teams to ensure these critical enterprise capabilities remain reliable and can evolve as the needs of the organisation change.

We are strengthening the engineering leadership and platform expertise within ERP Services as part of a wider evolution of the Corporate Technology operating model. The Engineering Lead will establish clear platform and team ownership, reporting to the Principal Engineer – Corporate Technology.

What you’ll work on

As Engineering Lead – ERP Services, you will own the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of the FT’s ERP technology capability.

You will lead the ERP engineering team, providing people leadership, technical direction and clear accountability for the health and performance of the platforms and services the team owns.

A key part of the role will be strengthening our internal ERP engineering capability. You will develop the technical knowledge of the team, establish clear ownership of platforms and services and ensure we have the skills and understanding required to operate and evolve our ERP estate effectively.

You will work closely with Product and Finance stakeholders to understand business priorities and translate them into engineering plans, balancing new capabilities and business change with platform health, technical debt and operational investment.

You will also work with the Principal Engineer and Architecture to ensure decisions within ERP Services support the longer-term direction of Corporate Technology and the wider FT technology estate.

Your responsibilities will include

Engineering & Platform Ownership

  • Owning the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of the ERP technology capability.
  • Providing clear technical direction for the platforms, integrations and supporting services owned by ERP Services.
  • Ensuring ERP platforms remain secure, resilient, scalable, maintainable and appropriately supported.
  • Establishing clear ownership across the team for systems, integrations and technical capabilities.
  • Ensuring engineering decisions consider reliability, security, operability, maintainability, cost and long-term sustainability.
  • Maintaining visibility of platform health, technical debt, lifecycle risks and significant dependencies.
  • Working with the Principal Engineer and Architecture on material technical decisions and longer-term platform direction.
  • Ensuring the team maintains sufficient technical understanding of its platforms to make informed decisions and challenge external recommendations.

People & Engineering Leadership

  • Leading, supporting and developing the engineers within ERP Services.
  • Setting clear expectations and providing regular coaching, feedback and career development.
  • Building a team culture based on ownership, accountability, collaboration and constructive technical challenge.
  • Developing ERP and enterprise platform expertise across the team rather than allowing critical knowledge to remain concentrated in individuals.
  • Identifying capability and skills gaps and developing plans to address them through development, recruitment or appropriate external expertise.
  • Creating opportunities for engineers to take greater technical ownership and develop their leadership capability.
  • Supporting recruitment and building a resilient team with the skills required for the future ERP technology landscape.
  • Ensuring appropriate succession and knowledge sharing across critical areas.

Delivery & Planning

  • Working with Product to translate business priorities and technology strategy into clear engineering plans and deliverable outcomes.
  • Owning engineering planning and resource allocation within ERP Services.
  • Ensuring engineering capacity appropriately balances business change, platform improvement, operational work and technical debt.
  • Identifying technical dependencies, risks and constraints early and ensuring these are visible in planning and prioritisation.
  • Ensuring delivery commitments are realistic and supported by appropriate technical understanding.
  • Working across teams where initiatives involve multiple platforms, integrations or engineering capabilities.
  • Providing clear visibility of engineering progress, risks and trade-offs to Product, technology leadership and relevant stakeholders.

ERP Platform Evolution

  • Developing a clear understanding of the current ERP estate and identifying opportunities to simplify, modernise and improve it.
  • Working with Product, Architecture and the Principal Engineer to shape the longer-term evolution of ERP technology.
  • Evaluating platform capabilities and determining when requirements should be addressed through standard functionality, configuration, integration or other engineering approaches.
  • Challenging unnecessary customisation and complexity where more sustainable solutions are available.
  • Ensuring platform upgrades, new capabilities and significant changes are introduced safely and sustainably.
  • Understanding vendor roadmaps and assessing their implications for the FT's technology direction and investment decisions.
  • Ensuring technical debt and lifecycle concerns are actively managed rather than accumulating through incremental business change.

Integration & Enterprise Technology

  • Ensuring the team understands and owns the integrations and data flows connecting ERP with the wider FT technology estate.
  • Working closely with Integration & Engineering Services and other platform teams to establish clear ownership of cross-system capabilities.
  • Ensuring integrations follow appropriate FT engineering and architectural standards.
  • Identifying opportunities to simplify interfaces, reduce duplication and improve reliability.
  • Supporting technical decisions that span ERP, Tax, People and other Corporate Technology capabilities.
  • Ensuring changes within ERP appropriately consider downstream and upstream impacts.

Operational Excellence & Risk

  • Owning the operational performance of ERP Services and ensuring critical services are appropriately monitored and supported.
  • Establishing effective approaches to observability, incident management, problem management, change management and operational readiness.
  • Ensuring recurring incidents and operational problems are investigated to their underlying causes and addressed sustainably.
  • Maintaining appropriate approaches to resilience, disaster recovery and business continuity.
  • Ensuring relevant security, data governance, compliance and technology standards are met.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. You are an experienced engineering leader with strong knowledge of ERP or similarly complex enterprise platforms and a track record of leading teams responsible for business-critical technology.

You combine people leadership with credible technical judgement. You are comfortable setting direction, making engineering decisions and working with your team on complex technical problems, while creating the ownership and autonomy for engineers to succeed.

You understand that enterprise platform engineering goes beyond implementing configuration or coordinating vendors. You think about the entire technology capability: the core platform, integrations, data flows, extensions, operational processes, security, resilience and how the platform evolves over time.

You are comfortable working closely with Finance and other business stakeholders, translating priorities and requirements into sustainable technology solutions and constructively challenging approaches that create unnecessary complexity or risk.

You are also interested in building capability. You can identify gaps in skills and knowledge, develop engineers and create a team that understands and genuinely owns its technology rather than relying disproportionately on individual specialists or external partners.

About the team

ERP Services sits within Corporate Technology, part of Internal Products, and owns the engineering capabilities supporting critical Finance and enterprise business processes across the FT.

The team is responsible for the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of our ERP technology estate, including Oracle Fusion and the integrations, data flows and supporting capabilities that connect it to the wider FT technology landscape.

ERP Services works closely with Finance, Product, Architecture, Integration & Engineering Services, Security and other Corporate Technology teams to ensure these critical enterprise capabilities remain reliable and can evolve as the needs of the organisation change.

We are strengthening the engineering leadership and platform expertise within ERP Services as part of a wider evolution of the Corporate Technology operating model. The Engineering Lead will establish clear platform and team ownership, reporting to the Principal Engineer – Corporate Technology.

What you’ll work on

As Engineering Lead – ERP Services, you will own the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of the FT’s ERP technology capability.

You will lead the ERP engineering team, providing people leadership, technical direction and clear accountability for the health and performance of the platforms and services the team owns.

A key part of the role will be strengthening our internal ERP engineering capability. You will develop the technical knowledge of the team, establish clear ownership of platforms and services and ensure we have the skills and understanding required to operate and evolve our ERP estate effectively.

You will work closely with Product and Finance stakeholders to understand business priorities and translate them into engineering plans, balancing new capabilities and business change with platform health, technical debt and operational investment.

You will also work with the Principal Engineer and Architecture to ensure decisions within ERP Services support the longer-term direction of Corporate Technology and the wider FT technology estate.

Engineering & Platform Ownership

  • Providing clear technical direction for the platforms, integrations and supporting services owned by ERP Services.
  • Ensuring ERP platforms remain secure, resilient, scalable, maintainable and appropriately supported.
  • Establishing clear ownership across the team for systems, integrations and technical capabilities.
  • Ensuring engineering decisions consider reliability, security, operability, maintainability, cost and long-term sustainability.
  • Maintaining visibility of platform health, technical debt, lifecycle risks and significant dependencies.
  • Working with the Principal Engineer and Architecture on material technical decisions and longer-term platform direction.
  • Ensuring the team maintains sufficient technical understanding of its platforms to make informed decisions and challenge external recommendations.

People & Engineering Leadership

  • Leading, supporting and developing the engineers within ERP Services.
  • Setting clear expectations and providing regular coaching, feedback and career development.
  • Building a team culture based on ownership, accountability, collaboration and constructive technical challenge.
  • Developing ERP and enterprise platform expertise across the team rather than allowing critical knowledge to remain concentrated in individuals.
  • Identifying capability and skills gaps and developing plans to address them through development, recruitment or appropriate external expertise.
  • Creating opportunities for engineers to take greater technical ownership and develop their leadership capability.
  • Supporting recruitment and building a resilient team with the skills required for the future ERP technology landscape.
  • Ensuring appropriate succession and knowledge sharing across critical areas.

Delivery & Planning

  • Working with Product to translate business priorities and technology strategy into clear engineering plans and deliverable outcomes.
  • Owning engineering planning and resource allocation within ERP Services.
  • Ensuring engineering capacity appropriately balances business change, platform improvement, operational work and technical debt.
  • Identifying technical dependencies, risks and constraints early and ensuring these are visible in planning and prioritisation.
  • Ensuring delivery commitments are realistic and supported by appropriate technical understanding.
  • Working across teams where initiatives involve multiple platforms, integrations or engineering capabilities.
  • Providing clear visibility of engineering progress, risks and trade-offs to Product, technology leadership and relevant stakeholders.

ERP Platform Evolution

  • Developing a clear understanding of the current ERP estate and identifying opportunities to simplify, modernise and improve it.
  • Working with Product, Architecture and the Principal Engineer to shape the longer-term evolution of ERP technology.
  • Evaluating platform capabilities and determining when requirements should be addressed through standard functionality, configuration, integration or other engineering approaches.
  • Challenging unnecessary customisation and complexity where more sustainable solutions are available.

Integration & Enterprise Technology

job.description:

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.
