job.title: MULTIMEDIA JOURNALIST - KMOV
job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first and/or second highest-rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 of such markets that were measured by Nielsen in 2025. We also own the largest Telemundo Affiliate group with 46 markets and Gray Digital Media, a full-service digital agency offering national and local clients digital marketing strategies with the most advanced digital products and services. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, as well as studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KMOV:

We operate a CBS + ABC duopoly in one of America's great news towns. That means more platforms for your work — First Alert 4 newscasts, new ABC 32 newscasts, and all-day streaming.

KMOV is the most watched television/digital news operation in Missouri and Southern Illinois with nationally-recognized and award-winning news, weather, and investigative content found both on-air and online. KMOV won the prestigious national Edward R. Murrow Award for Best Newscast in 2023. Based in suburban St. Louis County, KMOV’s home is a new multi-million-dollar state-of-the-art broadcasting and digital facility. Ranked as the #1 city in the nation in 2022 for new college graduates, St. Louis is now recognized for its low cost of living, convenient transportation, and robust arts and entertainment scene. Home to the world-famous Arch, St. Louis Cardinals baseball, City STL soccer, and Blues hockey, St. Louis is quickly becoming THE place to be.

Job Summary/Description:

We are hiring an MMJ to find the best moments in the St. Louis region.’ This MMJ will identify moments as they are happening and deliver them to the audience first.   If your instinct is to capture the moment that everyone will be talking about — the video, the sound, the development that makes our coverage the original source even when everyone in St. Louis is on the same story — keep reading.  

What Winning Looks Like Here:

In St. Louis, First Alert means something. It's a promise: when it matters, we alert first, we stay out front, and we don't wait for the 5 p.m. show to tell people what happened at 2 p.m.

As our Audience-First MMJ, you will:

• Hunt moments, not soundbites. Lead every story with the most memorable moment from the field — off the top, not buried at :45.
• Be the original source. On the day's biggest story, make our video, our detail, our reporting the one everyone else has to credit. How do you separate when it's 4 cameras on the same scene? Show us.
• Put audience over linear. Yes, your stories will air in our traditional newscasts on First Alert 4 and ABC 32. But first, you think audience: you shoot, you send, you collaborate live with our Digital Content Center to post with urgency — stream it, push it, publish it now.
• Live in the field. You hate sitting around in meetings. So do we — for this role. Your desk is your car. Your assignment is to be out, building, finding, breaking.

What You Do Every Day:

• Enterprise, break, and own hard news and breaking news in the St. Louis market
• Build and work sources aggressively — not just for today, but for the next big one
• Shoot, write, edit compelling, tight, moment-driven stories for broadcast, streaming, and digital
• Go live with confidence and clarity, especially when news is breaking and unscripted
• Communicate constantly with producers and the Digital Content Center: what's happening, what you have, what you need, what's next

You'll be coached, you'll be pushed, and you'll be given room to run if you earn it.

Qualifications/Requirements:

Who Thrives In This Role:

• 3+ years working in a TV newsroom as an MMJ/reporter — and you can prove you're different
• A reel that opens with moments, not standups. We should feel like we were there.
• Aggressive on breaking news, calm under chaos, relentless on follow-ups
• Strong photographer instincts: framing, natural sound, sequencing that tells the story without narration
• Digital-first habits: cut a vertical moment, write an urgent web alert and update it
• Source-builder: cops, courts, community, scanners, social — you have a system
• Team player who collaborates fast with photographers, producers, anchors, and digital producers

What We're Not Looking For:

• Someone who wants to anchor. This is not an anchor track.
• Someone who wants to wait for a 6 p.m. package to show their work.
• Someone who needs a meeting to decide to go after news.

How To Apply – Show Us You're Different

Don't send a generic cover letter. Send us:

1. Resume + link to reel (lead with your 3 best moments, not your 3 best packages)
2. In 150 words or less: Tell us about a time every station had the same story, and yours was different. What was the moment, how did you get it, and how fast did the audience see it?

job.title: MULTIMEDIA JOURNALIST - KSFY/KDLT (SIOUX FALLS)
job.description:
About Gray Media:

Gray Media, or Gray, is a multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. The company is the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 113 television markets that collectively reach approximately 36 percent of US television households. The portfolio includes 77 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first and/or second-highest-rated television station, as well as the largest Telemundo Affiliate group with 45 markets totaling nearly 1.5 million Hispanic TV Households. The company also owns Gray Digital Media, a full-service digital agency offering national and local clients digital marketing strategies with the most advanced digital products and services. Gray's additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KSFY/KDLT:

Sioux Falls is one of the fastest-growing cities in the Upper Midwest and is home to more than 200,000 people. Healthcare and finance make up much of the workforce in Sioux Falls. There is never a shortage of things to do here. Summers are packed with outdoor festivals and concert events. Many also enjoy the city’s nearly 30 miles of bike trails; be sure to stop by the beautiful waterfalls of the Big Sioux River! And winter doesn't mean people hibernate; there are plenty of outdoor and indoor activities all winter long. In 2014, the city built a 12,000-seat arena that has hosted everything from PBR events, hockey, and indoor football, to concerts with names like Paul McCartney, Carrie Underwood, and Ed Sheeran. The city is also home to a new indoor aquatic center, an indoor ice skating facility, a basketball arena, and an indoor tennis complex. There is no shortage of places to eat, either. Not only is Sioux Falls home to many familiar restaurant chains, but it's also known for many great locally-owned restaurants. And if you want to get away for the weekend, you can drive to Omaha in three hours, Minneapolis in four, and the Black Hills in five.

KSFY/KDLT is an award-winning television operation serving viewers in the eastern half of South Dakota as well as portions of southwest Minnesota and northwest Iowa. The stations operate from a new studio in downtown Sioux Falls as one rebranded organization called Dakota News Now. The facilities put Dakota News Now on the cutting edge of television and news gathering technology, making it one of the most state-of-the-art television stations in the market and the region. The Dakota News Now team produces 38 hours of news each week. Some of our employees have been here for more than 25 years. For others, this is their first job out of college. It's a great mix that gives us different perspectives while covering the news. People here enjoy the work they do, and everyone steps up to the plate during major news events like breaking news and severe weather.

Learn more about Dakota News Now & Sioux Falls here: https://www.dakotanewsnow.com/page/ksfykdlt-careers/

• Must possess good organizational and time management skills
• Must have the ability to shoot and edit your own stories and the ability to go live
• Excellent live reporting skills required, ability to ad-lib during breaking news
• Must be willing to work day shifts and evening shifts, longer hours, and different days as needed
• Travel will also be required

Qualifications/Requirements:

• Bachelor's or master's degree in journalism or related field
• Experience in on-air television reporting is preferred, but we are willing to train the right candidate
• Basic experience with newsroom computer systems is preferred (ENPS)
• Understanding of and adherence to AP Style (for digital platforms) and broadcast writing (for television).

Job Summary/Description:

Are you the kind of person who is naturally curious about the world around you? KTTC in Rochester, MN, is looking for a high-energy Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) who is ready to start their career by making a real impact. We’re not just looking for an employee; we’re looking for a storyteller who is eager to share facts, seek the truth, and own the news cycle across every screen—from the TV in the living room to the phone in the palm of a viewer's hand.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:  

What You'll Do:

• Own the news cycle: Gather, shoot, and edit high-impact content for multiple platforms, ensuring our audience stays informed.
• Pitch with purpose: Come ready to the editorial meeting with researched ideas pitched through Microsoft Teams. You’ll have already made the calls and prearranged interviews to hit the ground running.
• Master the multi-platform: Write and adapt stories for different screens—from the morning news to quick social updates and deep-dive web articles.
• Report live from the scene: Be the first on the ground when news breaks, delivering authoritative and calm live reports that keep our viewers connected.
• Verify and validate: Gather and verify factual information through interviews, observation, and deep research—because accuracy is our foundation.
• Manage your time: Take charge of your daily workflow—from getting out the door for fresh video to editing your final masterpiece before the deadline hits.
• Stay agile: Update stories as they evolve and be ready to fill in on different shifts when the news demands it.

Why You'll Love It Here:

• A launchpad for your career: Join a young, energetic newsroom led by anchors with decades of experience who are eager to mentor the next generation of journalists.
• Growth every day: We believe feedback should happen in real time, not just during a yearly review. You’ll grow faster here than anywhere else.
• Innovation focus: KTTC is evolving on purpose—we’re serious about the future of media and want you to help shape it.
• Community impact: Tell stories that actually matter to the people of Rochester and the surrounding area.
• Supportive culture: We value scrappiness and digital innovation, but we also value our people. You’ll have the tools and the team to do your best work.

Qualifications/Requirements:

What You Bring:

• The mindset: Above all else, a relentless desire to learn, seek the truth, and share stories that matter.
• Strong writing chops: You craft scripts and articles that are tight, clear, and compelling (AP style is your best friend).
• Technical potential: While we can teach you to shoot and edit video, a familiarity with camera equipment and systems like ENPS or Edius is a great head start.
• Self-motivated hustle: The ability to work independently in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment without breaking a sweat.
• Versatility: You can manage multiple projects at once and pivot quickly when breaking news hits.
• A valid driver’s license: You’re ready to hit the road and go where the story takes you.
• Human qualities: Empathy for the stories you tell, urgency in how you tell them, and the flexibility to roll with the punches of a dayside shift.

Ready to start your journey and own the news cycle in Rochester? Let’s create something amazing together.

- Must possess a strong understanding of daily newscast content and work in conjunction with producers to develop a dynamic product.

Ready to join a newsroom that aggressively uncovers the truth? For over six decades, WLOX has been South Mississippi's undisputed news leader, proudly holding down both the #1 and #2 spots as the region's ABC and CBS affiliate. We're building the future of local news with a sharp focus on impactful investigative journalism and leading the charge in digital storytelling across every platform. Here, you'll be part of an award-winning team committed to serving our community while shaping the evolving landscape of media.

Are you wired to uncover stories that truly matter? Do you thrive at the intersection of local news and digital speed? WLOX is on the hunt for a Multimedia Journalist who can bring their A-game to every platform, from broadcast to the web, and into the heart of our community. If you're a self-starter with a nose for news and a passion for connecting with audiences wherever they are, then this is your opportunity to make a significant impact!

Duties/Responsibilities will include (but not be limited to):

- Craft compelling stories: Write, shoot, and edit engaging news stories for TV, web, and all our digital platforms, ensuring our community is always informed and connected.

- Unearth vital narratives: Research, pitch, and develop impactful news stories that resonate deeply with our local audience and shed light on important issues.
- Own the moment: Navigate fast-paced, high-pressure environments and make sound, split-second decisions during live broadcasts, maintaining composure and confidence under pressure.
- Step up to the anchor desk: Seize opportunities to fill in as an anchor, showcasing your versatility and leadership in front of the camera (based on your interest and ability, of course!).

- A degree in Communications/Journalism or an equivalent passion-driven, real-world experience (we value grit and smarts!).
- An insatiable curiosity for current events and what truly matters to our local community.

- Team player & solo star: You thrive in collaborative environments but are equally effective working independently, especially when deadlines are tight.
- Physical readiness: Able to confidently lift and carry essential equipment, including your tripod, camera, and lights—because great stories don't always happen in a studio!
- A clean driving record and a valid driver's license (essential for covering stories across our community).
- Unshakeable news judgment: You know a story when you see it, how to tell it responsibly, and why it matters to our viewers.
- Urgency with empathy: You're driven to get the story first, but always with respect, understanding, and a commitment to accuracy.

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first- and/or second-highest-rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 such markets measured by Nielsen in 2025. We also own the largest Telemundo Affiliate group, with 47 markets, and Gray Digital Media, a full-service digital agency offering national and local clients digital marketing strategies and the most advanced digital products and services. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KTUU

Alaska's News Source has a reputation of excellence as the state's most-watched news source, producing 32 hours of broadcast news, weather, and sports content each week on KTUU-TV/Channel 2 and KYES/Channel 5 in Anchorage as well as KATH and KYEX in Southeast Alaska and KTVF and KXDF in Fairbanks. Strong reach and brand loyalty are augmented by added broadcast distribution to more than 200 rural communities throughout the state via ARCS-TV, Alaska's rural communications service. A leader in digital content, AlaskasNewSource.com offers breaking news and statewide community coverage. Our News and Weather Apps, podcasts, and streamed content offered through Connected TV platforms reach audiences far beyond broadcast. Our mission is "To Tell Alaska's Story," and we strive to consistently distinguish ourselves as Alaska's preferred source for news, information, and community service.

Job Summary/Description:

Alaska's News Source is looking for a versatile, news-driven journalist who is equally at home in the field, stacking/writing/creating newscasts and producing breaking news in the control room. As an MMJ/ Producer, you'll spend two days a week leading our newscasts as a producer and three days each week reporting in the field — gathering, shooting, and reporting/delivering stories that matter to and impact Alaskans. This is not a role for someone who wants to do one thing. It's a role for someone who loves all of it! The MMJ/Producer schedule is 2:30 p.m.-10:30 p.m. Wed-Sun.

Duties/Responsibilities will include (but not be limited to):

Producing (Two Days A Week):
- Produce 2 newscasts per day with strong story selection, compelling teases, and clean show flow
- Make real-time editorial decisions during breaking news situations with minimal supervision
- Collaborate with anchors, meteorologists, and directors to deliver a polished, audience-first broadcast
- Write and edit copy, teases, and anchor reads under deadline pressure
- Write and post copy daily on all digital platforms as new information is learned and throughout your assigned shift. This includes copy for web, social media, our news app, our digital desk/CTV, and within our television newscasts on broadcast.

MMJ/Reporting (Three Days a Week):
- Research, pitch, shoot, write, edit, and present original news packages and live reports
- Gather content with a multi-platform mindset — thinking about what works on social and digital, not just on air
- File social content including vertical videos from the field in real time when news warrants it
- Develop and maintain sources across the state of Alaska
- Contribute story ideas that serve our broadcast and digital audiences

Qualifications/Requirements:

- Experience in both broadcast producing and MMJ reporting
- Strong editorial judgment, especially in breaking news situations
- Ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines simultaneously
- A digital-aware mindset: you think about your audience on every platform, not just the one watching at 6:00 pm
- Excellent writing skills, tight, active, conversational broadcast copy
- Self-motivated and dependable; weekends require someone who leads without being managed
- Must have a desire to win, a positive attitude, and the ability to reflect on your work and apply feedback
- Ability to work a combination of dayside and nightside shifts, as well as overtime when warranted for breaking news or special coverage
- Valid driver's license and ability to drive a company vehicle
- A journalism-related degree (or similar) is preferred
- Must be able to carry 35+ pounds of gear and be experienced in shooting and editing unique content. We have photographers and editors to partner with on select assignments.

job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About WLIO:

Located in Lima, Ohio, WLIO is proud to bring all four major networks—NBC, CBS, ABC, and FOX—under one roof. As a station serving the Midwest, we enjoy the beauty and variety of all four seasons while staying closely connected to the communities we serve.

WLIO offers applicants the opportunity to be part of a dynamic, collaborative team in a welcoming market where journalists and media professionals can make a meaningful impact.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you a digital dynamo who knows how to turn clicks into customers? Do you thrive on the thrill of the hunt—and the satisfaction of seeing your clients' businesses grow? We’re looking for a Multi-Media Sales Manager who lives and breathes digital strategy but understands the power of a multi-platform approach. At WLIO, we bring all four major networks (NBC, CBS, ABC, and FOX) under one roof, giving you an unmatched toolkit to help local businesses dominate the Lima market. If you’re ready to lead a team that’s as energetic as it is innovative, we want to talk to you.

As our Multi-Media Sales Manager specializing in Digital, you are the catalyst for growth in the Lima market. You aren't just managing a team; you are a digital evangelist, a strategic coach, and a consultative partner to our advertisers. You will lead the charge in growing our digital footprint by developing cutting-edge sales strategies across OTT, SEO, social, and web to ensure all budgets and goals are crushed. From overseeing pricing and inventory to mentoring our Multimedia Executives, you’ll own the digital lifecycle and foster a high-energy, winning culture that puts our clients first.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Drive digital revenue: Lead the charge in growing our digital footprint by developing and executing cutting-edge sales strategies across OTT, SEO, social, and web to ensure all budgets and goals are met or exceeded.
  • Coach for greatness: Provide ongoing digital training and subject-matter expertise to the sales team, helping them uncover new opportunities and close complex multi-platform deals.
  • Craft winning solutions: Partner with local businesses to understand their unique challenges and build custom, integrated marketing campaigns—from programmatic to streaming—that deliver real ROI.
  • Own the market: Oversee digital pricing, inventory management, and revenue forecasting in tandem with the Director of Sales to ensure WLIO remains the go-to destination for innovative advertising.
  • Master the execution: Manage the lifecycle of digital campaigns from order entry to completion, ensuring every tag, tracking detail, and creative asset is perfectly aligned for success.
  • Analyze and optimize: Translate campaign data into actionable insights and reporting, providing clients with the "real talk" and performance recommendations they need to stay ahead of the curve.
  • Promote a winning culture: Foster a positive, high-energy environment where accountability and collaboration are the standard, not the exception.

Qualifications/Requirements:

  • Digital Expertise: Minimum of two years of digital sales experience with a deep understanding of OTT, SEM, social, and programmatic advertising.
  • Proven Leadership: Advanced leadership skills with a track record of achieving budgets and the ability to manage multiple tasks, deadlines, and—most importantly—people.
  • Strategic Communication: Strong presentation experience and excellent written/verbal skills; you can take complex data and turn it into a compelling narrative for a business owner.
  • Problem-Solving Prowess: The unique ability to translate client problems into digital opportunities, maintaining ownership of every challenge until it’s resolved.
  • Technical Proficiency: Expert proficiency in PowerPoint, Excel, social media, and CRM/order-entry systems (experience with Engage is a major plus).
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in marketing, advertising, business, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
  • The "Gray" Factor: A relentless sense of urgency, a collaborative spirit, and a passion for helping local businesses thrive in a digital-first world.

Why You'll Love It Here:

  • Unmatched reach: With four major networks at your fingertips, you have the most powerful advertising platform in the region to play with.
  • A collaborative culture: We’re a dynamic, welcoming team where your ideas aren't just heard—they're celebrated.
  • Real community impact: You’ll be helping local businesses in Lima thrive, making a tangible difference in the place we call home.
  • Innovation at scale: Gray Media is evolving on purpose, and you’ll be at the forefront of the future of media with access to the best tools in the industry.

Ready to lead the digital revolution in Lima? Let’s create something amazing together.

Sales Leadership and Development:
* Lead, coach, and support Media Executives and other sales team members in achieving individual and team revenue goals.

job.title: NATIONAL & REGIONAL SALES ASSISTANT - KBTX
job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first- and/or second-highest-rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 markets measured by Nielsen in 2025. We also own the largest Telemundo Affiliate group with 46 markets and Gray Digital Media, a full-service digital agency offering national and local clients digital marketing strategies with the most advanced digital products and services. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KBTX:

KBTX Media operates the CBS and CW affiliates in Bryan-College Station, Texas, serving an 18-county area known as the Brazos Valley. For nearly 70 years, we’ve been the dominant choice for local news and entertainment. Our team produces nearly 40 hours of broadcast content each week, along with a constant presence online at KBTX.com.

KBTX is routinely recognized among the best in the state by organizations including the Associated Press, RTDNA, and the Lone Star EMMY Chapter of the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences. The station has won four consecutive Texas Association of Broadcasters’ Bonner McLane Public Service awards, and in 2023 won a National Edward R. Murrow Award for Digital content. KBTX is also a recent Texas AP Broadcasters/Freedom of Information Foundation of Texas Station of the Year and Texas Associated Press Broadcasters Station of the Year.

The station has launched the careers of many well-known journalists, meteorologists, and network executives, and takes pride in helping talent grow quickly into the nation’s largest television markets. The work family of KBTX is made up of a group of dedicated, professional, and passionate individuals who are the backbone of our daily mission.

Bryan-College Station, Texas, is a community of more than 250,000 people and the largest single metro in the Waco-Temple-Bryan DMA. The twin cities have a unique small-town feeling, but offer big city amenities, including a vibrant arts community, a city-wide, all-terrain trail system, and world-class dining and nightlife. Bryan and College Station are routinely recognized as a leader in quality of life and as one of the fastest-growing communities in the country.
College Station is home to Texas A&M University, the nation’s largest university. Aggie home football games attract more than 100,000 in the stands, with tens of thousands more camped outside celebrating at tailgates during football weekends.

Learn more about KBTX at www.kbtx.com.

Job Summary/Description:  

KBTX Media is seeking an organized, meticulously detail-oriented individual to provide administrative support for our national and regional sales accounts. Responsibilities will include assisting the National Sales Manager and local Media Executives with account management, including order entry, order management, post-buy analysis, client communication, and follow-up, along with all other duties associated with account management. Job duties will also include serving as backup for all account traffic instructions.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Assist with all station account management with special focus on national/regional accounts
• Provide support to sales management and sales team for order entry in WideOrbit Traffic system
• Daily maintenance of all national/regional contract orders, revisions, additions, etc.
• Daily makegood and preemption reconciliation, including sending makegood offers
• Local and network program change notifications
• Communication with agencies, including providing make-good offers, pre- or post-spot placement reports, confirmation of contracts, late-run notifications, research credit requests, or contract discrepancies
• Assist with daily log reconciliation
• Assist with daily traffic and copy maintenance as needed
• Assist with all political advertising contracts and FCC political file upkeep
• Assist with advance log maintenance to allow for maximum use of inventory or provide advance program change notifications/makegood offers

Qualifications/Requirements:

• Applicant must be detail-oriented and be proficient in accurate data entry
• Strong organizational skills with ability to multitask while meeting daily deadlines
• Work well in a fast-paced environment, prioritizing and managing time wisely
• Be proficient in Microsoft Office products, including Excel and PowerPoint
• Prior experience and working knowledge of Wide Orbit Traffic systems is a plus
• Possess a valid driver’s license, dependable mode of transportation with vehicle insurance, and a clean driving record
• Sales experience is not required; however, the motivation to become a member of one of the top-selling sales teams in the region is important.

EDUCATION OR FORMAL TRAINING:
Associate’s Degree or Four-Year Degree preferred, but not required

KCTV5 is the CBS affiliate serving the Kansas City metropolitan area.

Job Summary/Description:

KCTV 5 is looking for a Weekend Evening Anchor/MMJ who is as comfortable going live on a streaming desk as they are anchoring a traditional newscast. This role is built for a journalist who thinks in multiple platforms, someone who can deliver a broadcast package, produce a 60-second vertical explainer, and anchor a streaming update all in the same shift. If you believe local news should meet audiences where they are on broadcast, on streaming, and on social, this role is for you.

Duties/Responsibilities will include (but not be limited to):

• Anchor weekend evening newscasts with a focus on local impact, utility, and community connection, delivering content that earns trust with audiences across all age groups.
• Produce and present streaming desk updates between and outside of traditional newscasts, providing live, real-time coverage of breaking news, severe weather, and developing stories for audiences watching on connected TV platforms (Roku, Amazon Fire TV, Smart TV apps, etc.).
• Report and shoot as a Multi-Media Journalist (MMJ), producing broadcast-quality packages while simultaneously capturing vertical video assets for social and streaming platforms.
• Build multi-platform story plans at the start of each shift, identifying the broadcast output, the streaming update, and the platform-native social content for each assigned story.
• Produce platform-native vertical video (50-60 seconds) for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts that are more than just a cut-down from broadcast.
• Anchor or contribute to streaming-only content, including live breaking news coverage, "what we know so far" explainers, and VOD segments designed for on-demand viewing outside traditional newscast windows.
• Be our content and editorial leader on the weekends by engaging in story selection and decision-making.
• Engage with audiences in comments and DMs on your stories, answering questions and mining community feedback for follow-up story ideas.
• Participate in editorial meetings with a multi-platform mindset, contributing platform assignments, digital deadlines, and story format recommendations alongside traditional broadcast planning.

Qualifications/Requirements:

• Minimum 2 years of on-air experience in broadcast news as a reporter, anchor, or MMJ.
• Demonstrated experience producing content natively for streaming and/or social video platforms, including vertical video for TikTok, Instagram Reels, or YouTube Shorts.
• Strong live anchoring/reporting skills with the ability to deliver calm, credible, and conversational coverage during breaking news and/or severe weather.
• Mobile journalism proficiency, ability to shoot, edit, and publish content independently in the field, including vertical video capture with reuse across platforms in mind.
• Understanding of audience behavior across platforms, including when and why viewers turn to streaming vs. broadcast vs. social, and how to tailor content accordingly.
• Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, or related field preferred, or equivalent professional experience.
• Ability to work a weekend evening schedule, including holidays, and to pivot quickly when breaking news or severe weather demands extended coverage across all platforms.

About KWCH:

KWCH (12 News) is a CBS television affiliate serving Wichita as well as central and western Kansas. KWCH is the market leader, providing viewers with local news, weather, and breaking news coverage. The news team is a 2026 National Murrow Award winner. Wichita is ranked as one of the best cities for young professionals - where you can enjoy a high quality of life, a low cost of living, and a vibrant community.

Job Summary/Description:

Do you have the authority to lead a newsroom and the storytelling chops to own the weekend? We’re looking for more than just an anchor; we need a Weekend Newsroom Leader who can drive coverage, mentor a team, and connect with our Wichita audience across every platform. If you’re a high-energy journalist who thrives on the desk and in the field—and you’re ready to step into a management-level mindset—KWCH (12 News) wants you to lead the way.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

* Lead the weekend charge: Act as the primary editorial voice on Saturdays and Sundays, guiding the team and making the big calls when news breaks.
Anchor with authority: Deliver high-energy, conversational newscasts that keep Wichita informed and engaged, whether they’re watching on TV or streaming on the go.
* Own the story: Report and produce compelling content as an MMJ, finding the "why" behind the headlines and bringing local stories to life.
Drive digital first: Don't just wait for the 6 PM news; engage our audience all day on social media, our app, and streaming platforms.
* Collaborate and mentor: Work closely with producers and the assignment desk to sharpen our coverage and help younger journalists level up.
* Represent the brand: Be a trusted face of 12 News in the community, building relationships and staying connected to the people we serve.

Qualifications/Requirements:

* Proven leadership: You have at least 2 years of experience and a "manager-in-the-making" mindset—you know how to take charge and keep a team focused.
* Dynamic presence: You have a "sparkling" on-camera energy that feels authentic and authoritative.
* MMJ mastery: You’re a pro at shooting, editing, and writing your own stories under tight deadlines.
* Sharp news judgment: You understand journalism ethics and know exactly what makes a story relevant to our viewers.
* Digital fluency: You live on social media and understand how to pivot content for different platforms (you know digital isn't an afterthought).

job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. About WIS:

WIS is the #1 local media organization in the capital city market of Columbia, South Carolina. As the top-rated broadcast television station serving South Carolina's Midlands since 1953, WIS offers the opportunity to join an award-winning culture built upon decades of market leadership.

WIS is currently recognized as the South Carolina Broadcasters Association's Station of the Year and has won the award a record 17 times. WIS has earned the Edward R. Murrow Award for Journalism Excellence, the National Association of Broadcasters' Service to America Award, the George Foster Peabody Award, and has more than 70 Emmy nominations in the last 5 years. Among the many notable former journalists who helped set our standard, NBC Today Show co-host Craig Melvin began his career with WIS as an intern, photographer, reporter, then anchor.

WIS produces more than 60 hours of live, local broadcast programming per week, as well as original content for multiple digital platforms. The station offers a unique variety of multiplatform advertising solutions, sponsored content, and professional creative services for businesses of any size.

Columbia, South Carolina, is a vibrant and growing capital city with a diverse population. It is home to the U.S. Army's largest installation for Basic Combat Training, Fort Jackson, along with the University of South Carolina and multiple other colleges and universities. WIS is located downtown, just two blocks from the South Carolina State House.

Our community combines affordable quality of living with a variety of entertainment and activities to accommodate your lifestyle, whether it's our 50,000-acre Lake Murray, our Columbia Fireflies minor league baseball team, the Riverbanks Zoo & Gardens, nearby Congaree National Park, or so much more.

Job Summary/Description:                       

Are you a visionary leader who thrives on the adrenaline of a fast-paced newsroom? Do you believe that being "Your First Alert" isn't just a slogan, but a commitment to keeping a community informed, prepared, and connected across every screen they own? WIS-TV, the #1 local media organization in Columbia, South Carolina, since 1953, is looking for a News Director to lead our award-winning team into the future. We’re looking for a multiplatform strategist and a culture-builder who will inspire a talented staff to reach new heights of journalistic excellence.

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

What You'll Do:
• Lead the legacy: Take the helm of the largest news staff in the market, driving the strategic vision for a station that has been a community staple for over 70 years.
• Own the "Your First Alert" brand: Oversee all systems and workflows to ensure we are the most trusted source for breaking news and weather, delivering urgency and accuracy every single time.
• Drive multiplatform growth: Use data and research to aggressively grow our audience on emerging platforms, ensuring our content is as dynamic on a smartphone as it is on a TV.
• Coach your team to greatness: Recruit, hire, and mentor the next generation of journalists, providing consistent, constructive feedback that turns "good" into "award-winning."
• Foster a winning culture: Build a workplace where every team member feels visible, valued, and respected, creating an environment of high expectations and mutual support.
• Collaborate across the building: Partner with other station leaders to set and smash collective goals, participating in annual strategic planning to keep WIS at the top.
• Manage with precision: Handle the business side of news, from disciplined budget management and ROI delivery to contract negotiations and HR support, with total confidence.

What You Bring:
• A "people first" approach: You believe that a thriving culture is the foundation of a successful newsroom, and you have the attention to detail necessary to manage the systems that allow for it.
• A multiplatform mindset: You produce content for the "news finds me" crowd in today's algorithm-driven environment, and you adapt accordingly as the wind shifts direction.
• Proven leadership experience: You’ve successfully led a newsroom (or a significant department) and have the track record to prove it.
• Impeccable journalistic integrity: You have a deep understanding of media law and ethics, ensuring our reporting is always fair, accurate, and impactful.
• Exceptional communication skills: You can pivot from a high-level strategy meeting to a one-on-one talent coaching session without missing a beat.
• A passion for community: You understand the unique pulse of South Carolina's Midlands and are ready to represent WIS at public events and community initiatives.
• Sense of urgency: You thrive under deadline pressure and know how to lead a team through the chaos of a major breaking news event.

Why You'll Love It Here:
• The #1 spot: You’ll be leading the market leader, with the resources and reputation of a legacy station behind you.
• Innovation at scale: Gray Media is at the forefront of the industry’s evolution. You’ll have the tools and the freedom to experiment and innovate.
• Real community impact: In Columbia, WIS is an institution. You'll feel it the moment you wear our logo anywhere in town, and you'll see the direct results of your team's work every day.
• A deep bench of talent: You’ll work with some of the best journalists in the business who are as passionate about the mission as you are.
• Growth opportunities: We invest in our people with training, tools, mentorship, and more. We want to see you succeed.

Qualifications/Requirements:

• Bachelor's degree in Broadcast Journalism, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and work-related experience.
• Excellent communication skills, both oral and written.
• Minimum of five years' experience in news programming production, with at least two years' experience in a leadership role.
• Experience guiding, directing, and motivating a team, including setting performance standards and monitoring progress.
• Experience establishing long-range objectives and specifying the strategies and actions to achieve them.
• Ability to identify the developmental needs of others and to coach, mentor, and inspire others to improve their knowledge of skills.
• Experience preparing and maintaining departmental budgets.
• Proficiency with newsroom and station technology.
• Ability to meet deadlines, prioritize assignments, and handle multiple tasks simultaneously.
• Ability to effectively listen to fully understand employee needs and communicate with a team to shape a solution.
• Coachable, committed, and aware, with the ability to accept candid feedback in the spirit that there's always room for improvement.

job.description:
About Gray Media:

We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. About WECT:

WECT News has been Where News Comes First in Southeastern North Carolina for over 70 years. We're the NBC affiliate in the rapidly growing Wilmington market, serving New Hanover, Brunswick, Columbus, Pender, and Bladen counties that make up the beautiful coastal Cape Fear Region. WECT is the most accessible local news outlet in our market, with WECT.com, News & Weather apps, and streaming platforms. WECT is the dominant #1 station in the market.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you a visual storyteller who lives for the "wow" factor?

Do you thrive on the adrenaline of a breaking story and the satisfaction of a deep-dive community piece? We’re looking for a Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) who doesn't just report the news but owns it—across every screen.

Whether you’re crafting a lead for one of our on-air newscasts, going live on our streaming newscasts in the WECT Digital Studio, or engaging with our audience on social, you’ll be the heartbeat of the Cape Fear region.

If you’re a scrappy, digital-first journalist who wants to make a real impact in southeastern North Carolina, let’s talk.

Duties/Responsibilities will include (but not be limited to):

What You'll Do:
* Own the story: Manage and develop compelling content from initial concept to final publication across digital, social, and broadcast platforms.
* Drive digital engagement: Create platform-specific content that meets our audience where they are—on their phones, their TVs, and everywhere in between.
* Master the craft: Write, edit, and produce high-quality stories with speed, accuracy, and a killer creative eye.
* Respond with urgency: Jump into breaking news situations with authority and calm, keeping our community informed in real-time.
* Connect with the community: Build deep roots in the Cape Fear region, developing sources and uncovering the stories that truly matter to our neighbors.
*Step into the spotlight: Take advantage of potential anchoring opportunities to lead our coverage and connect directly with viewers.

What You Bring:
* A digital-first mindset: You understand that "news" happens 24/7, and you’re ready to feed the beast on social and streaming first.
* Killer storytelling skills: You know how to find the "human" element in every story and make it resonate with an audience.
* Technical chops: You’re a pro with a camera and an editing suite (and you’re not afraid to learn new tools as they emerge).
* Sharp news judgment: You know what’s important, what’s interesting, and how to tell the difference under pressure.
* A positive, "can-do" attitude: You’re a team player who lifts others up and thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.
* Urgency and empathy: You care about the stories you tell and the people they affect, and you move fast to get them right.
* Flexibility: News doesn't follow a 9-to-5 schedule, and neither do you—you’re ready to go where the story takes you.

Qualifications/Requirements:

* Bachelor’s degree in journalism or related field preferred
* Strong writing skills (broadcast and print style)
* Experience with CMS/digital publishing platforms
* Experience with broadcast newsroom software such as ENPS
* Experience with video editing software (preferably Edius)
* Must be able to lift 25-30 lbs and pass a motor vehicle background check

There has always been a family atmosphere at WTVG. We care about each other, and know that we are stronger as one team than as many individuals. We take our jobs seriously, and know that we can be successful and have fun at the same time.

About KBTX:

KBTX Media operates the CBS and CW affiliates in Bryan-College Station, Texas, serving an 18-county area known as the Brazos Valley. For nearly 70 years, we’ve been the dominant choice for local news and entertainment. Our team produces nearly 40 hours of broadcast content each week, along with a constant presence online at KBTX.com.
KBTX is routinely recognized among the best in the state by organizations including the Associated Press, RTDNA, and the Lone Star EMMY Chapter of the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences. The station has won four consecutive Texas Association of Broadcasters’ Bonner McLane Public Service awards, and in 2023 won a National Edward R. Murrow Award for Digital content. KBTX is also a recent Texas AP Broadcasters/Freedom of Information Foundation of Texas Station of the Year and Texas Associated Press Broadcasters Station of the Year.

The station has launched the careers of many well-known journalists, meteorologists and network executives, and takes pride in helping talent grow quickly into the nation’s largest television markets. The work family of KBTX is made up of a group of dedicated, professional, and passionate individuals who are the backbone of our daily mission.
Bryan-College Station, Texas, is a community of more than 250,000 people and the largest single metro in the Waco-Temple-Bryan DMA. The twin cities have a unique small-town feeling, but offer big city amenities, including a vibrant arts community, a city-wide, all-terrain trail system, and world-class dining and nightlife. Bryan and College Station are routinely recognized as a leader in quality of life and as one of the fastest-growing communities in the country.
College Station is home to Texas A&M University, the nation’s largest university. Aggie home football games attract more than 100,000 in the stands, with tens of thousands more camped outside celebrating at tailgates during football weekends.

Learn more about KBTX at www.kbtx.com.

Job Summary/Description:

KBTX Media is looking for a part-time photojournalist to join the Brazos Valley’s most-watched television station. The photojournalist will take an active role in the production of several station franchises and work alongside both the news and creative services departments.

A successful candidate will write, shoot, edit, and present compelling content both on-air and online. You’ll also play a key role in working with other KBTX journalists to develop both long- and short-term stories with a focus on uncovering the human side of each story. 

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to): 

- Identifying the day’s most important stories and sourcing materials relevant to your audience
- Researching, gathering, writing, and editing daily content for television and digital platforms
- Generating daily stories and content, along with regular enterprise reporting
- Working alongside other KBTX team members to produce impactful, high-energy live content
- Meeting daily and weekly deadlines in a fast-paced environment, including a strong digital focus

Qualifications/Requirements:

- You must independently enterprise content, enjoy and remain active on social media, and use your storytelling skills to offer meaningful context to issues affecting the  Brazos Valley. Great writing, a strong eye for content, and a willingness to learn will earn you this position.
- Candidates should also exhibit a good work ethic, strong people skills, the ability to be a team player, and always maintain a professional attitude. This position requires availability to work weekends and may require holiday work.
- Experience in a TV newsroom, as well as a college degree in broadcast journalism or a related field, is expected. Experience in reviewing legal/court documents, submitting open records requests, and an established and responsible presence on digital platforms are a big plus.

KOLN is a strong number one in the Lincoln, Nebraska market and part of the Gray Nebraska network in which three stations, KOLN, KSNB & KNOP, work closely together to serve Nebraska viewers. The network of stations has a strong focus on innovation, while maintaining a positive work environment.

Why You’ll Love This Role:
Create original content that helps Nebraska audiences connect with local news.
Collaborate with journalists across KOLN, KSNB and KNOP.
Build experience across social video, YouTube, websites, and live newscasts.

Job Summary/Description:

Schedule: 1:30 p.m. to 10:30 p.m., Monday- Friday
Can you turn the news of the day into video people want to watch and share? Join the digital team serving KOLN, KSNB and KNOP, and help bring local, impactful and trustworthy Nebraska news to audiences across social platforms. You’ll shoot and edit your own vertical videos, help colleagues bring their stories to life on social, and support our YouTube and website coverage. Based in the KOLN newsroom in Lincoln, you’ll work with a digital team serving all three stations under the direction of our Digital Director.

* Create original video: Write, shoot, edit, and publish vertical news videos daily, adjusting priorities for breaking news.

* Support YouTube: Help create compelling thumbnails and headlines and adapt news coverage into longer-form YouTube videos.

* News judgment: You know how to identify important stories and make calm decisions under deadline pressure.

*A collaborative approach: You communicate well, enjoy helping others, and thrive in a fast-paced team environment.
Journalistic principles: You understand and follow the standards and practices that support trustworthy reporting.

job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first- and/or second-highest-rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 of such markets that were measured by Nielsen in 2025. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KTVK/KPHO:

Home to 3TV, CBS 5, and Arizona’s Family Sports, Arizona’s Family produces 100+ hours of local news and programming every week. 3TV is #1 in Arizona and one of the strongest independent stations in the country. Our CBS station is highly competitive in news and has top-rated sports and prime content. Our digital reach is also best-in-market—Azfamily.com leads the market in multi-platform unique users and is home to Arizona’s Family Originals (long-form programs, documentaries, docuseries, and podcasts, including True Crime Arizona, nearing 2M downloads). Arizona’s Family Sports features premier properties, including the Arizona Cardinals, Phoenix Suns, Phoenix Mercury, Phoenix Rising, and AIA state championships.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you obsessed with the creator economy? Do you understand why some videos explode to millions of views while others disappear into the void? Can you take a 45-minute podcast episode and turn it into five pieces of content that each hit differently on five different platforms? Then we need to talk.

Arizona's Family is looking for a Social Media Video Producer who is laser-focused on growing our content and talent through bold, creative, platform-native video content. This isn't a traditional TV job — this is a digital-first, audience-obsessed, growth-driven role for someone who thinks like a content creator, executes like a producer, and analyzes like a strategist.

You'll be the engine behind turning our long-form streaming content and podcast episodes into short-form social gold — building loyal audiences, driving subscriptions, and putting Arizona's Family at the forefront of the next era of local media.

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

• Transform long-form into short-form magic: Watch, listen to, and deeply understand our streaming shows and podcast episodes — then identify and clip the moments that will hook audiences on TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Facebook, and X.
• Produce original social video content: Concept, shoot, and edit original short-form video content — teasers, trailers, behind-the-scenes, host spotlights, audiograms, and promotional clips — that drive tune-in and subscriptions.
• Grow our streaming and podcast audiences: Develop and execute platform-specific social strategies designed to convert casual scrollers into loyal subscribers and regular listeners/viewers.
• Be a storytelling architect: Identify the most compelling hooks, soundbites, and moments from each episode and package them into irresistible, binge-worthy content that leaves audiences wanting more.
• Manage content calendars: Plan, schedule, and publish content across all platforms with consistency and strategic timing — building anticipation before episodes drop and sustaining momentum after.
• Optimize for each platform: You don't post the same video everywhere. You understand aspect ratios, caption strategies, hashtag culture, trending audio, and algorithm behavior on every major platform — and you create accordingly.
• Engage and grow communities: Foster authentic engagement around our shows and podcasts — responding to comments, collaborating with hosts on their personal channels, and identifying opportunities to tap into trending conversations.
• Track, analyze, and iterate: Monitor performance metrics, including views, watch time, follower growth, click-throughs, and conversion rates, and use data to continuously refine your content strategy.
• Collaborate with field crews and talent: Work closely with our team and coach them to create authentic, engaging content, ensuring their personal brands amplify azfamily.
• Stay ahead of trends: You're always watching what's working in the creator space, new formats, emerging platforms, and viral trends that you're quick to test and adapt.
• Self-starter energy: You don't wait to be told what to create. You bring ideas, pitch concepts, and take full ownership of your content pipeline.
• Collaborative spirit: You work well with hosts, talent, and cross-functional teams — making everyone around you look and sound better.
• Bonus: Experience with audiogram tools (Headliner, Descript), podcast distribution platforms (Spotify, Apple Podcasts, iHeart), or streaming platform management (Roku, Amazon Fire, YouTube TV).
• College degree preferred.

What You'll Be Growing:

• You'll play a direct role in expanding the reach and audience of Arizona's Family's growing portfolio, which may include:
• Original podcasts covering Arizona news, politics, sports, lifestyle, and culture
• Streaming shows distributed across platforms like Roku, Amazon Fire TV, Apple TV, and YouTube
• Long-form interview and documentary-style content
• Arizona-focused lifestyle and community programming

Why You'll Love It Here:

• Be a pioneer: This is a ground-floor opportunity to shape how Arizona's Family grows in the streaming and podcast space — your fingerprints will be on everything.
• Creative freedom: Bring your boldest ideas. We want someone who pushes boundaries, experiments fearlessly, and isn't afraid to try something new.
• See your impact in real time: Watch follower counts climb, episode downloads grow, and audiences engage with content you created.
• Work with great talent: Collaborate with experienced journalists, charismatic hosts, and a passionate digital team who are all rowing in the same direction.
• Arizona's biggest media stage: Help build the future of local media in one of the fastest-growing markets in the country.
• Room to grow: Gray Media is investing heavily in streaming and digital — and so are we. This role has serious upward trajectory.

Qualifications/Requirements:

• 2–4+ years of experience in social media video production, digital content creation, or a related field — ideally with experience growing a podcast, streaming show, YouTube channel, or creator brand.
• Expert short-form video skills: You live and breathe Reels, TikToks, and Shorts. You know how to hook an audience in the first 2 seconds and keep them watching.
• Strong video editing proficiency: Fluency in Adobe Premiere Pro, CapCut, DaVinci Resolve, or similar tools. Motion graphics experience (After Effects) is a major plus.
• Platform-native thinking: You don't just repurpose content — you reimagine it for each platform's unique culture, format, and audience behavior.
• Podcast and streaming fluency: You're a regular podcast listener and streaming viewer. You understand the medium, the audience expectations, and what makes people subscribe and come back.
• Copywriting chops: You can write scroll-stopping captions, compelling CTAs, and engaging on-screen text that enhances your video content.
• Growth mindset: You're not satisfied with vanity metrics. You care about real audience growth, retention, and conversion — and you know how to move those numbers.
• Self-starter energy: You don't wait to be told what to create. You bring ideas, pitch concepts, and take full ownership of your content pipeline.
• Collaborative spirit: You work well with hosts, talent, and cross-functional teams — making everyone around you look and sound better.
• Bonus: Experience with audiogram tools (Headliner, Descript), podcast distribution platforms (Spotify, Apple Podcasts, iHeart), or streaming platform management (Roku, Amazon Fire, YouTube TV).
• College degree preferred.

About WMTV:

WMTV is the NBC affiliate and Gray Television-owned station serving south-central Wisconsin. We are the #1 station—leading the market in news and weather coverage. We are recognized for sharing information with accuracy and immediacy on all platforms.

We work hard and take pride in getting it right. For four years in a row, WMTV was honored as the Wisconsin Broadcasters Association “News Operation of the Year”. As well as being the recipient of the Edward R. Murrow Regional "Overall Excellence" Award.

What’s better than working at the #1 station in the nation’s #1 city? Join our award-winning team and live, work, and play in a community that is consistently named one of the best places to live in America. We are just 1.5 hours from Milwaukee, 2.5 hours from Chicago, and 5 hours from Minneapolis/St. Paul.

Job Summary/Description:

WMTV has an immediate opening for a Technical Media Producer. The Technical Media Producer (“TMP”) is responsible for operating the equipment in our broadcast control center that keeps WMTV’s programming on air and online. The TMP directs live and prerecorded productions as assigned, using our Ross Overdrive production automation system paired with coding in ENPS to deliver a quality News Show. The TMP also handles all master control duties in our facility, such as recording, playback, switching, and quality-checking programming for air. This position offers an opportunity for video editing and field directing.

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

job.description:
About Gray Media:

We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About WSAW:

WSAW is Wausau's first TV station, debuting 71 years ago in 1954. Together, WSAW/WZAW produce more than 30 hours of news each week. We work hard and celebrate our wins. In 2026, the news team was recognized as the Wisconsin Broadcasters Association "News Operation of the Year" and also the small-market "Station of the Year" (for coverage airing in 2025). Also in 2026, WSAW's podcast "Wisconsin Cold Cases: Who Killed Gerald Mork?" was honored with a Regional Edward R. Murrow Award. These are just a few examples of the honors WSAW has received in recent years.

 North Central Wisconsin is also known as "Wisconsin's Basecamp." In Wausau, you will live and work where thousands of people come to vacation each year. Whether you're skiing down the slopes of Granite Peak, boating on Lake Du Bay, or enjoying Concerts on the Square or a show at The Grand Theater in downtown Wausau, there's something for everyone, and you will enjoy the community we serve. Wausau is also located 3 hours or less from Minneapolis, Milwaukee, and Green Bay, and is just a two-hour drive from Madison, the state's capital city.

WSAW's viewing area covers 11 counties, including the cities of Stevens Point, Wisconsin Rapids, Marshfield, Rhinelander, and the summer retreat hotspot of Minocqua. WSAW is dedicated to serving the community and does so through several weeks-long campaigns such as the Share Your Holidays food drive and our annual Diaper Drive.

Job Summary/Description:

WSAW has an immediate opening for a Technical Media Producer. This position is responsible for technical direction of our live newscasts and monitoring/maintaining the accurate operation of all our broadcast channels.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

- Monitoring and maintaining the accurate operation of all our broadcast channels.
- Maintaining operational logs.
- Quality control of prerecorded programming and commercial advertisements.
- Monitoring and logging of our transmitter operations and tower lights.
- Preparing technical rundowns of live productions in our AP ENPS software and Ross Overdrive system.
- Performing technical director duties for our live productions, which include adjusting cameras, preparing video sources, cueing up graphics, and adjusting audio levels in our Ross Overdrive system.

Qualifications/Requirements:

- Computer experience and willingness to learn are a must.
- Experience in television, video, and audio production is preferable but not required.
- A successful applicant will be dependable, focused, detail-oriented, and possess strong multitasking skills.
- Work with a sense of immediacy, independently and as a team. It is our culture.
- Have the desire to win, as well as the ability to reflect on your work and apply feedback.
- Excellent communication skills (written and verbal), proven news judgment, ethics, and integrity.
- Must be able to work quickly, meet deadlines, multitask, and show composure, especially during live sporting events and breaking news.
- Flexibility to work long hours/overtime, weekends, and overnights as needed for breaking news and specialized coverage.

About KWCH:

KWCH 12 was the first television station in Kansas and began broadcasting on July 1st, 1953, under the call letters KTVH Channel 12. The station was licensed to and broadcast from Hutchinson, Kansas, about 45 miles northwest of Wichita. In 1956, station facilities were moved to the current location on 37th St North in Wichita. In 1983, KTVH call letters changed to KWCH and ownership was consolidated with three other Kansas stations in the market. These satellite stations include KBSD in Dodge City, KBSH in Hays, and KBSL in Goodland. Since 1985, KWCH has held the #1 position for 6 pm and 10 pm news in the Wichita-Hutchinson Plus television market. KWCH has remained dominant since that time, and Eyewitness News is the #1 news at Noon, 5 pm, 6 pm, and 10 pm.

Job Summary/Description:

KWCH-TV is currently accepting applications for a part-time Technical Media Producer to join the #1-rated news team in Kansas. This position is responsible for operating broadcast production equipment to produce newscasts and for Master Control Operations.

• Must be able to work with other departments and work well in a team environment
• Ability to work independently with little supervision
• Ability to remain positive and foster a positive work environment
• Must have an energetic attitude and be able to represent all TV stations in public in a positive, professional manner

• Operates studio camera and Chyron as directed by Producer and/or Director during newscasts or other special programming
• Responsible for operating the teleprompter, controlling the pace
• Use non-linear editing when necessary
• Responsible for the input and recall of all news graphics for daily newscasts and the construction and input of graphic elements for all production in studio and for mobile services
• Communicates instructions to talent and guests during live and live-on-tape productions
• Produces daily/weekly promos
• Perform other job-related duties as assigned
• Will be required to operate field cameras and lighting equipment as required while assisting with remote production events
• Operate robotic cameras
• Helps to assure a high-quality broadcast by monitoring on-air and cable broadcast signals, following the program log to air programs, breaks, and promotions.
• Monitor and control transmitter output and resolve any on-air problems
• Provide support for future broadcasts by recording programs from satellite feeds and dubbing tapes from various sources.
• Utilizes multiple on-air playlists to ensure playback of all programs, commercials, and promotions according to standard departmental procedures.
• Helps to assure compliance with applicable regulations and communication with other departments by maintaining transmitter and discrepancy logs, equipment incident reports, daily reports of records, and the Master Control Log.
• Communicates with sites and studios regarding accurate start and end times for live event segments and the airing of promotions. Responsible for making necessary adjustments to appropriate lists and logs.

job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first- and/or second-highest-rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 such markets measured by Nielsen in 2025. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, as well as studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios. 

About KFYR: 

A job at our station is a learning experience unlike any you’ll find in a classroom. Daily hands-on involvement of senior staff guarantees a good product that not only serves our viewers but will take our team members to the next level. With over 36 hours of news on our channels each week, KFYR-TV is truly Western North Dakota’s news leader. Our viewers have come to depend on our news team to be quick, fair, and accurate… from the first tweet and post, to the nightly wrap-up and anchor explainer, you’ll get all the news… and perhaps most important in a state where weather can kill you… an accurate and up-to-the-minute forecast. If you love the outdoors, you can’t beat North Dakota for boating, fishing (in all seasons), and hunting. We have more golf courses… some of them world-class… per capita than any other state. And in the winter, those same courses are perfect for cross-country skiers and snowboarders.

Job Summary/Description:

Maybe you’ve never thought of a career as a Technical Media Producer because you’ve never heard of it! Or maybe you’re nervous about the fact that you don’t have any experience in live broadcast production. If you’re not afraid of a challenge and work well as a team, then this may be the next step for you.

The Technical Media Producer has the general responsibility for directing live or pre-recorded productions, monitoring the station’s on-air signals, transmitter, and FCC logs, and ingesting daily programming and commercials. Regular assignments will involve directing newscasts, misc. station productions, special programs, breaking news, live sports, and severe weather.

Duties and responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

• Direct / Technical Direct live or pre-recorded productions (studio or remote).
• Direct/TD during breaking news and severe weather coverage.
• Ensure consistent on-air “look” with minimal error.
• Proficient operation and knowledge of Overdrive, production switcher, and supporting equipment.
• Ability to operate between multiple control rooms with no change in overall performance, and proper, effective communication within the TMP team.
• Proper and effective communication with Newsroom personnel, with the ability to handle changing situations.
• All Master Control needs, including media management, automation playout, and quality control.
• Proficient operation and knowledge of Master Control operation and supporting equipment, including but not limited to routers, automation, multichannel, digital servers, programming and spot ingest, ftp downloads, FCC requirements, closed captioning, EAS tests, Amber Alerts, transmitter and tower light requirements, News Live Shot and TVU set-up, Severe Weather Alerts and coverage, and breaking news coverage.
• Understanding and ability to implement backup systems and workflow when needed.
• Assist in production schedules, reports, and projects as assigned.
• Ability to adhere to all FCC procedures and requirements,
• Other duties as assigned

Qualifications/Requirements:

• Ability to perform the job requirements as described
• Strong computer, editing, and video skills.
• Ability to complete regular duties within regular work shifts/days/weeks without compromising quality
• Maintain a permanent residence within 30 minutes of the station

KOLO is a station that gets the job done. Many of our employees have been with the company for years, and they pride themselves on their expertise and their ability to succeed. While Reno/Tahoe is a 100+ market, it has all the characteristics of a much larger West Coast market. In fact, some say Reno has a superior lifestyle and outdoor activities to its much larger neighboring markets. For these and many other reasons, KOLO is able to attract top-notch individuals. We pride ourselves on not limiting ourselves to the "news conference or press release journalism" stories that are easy to get. Our journalists know they need to tell stories on issues that matter to the Northern Nevada community and our viewers. Much of the station's identity is from KOLOCares, a program designed to better serve Northern Nevada through the wonderful non-profit organizations that are part of the community. KOLOCares was recently honored by the National Association of Broadcasters' Celebration of Service to Community Award. Every station is tasked to serve their community, but KOLO takes pride in finding unique ways to help our non-profit partners to reach their goals.

Reno has an illustrious history of boom or bust, and right now the area is booming! Life in Reno/Tahoe is not just about work. Northern Nevada boasts remarkable outdoor activities highlighted by the spectacular beauty of Lake Tahoe, world-renowned ski resorts in the Sierra, trout fishing in the Truckee River and Pyramid Lake, placid campgrounds, miles of hiking and biking trails and, yes, casinos. San Francisco, Yosemite, and Napa Valley are all an easy drive for a weekend getaway. Many Northern Californians spend their weekends in Reno, especially with the summer festivities that feature balloon races, Hot August Nights, and the nation's largest BBQ rib festival. There is always something happening in Reno, the "Biggest Little City in the World."
