Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Real Chemistry Media is a data-driven media and omnichannel activation practice redefining how healthcare brands connect with the people who matter most. Powered by proprietary data, advanced technology, AI, automation and deep healthcare expertise, we create seamless, audience-first experiences that connect brands with patients, caregivers and healthcare professionals. Through strategic media planning, precision targeting, cross-channel activation and continuous optimization, we help clients deliver the right message to the right audience at the right moment, driving measurable business outcomes and meaningful impact across the customer journey.

Real Chemistry is looking for a Supervisor, Paid Search to join our growing team!

The Supervisor, Paid Search serves as the day-to-day client relationship and strategic channel lead across a dedicated portfolio of accounts, owning paid search strategy, campaign performance, and operational excellence. This individual translates client business objectives into comprehensive channel media plans, oversees account evolution and innovation, and is accountable for consistently delivering and exceeding established performance expectations. The Supervisor leads and develops a team of paid search professionals, orchestrates account priorities and cross-functional initiatives, and serves as a trusted channel expert to clients and internal stakeholders while advancing the capabilities of the broader Paid Search practice.

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—New York City, Boston, Chicago, San Francisco, Indianapolis, or Lambertville (NJ)—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs.

What you'll do:

  • Own the day-to-day client relationship for a dedicated paid search portfolio — serving as the primary contact for questions, updates, and strategic recommendations across all levels of client engagement
  • Own the development of paid search media plans, comprehensive media briefs, channel strategies, and measurement recommendations that directly align with client business objectives and broader integrated media strategies
  • Oversee all aspects of campaign management, including objectives, audiences, testing frameworks, and account restructures, ensuring flawless launches and consistently strong performance against KPIs
  • Design and lead optimization initiatives and innovation roadmaps; introducing new platforms, audiences, and technologies to drive account evolution and cross-channel integration
  • Lead the resolution of complex client business and campaign performance challenges, overseeing strategic optimization initiatives and account restructures to improve business outcomes
  • Translate media metrics and campaign performance into clear client business insights, owning the ROI narrative with authority
  • Oversee budget tracking and allocation across campaigns to maximize return, ensuring compliance with regulatory and industry standards including promotional review requirements
  • Supervise, mentor, and develop junior team members — providing guidance, training, and performance feedback in both in-person and remote settings
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives with Integrated Media, Analytics, Strategy, Creative, Client Experience, Ad Operations, and agency partners to advance integrated media strategies and identify opportunities for cross-channel collaboration
  • Drive process improvements, evolve practice documentation, and champion the adoption of best practices, operational standards, and platform innovations across the Paid Search team

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • Our Company values — Best Together, Impact Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always, and Accountability with an "I" — genuinely resonate with how you work and lead.
  • You demonstrate the Real Chemistry Can mindset by approaching challenges with optimism, accountability, creativity, and a solutions-oriented attitude, always looking for ways to make a meaningful impact for our clients, colleagues, and communities.
  • You are adaptable, resilient, and comfortable adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment. As our business grows and changes, so do we.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful, with strong prioritization skills, intellectual curiosity, and a desire to leverage data to inform decisions and drive outcomes.
  • You are energized by innovation and the transformative potential of AI, actively exploring new technologies, identifying opportunities to work smarter, and championing practical, responsible AI adoption that drives meaningful business impact.

What you should have:

  • 5+ years of paid search experience, with a track record of managing and growing client accounts, ideally within an agency or healthcare/pharma setting
  • Deep platform expertise across Google Ads and Microsoft Advertising; experience implementing new platforms, DSPs, or audience technologies is a strong plus
  • Proven ability to develop and present channel strategy, media plans, and performance narratives directly to clients with confidence and authority
  • Strong analytical mindset — able to make data-driven decisions, defend them to stakeholders, and translate complex metrics into actionable business insights
  • Experience supervising or mentoring junior team members, with the ability to coach and develop talent in a remote or hybrid environment
  • Highly organized, with the ability to manage multiple accounts, cross-functional workstreams, and competing priorities simultaneously
  • Familiarity with regulatory and promotional review requirements in healthcare or pharmaceutical advertising preferred
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build and sustain strong client and internal relationships

Pay Range: $90,000 - $105,000

job.title: Syracuse University 2027 Weiss Center Ambassador
job.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centered creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

2027 Weiss Center Ambassadors

*IMPORTANT NOTE*: This application is only for students who are currently enrolled at Syracuse University. If you are not a current Syracuse University student but are interested in applying for Real Chemistry's 2027 summer internship program, please keep an eye out for the job posting, which will go live in December 2026. We look forward to receiving and reviewing your applications then!

2027 Application Deadline: December 4, 2026

About the Weiss Center:
The Weiss Center is a student, faculty and industry-powered incubator that complements classroom curriculum through immersive, real-world application. By connecting classroom learning with the pace and expectations of the communications field, the Center helps students build the skills, perspective and confidence to enter the industry with a leg up.  

About the Role:
Each year, two Syracuse University students are selected to serve as Weiss Center Brand Ambassadors. The program offers a multifaceted experience that allows students to represent the Center on campus, contribute to its programming, and work alongside Real Chemistry experts and clients through a summer internship and other hands-on opportunities. Along the way, Ambassadors build the professional skills, experience and relationships needed to succeed in an evolving communications industry. 

Key Responsibilities: 

  • Summer Internship: Complete a full-time, paid, 10-week summer internship with Real Chemistry 
  • Promote Center programming: Work alongside Real Chemistry staff to drive awareness and provide on-the-ground support for the Center’s fall and spring programming, including the Jim Weiss Lecture Series, expert-led workshops, class visits and other hands-on learning experiences. 
  • Manage social and digital content: Manage Weiss Center social channels and collaborate with peers to develop blog posts and multimedia content. 
  • Build professional connections: Attend exclusive networking opportunities with Real Chemistry executives, staff and clients, as well as Syracuse faculty. 
  • Support a potential NYC benchmark trip: Help plan and attend a visit to the Real Chemistry office and other firms, pending schedule. 
  • SXSW trip: Participate in an all-expenses-paid trip to Austin, Texas to attend Real Chemistry’s events at the SXSW Interactive conference and support social media and digital content development

Candidate Profile:
We are seeking students who are enthusiastic about communications, curious about emerging industry trends and eager to help their peers connect with professional learning opportunities. 

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with an ability to adapt messages for student audiences.
  • Interest in social media, digital storytelling, AI & technology, analytics and/or the evolving communications industry.
  • Creativity, initiative and a collaborative approach to projects.
  • Organization and time-management skills, including the ability to follow through on agreed responsibilities.
  • Comfort engaging with peers and helping foster an inclusive campus community.
    • Other on-campus involvement is a plus 
  • Willingness to learn, receive feedback and contribute new ideas. 

Eligibility for the 2027 cohort: 

  • Qualified Syracuse University sophomores and juniors who will be on campus for the Spring and Fall 2027 semesters.
  • Minimum GPA: 3.0.
  • Selection as an Ambassador is contingent on being qualified for the summer 2027 internship program with Real Chemistry.
  • Particular interest in students with a background or interest in public relations, communications, advertising, marketing and/or information studies. 

2027 Ambassador Program Details:

  • Term: Proposed Spring and Fall 2027 on-campus service, plus a full-time, paid, 10-week summer internship. Note: Specific dates of summer 2027 internship program TBD (tentatively June-August 2027)
  • SXSW attendance: Ability to travel for all-expense paid trip to Austin, Texas (tentatively March 14-17), pending schedule
  • Time commitment: Full-time during the 10-week summer internship (40 hours/week). Anticipate dedicating approximately 2-5 hours per week during the spring and fall 2027 semesters to the Weiss Center Brand Ambassador Program 
  • Location: On-campus availability for the Spring and Fall 2027 semesters, with potential program travel for one to two all-expenses paid events, pending schedule.
  • Compensation: The summer internship is paid ($20/hour); any potential travel (Austin, TX and/or NYC) are all-expenses-paid. The Brand Ambassador Program is an unpaid, volunteer opportunity.

job.title: Education & Community Engagement Manager
job.description:
This is a hybrid position. Applicants must reside in the Tri-State Area to be on location for occasional programming and meetings.



WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 

The Education and Community Engagement Manager supports the development, implementation, and refinement of Grammy Museum Education & Community Engagement programs with a focus on educator-facing initiatives, curriculum development, professional development, student recruitment, and regional program support. Based in New York City, you will help expand the Museum’s East Coast education presence and support programs primarily East of the Mississippi River including Grammy in the Schools, professional development sessions, and seasonal Grammy Camp support.

 

You will provide curriculum expertise across programs to ensure consistency, continuity, and alignment with the Museum’s educational goals. You will build and maintain relationships with K-12 teachers, school partners, districts, and arts education organizations to support educator engagement, student recruitment, and professional development. You will also support application and recruitment processes for student and educator programs, ensuring outreach, application review, and participant communication reflect program goals and expand access for students and teachers.

 

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 

Professional Development & Educator Engagement

  • Lead planning, development, and facilitation of educator professional development programs, including virtual, in-person, district-based, and conference-based sessions.
  • Build and maintain relationships with K–12 teachers, school districts, arts coordinators, and education partners to support professional development, program participation, student recruitment, and ongoing educator engagement.
  • Identify and cultivate professional development opportunities with schools, districts, conferences, and partner organizations.
  • Collect and synthesize educator feedback to inform future professional development offerings, curriculum tools, and program improvements.

 

Program Alignment

  • Provide curriculum expertise across Education programs to ensure consistency, continuity, and alignment with departmental learning goals, while remaining adaptable to different student, teacher, and community contexts.
  • Develop and refine learning objectives, instructional materials, rubrics, classroom extensions, and develop and maintain program manuals.
  • Support alignment of programs with music education, arts education, career and technical education, college/career readiness, and workforce development frameworks where appropriate.
  • Collaborate with internal team members to connect curriculum and instructional design across Grammy Camp, Grammy in the Schools, Industry Sessions, professional development, and other education initiatives.

 

Recruitment, Applications & Program Process Support

  • Support recruitment for student and educator programs including outreach to schools, teachers, districts, community partners, and professional networks, building an application pipeline.
  • Support application and review processes for selected programs, including outreach, applicant communication, submission tracking, rubric development, review coordination, and documentation.
  • Help ensure recruitment and application processes are accessible, organized, and aligned with program goals, student readiness, educator needs, and equity of access.
  • Collaborate with the Coordinator and program leads to maintain accurate applicant records, support review timelines, and communicate next steps to applicants and participants.

 

Grammy in the Schools Support

  • Support planning and implementation of Grammy in the Schools programs, particularly those based on the East Coast and primarily East of the Mississippi River.
  • Assist with educator and school partner communication, program planning, instructional materials, and on-site implementation.
  • Collaborate with team members to ensure Grammy in the Schools programming is educationally consistent, student-centered, and aligned with the Museum’s broader learning goals.
  • Support development of program resources that help students connect music learning to industry pathways, creative careers, and transferable skills.

 

Grammy Camp Support

  • Support Grammy Camp planning and implementation including curriculum alignment, faculty support, student learning outcomes, and summer travel for on-site program delivery.
  • Support faculty onboarding, curriculum implementation, instructional planning, and integration of curriculum benchmarks across the camp model.
  • Help ensure consistency across camp cities while supporting local adaptation based on partners, faculty, students, and facilities.

 

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with the Vice President, Senior Director, Senior Manager, and Coordinator to support program strategy, planning, implementation, and evaluation.
  • Collaborate with Marketing, Communications, Advancement, Production, Guest Services, and Finance as needed.
  • Support public programs in New York as needed.
  • Represent the Education & Community Engagement team in meetings with schools, districts, partners, artists, faculty, and external stakeholders.
  • Travel for programs, conferences, partner meetings, Grammy Camp, Grammy in the Schools and other education initiatives as needed.
  SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 

  • Bachelor’s degree in music required. Master’s degree preferred in music education or a related field.
  • 3-5+ years of experience in music education, curriculum development, professional development, and youth program implementation.
  • Experience designing or facilitating professional development for music educators preferred.
  • Strong understanding of secondary music education, music technology, ensemble instruction, career-connected learning, and/or music industry pathways.
  • Experience developing music curriculum, lesson plans, educator resources, rubrics, or instructional materials.
  • Experience supporting music student or educator recruitment and application review processes preferred.
  • Ability to build relationships and collaborate with music educators, students, artists, K-12 schools, districts, partners, and internal teams.
  • Strong writing, facilitation, and presentation skills.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple programs and timelines.
  • Willingness and ability to travel including significant summer travel to support Grammy Camp.

 

 

PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAIN ROLES

 

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

 

While performing the duties of this job, the employee will be required to stand, walk, and sit for long periods of time, and work at a computer for long periods of time.

 

The employee may be required to lift and/or move up to 60 pounds.

 

 

SALARY AND BENEFITS

 

The starting salary for this position is $66,300 to $70,800 per year, benchmarked against industry standards. Salaries for positions required to be in specific geographic locations reflect the corresponding labor market. 
 
The actual offer extended will depend on the candidate's experience, qualifications, and the role's requirements. Positions working 20+ hours per week also receive our comprehensive benefits package (with medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, generous paid time off, and more). Click here for an overview of our company benefits.


Explore our career opportunities to join a team that values creativity, innovation, and diversity. 

 

 

ABOUT THE RECORDING ACADEMY AND ITS AFFILIATES

 

RECORDING ACADEMY

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers, and all music professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators.

 

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. In addition to producing the Latin Grammy Awards to honor excellence in the recorded arts and sciences, The Latin Recording Academy provides educational and outreach programs for the Latin music community either directly or through its Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation.

 

LATIN GRAMMY CULTURAL FOUNDATION

The Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation is a charitable organization established by the Latin Recording Academy in 2014. The organization is dedicated to creating opportunities for the next generation of Latin music creators through scholarships, educational programs, grants, and access to creators and industry executives.

 

MUSICARES

A friend and ally of the music community, MusiCares was established by the Recording Academy to safeguard the health and well-being of all music people. A four-star charity and safety net in times of need, MusiCares offers confidential preventative, recovery, and emergency programs to address financial, medical, and personal health issues. Through the generosity of our donors and volunteer professionals, our dedicated team works across the country to ensure the music community has the resources and support it needs.

 

GRAMMY MUSEUM

The Grammy Museum is a nonprofit organization dedicated to celebrating and exploring music from yesterday and today to inspire the music of tomorrow through music preservation, education, exhibitions, and public programming and aims to create a world in which shared love of music sparks curiosity, creativity, and community. Programs include Grammy in the Schools education programs that are offered year-round for students, teachers, and schools throughout the United States. 

 

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

The Recording Academy, its affiliates, and the music industry have a strong culture of inclusion and respect for everyone. The Recording Academy makes intentional, courageous, and principled decisions for stronger business outcomes and ensures that all creators and professionals live and work in a fair and safe environment. It is the Recording Academy's policy to provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. The Recording Academy does not discriminate on the basis of race (nor traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion (including religious dress and grooming), creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), national origin, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. The Recording Academy will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would result in an undue hardship to the Recording Academy. This policy governs all aspects of employment, including selection, job assignment, compensation, promotion, discipline, termination, access to benefits and training, recruitment, hiring, transfer, and social and recreational programs.

job.description:
INTERNSHIP DETAILS 

 

SPRING INTERNSHIP 

APPLICATION DEADLINE FOR STUDENTS: 11/20/2026

*The Advocacy & Public Policy Intern position pays county/state minimum wage rates, based on work location. 



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

 

The Recording Academy Advocacy & Public Policy team is seeking a “rock star” student for a spring 2027 Internship with our team. 


Celebrating music through the Grammy® Awards, The Recording Academy continues its legacy as the premier national organization for honoring achievements in the recording arts and supporting the music community. As a membership organization, we represent the most talented music professionals in the world. Our members include recording artists, producers, engineers, attorneys, music supervisors, composers/arrangers, managers, agents, social media and record label executives and many others. 


Our paid Internship Program offers a unique opportunity for full-time college students (juniors or seniors) to gain on-site training in office administration, advocacy, and public policy, in exchange for college credit. Candidates should be energetic, hard-working and have aspirations of a career in the music industry. 



WHAT YOU'LL DO


  • Internship duration is for a semester (12 weeks or equivalent).
  • Hours are part-time (20-24 hours a week).
  • Intern will work both remotely and in the office during regular business hours. 
  • Intern will require personal laptop.
  • Projects will include assisting with the Academy’s grassroots advocacy initiatives, outreach to congressional offices, legislative research, database management, and administrative office support.



SKILLS & EXPERIENCE


  • Students must be currently enrolled in a College/University for an Undergraduate or Graduate program.
  • One year of course work towards degree in related field is preferred.
  • Letter from school stating that intern will receive college credit for the Recording Academy internship program.
  • Display an interest in music and/or government and advocacy work.
  • Possess strong verbal, written and analytical skills.
  • Exhibit proficient computer skills and social media proficiency.
  • Be a sophomore, junior, senior or graduate student.

SPRING INTERNSHIP 

APPLICATION DEADLINE FOR STUDENTS: 11/20/2026 

SPRING INTERNSHIP PROGRAM DATES: 1/11/2027 – 4/16/2027  

*The Communications Intern position pays county/state minimum wage rates, based on work location.



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR


Are you interested in a career in communications within the music industry? Are you passionate about public relations, media relations, and events, and want to learn more about these areas?


The Recording Academy—the organization behind the Grammy awards—is responsible for groundbreaking professional development, cultural enrichment, advocacy, education and human services programs for the music community. The Communications Department is seeking an intern to work in its fast-paced, dynamic department where multi-tasking is key, professionalism is enforced, and a desire to learn is essential.



WHAT YOU'LL DO


  • Internship duration is for a semester (12 weeks or equivalent).
  • Hours are part-time (20-24 hours a week).
  • Draft press materials while keeping to brand guidelines, perform copy editing services as necessary
  • Develop interesting story angles and fresh content ideas
  • Pitch genre-specific media, and supply writers with needed assets
  • Work events on-site, including press conferences, red carpet events, and media rooms
  • Coordinate event production paperwork and project trackers
  • Conduct market research
  • Generate media lists tailored to specific projects
  • Track press coverage and create media reports



SKILLS & EXPERIENCE


  • Currently enrolled in undergraduate program pursuing degree with major in Communications, Journalism, and/or Public Relations
  • Letter from school stating that intern will receive college credit for the recording academy internship. 
  • Possess strong verbal, written and analytical skills.
  • Be a junior, senior or graduate student.
  • Ability to multi-task while maintaining attention to detail
  • Ability to work as a member of a team
  • Proficiency in multiple computer applications including Microsoft Office programs
  • Honesty, trustworthiness, and ability to maintain confidential material and maintain professionalism



PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAIN ROLES:   

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.   


While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, and sit for long periods of time, and work at a computer for long periods of time. The employee will be required to lift and/or move up to 60 pounds.   

 

 

ABOUT THE RECORDING ACADEMY AND ITS AFFILIATES 

 

RECORDING ACADEMY 

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers, and all music professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators. 

 

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY 

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. In addition to producing the Latin Grammy Awards to honor excellence in the recorded arts and sciences, The Latin Recording Academy provides educational and outreach programs for the Latin music community either directly or through its Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation. 

 

LATIN GRAMMY CULTURAL FOUNDATION 

The Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation is a charitable organization established by the Latin Recording Academy in 2014. The organization is dedicated to creating opportunities for the next generation of Latin music creators through scholarships, educational programs, grants, and access to creators and industry executives. 

 

MUSICARES 

A friend and ally of the music community, MusiCares was established by the Recording Academy to safeguard the health and well-being of all music people. A four-star charity and safety net in times of need, MusiCares offers confidential preventative, recovery, and emergency programs to address financial, medical, and personal health issues. Through the generosity of our donors and volunteer professionals, our dedicated team works across the country to ensure the music community has the resources and support it needs. 

 

GRAMMY MUSEUM 

The Grammy Museum is a nonprofit organization dedicated to celebrating and exploring music from yesterday and today to inspire the music of tomorrow through music preservation, education, exhibitions, and public programming and aims to create a world in which shared love of music sparks curiosity, creativity, and community. Programs include GRAMMY in the Schools education programs that are offered year-round for students, teachers, and schools throughout the United States. 

 

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY 

The Recording Academy, its affiliates, and the music industry have a strong culture of inclusion and respect for everyone. The Recording Academy makes intentional, courageous, and principled decisions for stronger business outcomes and ensures that all creators and professionals live and work in a fair and safe environment. It is the Recording Academy's policy to provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. The Recording Academy does not discriminate on the basis of race (nor traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion (including religious dress and grooming), creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), national origin, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. job.title: Intern, MusiCares Research & Wellness in Music
job.description:
INTERNSHIP DETAILS  

  

SPRING INTERNSHIP  

APPLICATION DEADLINE FOR STUDENTS: 11/20/2026  

SPRING INTERNSHIP PROGRAM DATES: 1/11/2027 – 4/16/2027   

*The MusiCares Research & Wellness in Music Intern position pays county/state minimum wage rates, based on work location.  

  

  

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR  

  

Since 1989, MusiCares, the philanthropic affiliate of the Recording Academy, has been the largest safety net for everyone who works in music. MusiCares has provided over $145 million in assistance to music people across all professions for basic living needs, medical care, mental health, substance use treatment and disaster relief. In recent years, recognizing critical gaps in evidence, MusiCares has begun investing in research, both internally and through partners, to inform our programming and the industry more broadly.  

 

MusiCares is seeking an undergraduate or graduate-level intern to support two key areas of our research efforts: developing our research strategy and our Wellness in Music survey.  

 

This is a remote position, and the selected individual may choose to work from MusiCares’s offices in Santa Monica or New York City, if located in those cities and preferred. 

 

  

WHAT YOU'LL DO  

  

Wellness in Music Survey Support: 

 

In 2020, MusiCares launched our Wellness in Music survey, an annual survey examining the financial, health and mental wellbeing of people in music. The survey has grown to be a formative set of data to inform MusiCares and the music community on key issues affecting this population.  

Each spring, MusiCares launches the survey through our network of thousands of individuals and across social media, and later completes analysis to identify key findings and trends. As part of this effort, MusiCares compiles and amplifies these findings through media outreach. In 2027, we will be taking the opportunity to refine the survey to improve the depth and quality of data captured.  

 

Responsibilities include:  

 

  • Refine and update the Wellness in Music survey, taking into account MusiCares’s data needs, available external data, and gaps in industry information. 
  • Partner with the ED and VP, HHS to define an analysis plan. 
  • Collaborate with the MusiCares team to disseminate the survey through our network and on social media. 
  • Conduct analysis, per the defined analysis plan. 
  • Support the development of messaging for external dissemination. 

 

Research Strategy Assessment and Design Support (approximately 4 weeks): 

 

  • Conduct a detailed review of existing research and data on the health and wellbeing of music people and compile into key findings. 
  • Identify key trends in emerging research, as well as critical gaps in our understanding. 
  • Collaborate with the Health and Human Services team to understand areas in which research and evidence could better inform their programs. 
  • Support the development of an organizational research strategy. 

 

 

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE   

  

  • Intern will work directly with the MusiCares Executive Director and Vice President, Health and Human Services. 
  • Currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate level program at a college/university, focused on public health, social work, economics, business, the music industry or a related field. One year of course work towards degree in related field is preferred.  
  • Letter from school stating that intern will receive college credit for the MusiCares internship.  
  • Internship duration is for a semester (12 weeks or equivalent).  
  • Hours are part-time (approximately 10-20 hours a week), with at least 10 hours each week during normal business hours to align with MusiCares staff. 
  • Display an interest in music and commitment to a career in the recording industry, along with a passion for serving the needs of under-resourced communities.  
  • Possess strong verbal, written and analytical skills.  
  • Demonstrated experience supporting research, analyzing publications and data sets.  
  • Exhibit proficient computer skills.

job.title: Intern, Songwriters & Composers Wing
job.description:
INTERNSHIP DETAILS 

 

SPRING INTERNSHIP 

APPLICATION DEADLINE FOR STUDENTS: 11/20/2026 

SPRING INTERNSHIP PROGRAM DATES: 1/11/2027 – 4/16/2027  

*The Songwriters & Composers Wing Intern position pays county/state minimum wage rates, based on work location. 

 

 

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

 

The Recording Academy Songwriters & Composers Wing is seeking a “rock star” student for a spring 2027 Internship with our team. 


Celebrating music through the Grammy® Awards, The Recording Academy continues its legacy as the premier national organization for honoring achievements in the recording arts and supporting the music community. As a membership organization, we represent the most talented music professionals in the world. Our members include recording artists, producers, engineers, attorneys, music supervisors, composers/arrangers, managers, agents, social media and record label executives and many others. 


Our paid Internship Program offers a unique opportunity for full-time college students (juniors or seniors) to gain on-site training in office administration, events management and artist relations, in exchange for college credit. Candidates should be energetic, hard-working and have aspirations of a career in the music industry. 

 

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO 

 

  • Internship duration is for a semester (12 weeks or equivalent). 
  • Hours are part-time (20-24 hours a week). 
  • Intern will work with the chapter office on local events during regular business hours as well as some evenings and weekends. 
  • Internship will provide in-depth exposure to professional recording industry techniques and practices. 
  • Projects may include assistance with event management, educational programs, newsletters, membership recruitment, database management, demographics analysis, and administrative office support. 

 

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE  

 

  • Currently enrolled in a college/university. One year of course work towards degree in related field is preferred. 
  • Letter from school stating that intern will receive college credit for the Recording Academy internship. 
  • Display an interest in music and commitment to a career in the recording industry. 
  • Possess strong verbal, written and analytical skills. 
  • Exhibit proficient computer skills. 
  • Be a junior, senior or graduate student. 


PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAIN ROLES:   

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.   


While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, and sit for long periods of time, and work at a computer for long periods of time. The employee will be required to lift and/or move up to 60 pounds.   

 

 

ABOUT THE RECORDING ACADEMY AND ITS AFFILIATES 

 

RECORDING ACADEMY 

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers, and all music professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators. 

 

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY 

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. In addition to producing the Latin Grammy Awards to honor excellence in the recorded arts and sciences, The Latin Recording Academy provides educational and outreach programs for the Latin music community either directly or through its Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation. 

 

LATIN GRAMMY CULTURAL FOUNDATION 

The Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation is a charitable organization established by the Latin Recording Academy in 2014. The organization is dedicated to creating opportunities for the next generation of Latin music creators through scholarships, educational programs, grants, and access to creators and industry executives. 

 

MUSICARES 

A friend and ally of the music community, MusiCares was established by the Recording Academy to safeguard the health and well-being of all music people. A four-star charity and safety net in times of need, MusiCares offers confidential preventative, recovery, and emergency programs to address financial, medical, and personal health issues. Through the generosity of our donors and volunteer professionals, our dedicated team works across the country to ensure the music community has the resources and support it needs. 

 

GRAMMY MUSEUM 

The Grammy Museum is a nonprofit organization dedicated to celebrating and exploring music from yesterday and today to inspire the music of tomorrow through music preservation, education, exhibitions, and public programming and aims to create a world in which shared love of music sparks curiosity, creativity, and community. Programs include GRAMMY in the Schools education programs that are offered year-round for students, teachers, and schools throughout the United States. 

 

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY 

The Recording Academy, its affiliates, and the music industry have a strong culture of inclusion and respect for everyone. The Recording Academy makes intentional, courageous, and principled decisions for stronger business outcomes and ensures that all creators and professionals live and work in a fair and safe environment. It is the Recording Academy's policy to provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. The Recording Academy does not discriminate on the basis of race (nor traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion (including religious dress and grooming), creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), national origin, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. The Recording Academy will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would result in an undue hardship to the Recording Academy. This policy governs all aspects of employment, including selection, job assignment, compensation, promotion, discipline, termination, access to benefits and training, recruitment, hiring, transfer, and social and recreational programs.

job.description:

Media Sales Strategist

Who we're looking for:  

  

We are seeking a dynamic Media Sales Strategist to join our team. This role is pivotal in driving revenue across multiple platforms, including Radio, Television, Digital, Out-of-Home (OOH), and Sports. The Media Sales Strategist will enhance operational efficiency and streamline sales tasks, allowing Account Managers to focus on building strong business relationships and improving solution selling skills.

 

The ideal candidate will possess a solid background in multimedia sales, exceptional project management skills, strong technical proficiency and a collaborative approach to working with both internal and external stakeholders, along with a keen understanding of the evolving media landscape. 

  

What you'll do:  

  

Transactional Task Management 

  • Exceed annual revenue targets by efficiently managing transactions and ensuring operational accuracy.
  • Assist Account Managers in developing strategy and crafting multi-media proposals and presentations that align with client KPIs.
  • Utilize AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot) to enhance efficiency and share insights with the team. 

  

Campaign Support 

  • Assist with operational details for campaign development and execution, ensuring seamless communication with internal teams and clients as needed.  
  • Collaborate with departments such as Credit, Creative, AdOps, Branded Content & Integrations, Go-to-Market Team, and Insights.  
  • Working knowledge of the RSM order management systems (S4M, DOMO and Hivestack) and monitor campaigns for optimal performance. 
  • Collaborate closely with sales teams to ensure all campaign deliverables are aligned and completed according to their business requirements 

  

Data Hygiene Maintenance 

  • Oversee the post-sale client journey for digital, OOH and post-campaign for TV and Radio campaigns, with creation of multiplatform wrap reports. 

  

Enable Consultative Selling 

  • Assist Account Managers by managing proposals, developing media strategy, and managing campaign deliverables, allowing them to focus on strategic sales priorities.
  • Foster a solution-focused team culture that promotes continuous learning and collaboration.
  • Assist with customer service support in the absence of Account Managers. 

  

What you'll bring:  

  • Proven success in a consultative sales or agency role, acting as a trusted advisor to clients.
  • Solid understanding of various media channels, including radio, linear TV, digital display, Video/Connected TV, OOH
  • Proficiency in using data and analytics to inform strategy and measure success.
  • Excellent written and oral communication and presentation skills.

  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency with various programs and systems relevant to media sales.
  • Strong relationship-building skills with both internal and external stakeholders.

  • Creative problem-solver, open to diverse ideas.
  • Flexibility and adaptability to changing business conditions.
  • Strong time management skills to effectively track and prioritize responsibilities.
  • Passionate about media and its evolving landscape.

  • Competitive & flexible health and dental benefits, pension plan, RRSP, TFSA, and Stock matching programs.

About Us - Values Overview

Welcome to the University of North Texas System. The UNT System includes the University of North Texas in Denton and Frisco, the University of North Texas at Dallas and UNT Dallas College of Law, and University of North Texas Health Fort Worth. We are the only university system based exclusively in the robust Dallas-Fort Worth region. We are growing with the North Texas region, employing more than 14,000 employees, educating a record 49,000+ students across our system, and awarding nearly 12,000 degrees each year. We are one team comprised of individuals who are committed to excellence, curiosity and innovation. We are transforming lives and creating economic opportunity through education. We champion a people-first values-based culture where We Care about each other and those we serve. We believe that we are Better Together because we foster an environment of respect, belonging, and access for all. We demonstrate Courageous Integrity through setting exceptional standards and acting in the best interest of our communities. We are encouraged to Be Curious about opportunities for learning, creating, discovering, and innovating, and are encouraged to learn from failure. Show Your Fire by joining our team and exhibiting your passion and pride in your work as part of our UNT System team. Learn more about the UNT System and how we live our values at www.UNTSystem.edu.

Department Summary

The Frank W. and Sue Mayborn School of Journalism is an ACEJMC-accredited school with the only professionally accredited journalism master’s program in the four-state region of Texas, Oklahoma, New Mexico, and Arkansas. The school is located in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, in one of the largest media markets in the country. We offer journalism classes in public relations, advertising, print/digital, broadcast/digital, and photojournalism. The Mayborn enrolls approximately 750 undergraduate students and 50 graduate students. Graduates have won many national and international awards, including Pulitzer Prizes. The school offers students multi-platform professional opportunities including the award-winning North Texas Daily student newspaper, Denton Public Access TV, and student-run photography and ad/PR agencies. The school also hosts the annual Mayborn Literary Nonfiction Conference, the nationally acclaimed conference for aspiring and experienced writers, journalists and authors.

UNT has a highly diverse campus with a wide range of languages spoken in addition to English. We welcome candidates who have experience with HSI/MSIs and/or who speak Spanish, Vietnamese, American Sign Language, Chinese (Cantonese, Mandarin and other variations), Arabic, Tagalog, Farsi, French, or/and Yoruba.

Position Overview

The Frank W. and Sue Mayborn School of Journalism seeks qualified individuals for its Adjunct Instructor pool and welcomes applicants at any time. This posting is for the Fall 2026, Spring 2027 and Summer 2027 semesters. The specific courses involved may vary from semester to semester and openings to teach these courses develop on a periodic basis, depending on department teaching needs.

The anticipated need is for:

News Writing – Introductory and Advanced
Photojournalism – Introductory and Advanced
Broadcast – Introductory and Advanced
Magazine Writing and Publishing – Undergraduate and Graduate
Race, Gender & Media; Sports, Food, Music and Opinion Journalism
Digital Media for Journalists
Law & Ethics

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in journalism or related field and at least 10 years of direct professional experience in media.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in journalism or related field and three years full-time experience in media and/or college teaching.

Experience teaching online classes is a plus.

The News Anchor serves as the primary presenter of news stories and other content for all platforms in a manner that is clear, engaging and meaningful to news consumers.

Are you looking for an opportunity to gain journalistic experience in both the newsroom and the field? Do you want to pitch stories, deliver newscasts, and connect with your local community? Apply to be an Anchor/Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) at Spectrum News NECN.

 

Spectrum News NECN covers MA, NH, ME, VT, RI, and CT. We use innovative journalistic approaches, backed by comprehensive research, to engage and inform viewers on the most essential news, issues, and events taking place in their communities. 

 

Beyond TV news distribution, our newsrooms publish via the Spectrum News app and connected television. We’re committed to providing viewers with 24-hour news—no matter how, when, and where they want it. Check out all the ways we share news on the Spectrum News Mobile App. 


As an Anchor/MMJ, you’ll build a vital connection between a story and your audience. From pitching stories to delivering engaging newscasts, your responsibilities will encompass all aspects of reporting and anchoring. You’ll be part of a collaborative team that creates compelling, timely, accurate, character-driven content to connect with viewers across traditional and digital platforms.

 

WHAT OUR ANCHOR/MULTIMEDIA JOURNALISTS ENJOY MOST

  • Striking a balance between reporting and anchoring
  • Going into the field to discover original stories and delivering news in-studio
  • Telling character-driven stories that resonate with local communities
  • Working across platforms including TV news, connected television, and digital news

 

As a part of Spectrum News NECN, you’re creative, highly technical, and ready to bring your community’s stories to life in our newsroom. You value accuracy and want to leverage your curiosity and storytelling abilities to share inspiring news across multiple platforms. Each day is fast paced in a constantly evolving work environment with new stories to tell and perspectives to uncover. If you’re a nimble, passionate team player, you’ll find a home on our team.

job.title: Anchor/Multimedia Journalist - Spectrum News SN+
job.description:
This role requires the ability to work lawfully in the U.S. without employment-based immigration sponsorship, now or in the future.

Are you looking for an opportunity to gain journalistic experience in both the newsroom and the field? Do you want to pitch stories, deliver newscasts, and connect with your local community? Apply to be an Anchor/Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) at Spectrum News.

 

Part of Charter Communications, Spectrum News is made up of over 30 hyper-local news and regional sports networks dedicated to producing original, unbiased, and high-quality content. We use innovative journalistic approaches, backed by comprehensive research, to engage and inform viewers on the most essential news, issues, and events taking place in their communities.

 

Beyond TV news distribution, our newsrooms publish via the Spectrum News app and connected television. We’re committed to providing viewers with 24-hour news—no matter how, when, and where they want it. Check out all the ways we share news on the Spectrum News Mobile App. 


As an Anchor/MMJ, you’ll build a vital connection between a story and your audience. From pitching stories to delivering engaging newscasts, your responsibilities will encompass all aspects of reporting and anchoring. You’ll be part of a collaborative team that creates compelling, timely, accurate, character-driven content to connect with viewers across traditional and digital platforms.

 

WHAT OUR ANCHOR/MULTIMEDIA JOURNALISTS ENJOY MOST

  • Striking a balance between reporting and anchoring
  • Going into the field to discover original stories and delivering news in-studio
  • Telling character-driven stories that resonate with local communities
  • Working across platforms including TV news, connected television, and digital news

 

As a part of Spectrum News, you’re creative, highly technical, and ready to bring your community’s stories to life in our newsroom. You value accuracy and want to leverage your curiosity and storytelling abilities to share inspiring news across multiple platforms. Each day is fast paced in a constantly evolving work environment with new stories to tell and perspectives to uncover. If you’re a nimble, passionate team player, you’ll find a home on our team.

 


WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO SPECTRUM NEWS

 

Required Qualifications

  • Experience: Television news anchoring - 3+ years, Television news reporting - 5+ years
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Broadcast Journalism, Communications, or related field; or comparable television work experience
  • Technical Skills: Video editing, still photography, social media marketing
  • Skills: Reporting and anchoring
  • Abilities: Managing multiple priorities effectively, lifting and carrying up to 30 pounds
  • Travel Ability: Must be open to travel to discover the important stories in your neighborhood and willing to interact with the community
  • Schedule: Work different shifts or longer shifts due to 'breaking news' and severe weather emergencies and able to work weekends and holidays
  • Valid driver's license for authorized driving in the state of residence

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in a 24-hour news channel

 

Working Conditions

  • Works inside in a climate-controlled environment but may be assigned to field duties and be subjected to various weather conditions that could include extreme heat or cold conditions.

job.title: Anchor/Reporter
job.description:
Job Title: Anchor/Reporter

Station: WREG-TV / Memphis CBS

Reports to: Assistant News Director

Purpose/reason for this Position: WREG in Memphis is searching for a seasoned storyteller to join a team of champions. We’re looking for a digger who can uncover leads in one of the sauciest cities in America. This place is news heaven, and the journalist good enough to win this job will be aggressive, resourceful and relentless. If you lead by example… if you care about being fair and accurate… if you are born to connect with others… let us hear from you. If you love the give and take of social media… let us hear from you.

You must include a link of your work.

Core Job Functions:

* Pitches unique story ideas every day.

* Builds and maintains a list of sources

* Gathers and turns stories on deadline that are fair, accurate, grammatically correct, and engaging to the audience.

* Presents those stories on live television… on set and in the field… in an energetic, conversational and creative style

* Posts and promotes those stories on multiple digital platforms.

* Cultivates curiosity

* Relishes personal responsibility, including learning new things and adapting to change as the world and the industry evolve.

* Works well in a team environment.

* Refuses to give up, even when people aren’t returning telephone calls, e-mails or DM’s.

* Protects the reputation and integrity of self and that of the station.

* Welcomes coaching and constructive criticism without rolling up into a ball or becoming hostile.

Minimum Knowledge Skills & Abilities:

Command of the English language, secondary language such as Spanish, helpful. Should be able to write in complete sentences with proper spelling, punctuation and format. Should be able to function under extreme stress and deadline pressures. Experienced in anchoring, reporting and news gathering. Should have working knowledge of the Internet and feel comfortable using computers and electronic newsgathering equipment.

Requirements and Skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Broadcast Journalism, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and work-related experience
  • At least two years work experience
  • Must have current reel showcasing your work
  • Ability to meet deadlines, prioritize assignments and handle multiple tasks simultaneously
  • Valid driver’s license with a good driving record
  • Flexibility to work any shift

Physical Requirements:

The Anchor/Reporter must be able to sit, conduct telephone conversations, use electronic mail, write letters and memos, conduct face-to-face discussions with individuals or groups, make decisions without supervision, make decisions that impact the results of co-workers, work near others, work outdoors occasionally in all weather conditions, and work indoors in environmentally controlled conditions. In addition, the Anchor/Reporter must be able to lift, set up and operate equipment weighing up to 25 pounds, and be able to handle, control or feel objects, tools or controls. Repetitive movements are required. Work may be conducted in extremely bright or inadequate lighting conditions.

Statement about Other Duties:

The foregoing is not necessarily an exhaustive list of all functions essential to the job for which the employee is responsible, nor an exhaustive list of the minimum requirements and specifications necessary to perform the essential functions, including all responsibilities, skills, duties, requirements, efforts, or working conditions associated with the job. While this is intended to be an accurate reflection of the current job, management reserves the right to revise the job or to require that other or different functions be performed when circumstances change or exigencies require it.

Do you have an eye for detail? Are you looking to kickstart your journalism career in a 24/7 newsroom? Apply to be an Associate Producer at Spectrum News.

As an Associate Producer, you will collaborate with producers in the newsroom to craft compelling stories. Your creativity and upbeat attitude will be essential as you tackle sensitive topics and tell character-driven stories.   • Working with colleagues in a collaborative environment

As a part of Spectrum News, you’re creative, highly technical, and ready to bring your community’s stories to life in our newsroom. You value accuracy and want to leverage your curiosity and storytelling abilities to share inspiring news across multiple platforms.   • Education: High school diploma

job.title: Broadcast & Streaming Anchor
job.description:
KSNW is looking for an experienced journalist to join our team as a broadcast and digital streaming anchor. We are looking for an individual who is an ethical journalist, team player, strong writer, and eager to contribute to the overall growth of the newsroom. The anchor will play an active role contributing to and anchoring our noon broadcast and help lead and develop streaming content for our digital platforms, including KSN.com, our streaming channel KSN+, Youtube, and social media. This role will help develop and execute streaming shows, in-depth coverage of daily news stories, breaking news and other community-related content.

Key Responsibilities:    

  • Presents reports, voices, writes, edits, delivers live (scripted and unscripted) news segments for all platforms in a manner that is clear, engaging and meaningful to news consumers.
  • Gathers, writes and presents accurate and interesting information for news stories and other content for all platforms.
  • Evaluates news leads and tips to develop story ideas. Gathers and verifies accurate information about newsworthy events by interview, investigation, or observation.
  • Ensures that all news content meets company standards for journalistic integrity and production quality.
  • Assists in writing, copy editing, researching, video shooting/editing and coordinating news programming and other content.
  • Presents compelling, clear, creative and accurate live shots.
  • Works with news team to identify and execute livestream opportunities; ensure high-quality production, accuracy and audience engagement.
  • Responds to breaking news and other urgent newsrooms situations as required.
  • Contributes to development of new livestream concepts and interactive programming.
  • Coordinates interviews and segments for broadcast and digital platforms, including podcasts, live newscasts and taped segments
  • Participates in promotional activities including public appearances.
  • Performs special projects and other duties as assigned.
  • Writes, presents, and edits print and video content for broadcast and digital platforms, including vertical video.
  • Interacts with viewers/users on social media sites.

Requirements & Skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Broadcast Journalism, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and work-related experience.
  • Minimum 3 years’ experience in news reporting; regular or fill-in anchoring experience also required.
  • Fluency in English, bilingual in Spanish a plus.
  • Excellent communication skills, both oral and written with the ability to ad lib when required.
  • Superior on-air presence and excellent news judgment.
  • Proficiency with newsroom, digital and streaming computer systems (such as vMix, Akta), editing, camera equipment, computers, telephones, and other office equipment; willingness to learn new systems.
  • Ability to meet deadlines, prioritize assignments, and handle multiple assignments simultaneously.
  • Ability to effectively listen to fully understand problems and communicate with a team to shape a solution.
  • Valid driver’s license with a good driving record.
  • Flexibility to work any shift.

Provide resume and digital reel when applying

job.title: Executive Producer - Spectrum News 1
job.description:
This role requires the ability to work lawfully in the U.S. without employment-based immigration sponsorship, now or in the future.

Are you a natural born leader? Are you passionate about keeping communities connected and informed? Apply today to be an Executive Producer at Spectrum News.

 

Part of Charter Communications, Spectrum News is made up of over 30 hyper-local news and regional sports networks that are constantly expanding and dedicated to producing original, unbiased, and high-quality content. We use innovative journalistic approaches, backed by comprehensive research, to engage and inform viewers on the most essential news, issues, and events taking place in their communities. 

 

Beyond TV news distribution, our newsrooms publish via the Spectrum News app and connected television. We’re committed to providing viewers with 24-hour news—no matter how, when, and where they want it. Check out all the ways we share news on the Spectrum News Mobile App.


BE PART OF THE CONNECTION

 

As Executive Producer, you’ll own the vision for the newscast. You’ll lead your team through story creation to produce compelling, timely, and accurate newscasts. You’ll be responsible for building a positive team culture, while generating story ideas that reflect your local community. You’ll make data-informed decisions to connect your audience with the stories that matter.

 

WHAT OUR EXECUTIVE PRODUCERS ENJOY MOST

  • Uniting a team of storytellers
  • Overseeing projects start to finish, including breaking news coverage and issue-driven special programming
  • Hands-on management and training opportunities involving graphics, cameras, and cross-newsroom workflow

 

As a part of Spectrum News, you’re creative, highly technical, and ready to bring your community’s stories to life in our newsroom. You value accuracy and want to leverage your curiosity and storytelling abilities to share inspiring news across multiple platforms. Each day is fast-paced in a constantly evolving work environment with new stories to tell and perspectives to uncover. If you’re a nimble, passionate team player, you’ll find a home on our team.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience: Producing and executive producing in television news - 5+ years,
  • Management - 2+ years
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Broadcast Journalism or related field, or comparable television work experience

  • Skills: Basic editing and ability to effectively train others
  • Travel: Must be open to travel to discover the important stories in your neighborhood and willing to interact with the community

job.title: Host - new daily show
job.description:
Host, New Daily Show

KNKX | Full-time onsite in Tacoma, WA

Salary Range: $90,000 - $100,000 annually, depending on experience


About the Opportunity

KNKX has a strong history of creating memorable, award-winning content. From long-form documentaries to deep reporting, the station has always valued creativity and the stories that matter to Western Washington.

Now, KNKX is launching something new: a daily, one-hour news, interview, and storytelling program airing Monday through Friday at 3 PM. The show will cover the news of the day while making space for arts, culture, and the stories that surprise and connect us as a region.


We are hiring two Hosts for this show. This is a rare chance to be a founding voice of a new program at a station that is investing and growing. In a media landscape where newsrooms are contracting, KNKX is creating something, and the right people get to shape what it becomes.


This position is based in KNKX's Tacoma, WA studios 5 days a week. This is a SAG-AFTRA union position.


Why This Role Stands Out

  • Be a founding voice of a brand-new daily show and help define its identity from day one.
  • Join a collaborative 6-person production team that values ideas from everyone.
  • Work at a station with deep community trust and a signal that reaches from Vancouver, BC to the Oregon border.
  • Fill a real need: this show is part of KNKX's commitment to serving Western Washington with useful, engaging journalism.


The Role

As Host, you will be one of two on-air voices leading this new program. Reporting to the Executive Producer, and working in partnership with your co-host, and a production team, you will help shape the daily editorial direction, conduct interviews, and deliver a show that is warm, sharp, curious, and grounded in the community.


This is not a role where you show up and read what is handed to you. You are part of the producing force. You bring ideas, you pitch stories, you help decide who gets interviewed and what gets covered. You are also the backstop: the last person to touch something before it goes over the air. That means composure under pressure, the ability to pivot when news breaks, and the instinct to follow a conversation wherever it leads.


Key Responsibilities

On-Air Hosting

  • Host a daily, one-hour live news and culture program, managing show flow, timing, and transitions under live-broadcast pressure.
  • Lead 2-4 daily segments ranging from 10- to 20-minute interviews with newsmakers, community leaders, artists, and experts.
  • Pivot when news breaks. Be willing and able to rework the rundown on the fly during a live broadcast.
  • Interact with listeners through call-in segments and participate in live community events.


Segment Production and Editorial Sourcing

  • Write and edit scripts, intros, commentary, and promotional copy to public radio standards.
  • Source interview subjects and segment topics and pitch ideas in daily team meetings.
  • Collaborate with the Digital Editor to adapt on-air content for digital, podcast, and social media formats.


Community Engagement and Ambassadorship

  • Represent KNKX at public panels, live town halls, station events, fund drives, and community gatherings across Western Washington.
  • Engage authentically with listeners across digital, audio, and social channels to build trust and expand audience reach.
  • Take the show on the road through live remotes and community events.


What We're Looking For

Must-Haves

  • Experience: 7+ years of live broadcast experience in radio, television, or a comparable live format. We need someone with time in the saddle who has handled breaking news, quick pivots, and the pressure of live programming.
  • Interviewing Instincts: A skilled, curious interviewer who comes prepared but knows when to put the questions down and follow the conversation where it leads. You seek the "why" behind every story.
  • Collaboration: A team player who brings ideas, collaborates with producers, and contributes to the editorial direction of the show. This is not a role for someone who only cracks open the mic.
  • On-Air Presence: Someone warm, genuine, and authoritative. You connect with people across political, ideological, and geographic lines through empathy.
  • Writing: Sharp, concise broadcast writing for intros, commentary, scripts, and promotional copy.
  • Technical Proficiency: Working familiarity with digital audio workstations (e.g., Audition, Pro Tools, Hindenburg).
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, Political Science, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
  • Location: This position is based in KNKX's Tacoma, WA studios 5 days a week. This is a SAG-AFTRA union position.


Sets You Apart

  • Strong understanding of Pacific Northwest political dynamics, regional history, and Western Washington community issues.
  • Prior experience in public media (NPR/PRI/PRX network ecosystem).
  • Experience hosting or moderating live audience events and community panels.
  • A proven track record of sourcing diverse, non-traditional community voices across ideological and geographic boundaries.
  • A flexible, audience-first mindset. You think about what listeners need, not just what is interesting to you.
  • We want hosts who can handle the hard things and still bring joy and a twinkle in the eye.


About Us

At KNKX we work hard to create a culture where employees feel valued and respected, are trusted and encouraged to be a part of improvements that impact their work, create value, and help build trust in public media. KNKX's vision is to grow and become a more inclusive organization that brings joy, meaning, and understanding into people's lives. We value diverse perspectives and an array of life experiences.

KNKX is a Western Washington public media company, dedicated to bringing jazz, blues, regional news, and NPR programs to the Northwest and beyond. As an independent dual-format station, KNKX employees are energized in their mission to provide the very best music and news content to an audience of more than 400,000 weekly.


How to Apply

Apply here: https://knkx.bamboohr.com/careers/67?source=aWQ9NjE%3D

Submit your:

  • Resume
  • Cover letter detailing your connection to the Pacific Northwest and your editorial philosophy
  • Audio reel (3-5 minutes) featuring live interviews or hosting clips


Compensation and Benefits

Salary: $90,000 - $100,000 annually, depending on experience

KNKX offers a strong benefits package, including:

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage with FSA option
  • PTO and holidays, including the full week between Christmas and New Year's
  • 401(k) with generous company match
  • Disability, life, and AD&D insurance options
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)


Interview Process

  • One-way video interview (4 short questions recorded on your own time)
  • Phone screening with the myHR Partner hiring team
  • Interview with the KNKX hiring committee
  • Recording a test segment with KNKX on-air talent
  • Final onsite interview


Our hiring management partner is myHR Partner. myHR Partner is not a staffing service or recruiter. All resumes/applications will be reviewed for this position and only for our organization.


Thank you for considering us as a potential employer!


Additional Information and Conditions of Employment:

Prior to hire, references and a background check including criminal record history will be conducted. Information from the background check will not necessarily preclude employment but will be considered in determining the applicant's suitability and competence to perform in the position. This is a SAG-AFTRA represented position. Union membership will be required as a condition of employment, per the terms of the collective bargaining agreement.


KNKX is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of age, sex (including gender identity), marital status, sexual orientation, race, creed, color, national origin, veteran or military status, or the presence of any sensory, mental, or physical disability or the use of a trained dog guide or service animal by a person with a disability. You are welcome to include the name and pronoun you would like to be referred to in your materials and we will honor it. Persons requiring accommodation in the application process, during the recruitment process, or who need this job announcement in an alternative format, may contact the Human Resources Office at knkxhr@myhrpartner.com.

You should be able to come to work with enterprise story ideas, make contacts in the community, and a desire to win the day.

Requirements & Skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Broadcast Journalism
  • 2 years MMJ experience
  • Fluency in English
  • Excellent communication skills, both oral and written with the ability to ad lib when required
  • Ability to meet deadlines, prioritize assignments and handle multiple tasks simultaneously
  • Valid driver’s license with a good driving

Job description:

  • Shoots and edits news events and news reports
  • Writes stories for the web
  • Arranges interviews with people who can provide information about stories
  • Reviews copy and corrects errors in content, grammar and punctuation, following prescribed editorial style and formatting guidelines
  • Researches and analyzes background information related to news stories to be able to provide complete and accurate information
  • Gathers information about events through research, interviews, experience or attendance at political, news, sports, artistic, social or other functions
  • Pitches stories to news managers and news producers which are relevant to the local community
  • Performs special projects and other duties as assigned

Job Description

Nexstar Media Group is America’s largest local television and media company with 197 full power stations (including partner stations) in 115 markets addressing nearly 63% of US television households and a growing digital media operation. Nexstar’s platform delivers exceptional local content and network programming to inform and entertain viewers, while providing premium, scalable local advertising opportunities for advertisers and brands across all screens and devices.
