job.title: Broadcast Engineer, KSTU
job.description:
KSTU | Salt Lake City, UT | Full-time | Onsite

KSTU in Salt Lake City is looking for a skilled and solutions-driven Broadcast Engineer to keep the station's technical operations running at the highest level. In this hands-on role, you'll provide preventive maintenance, respond to emergency repairs, and oversee the daily operation of video, audio, and radio frequency (RF) systems — including satellite and microwave equipment. From the studio floor to the transmitter site, your expertise will be essential to ensuring KSTU delivers flawless broadcasts to audiences across the Salt Lake City area. If you're a technically sharp engineer who thrives at the intersection of broadcast craft and emerging technology, this is the opportunity you've been waiting for.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Provide world class customer service to all business partners internal and external to the Scripps organization with a positive "can do" attitude.
  • Support, maintain, and install the full range of broadcast, Radio Frequency (RF), and production systems based on both Serial Digital Interface (SDI), and Internet Protocol (IP) based architecture.
  • Setup and enhance software, hardware, server, automation and workflow systems, projects and equipment to enable our teams to be both productive and efficient. Ensure all meet current industry standards and comply with Company policies and expectations.
  • Partner with the news department to develop, build and support content workflow and support systems including integration and problem-solving software, hardware, networking and infrastructure. This will include support and integration of audio and video, cameras, editing systems, streaming, content management and workflow.
  • Use company purchasing management system to purchase and track assets and services as well as replacement cycles. This will include contributing to budgeting planning with the team and Director of Engineering to support business needs.
  • Drive and assist in the operation, support, and maintenance of mobile live trucks which may involve work in confined spaces and on top of vehicle with the use of mobile work platform. Live truck technology may include microwave, satellite, cellular bonding, and video/audio equipment.
  • Resolve complex problems not covered by existing procedures or practices independently, often under pressure.
  • Design improvements to our operation.
  • Maintain logs and reports as per FCC Rules and Regulations.
  • Provide, enhance, and utilize proactive monitoring system to anticipate technical issues and be able to act accordingly.
  • Update technical plan documentation when installations are completed to include changes that are made.
  • Document and maintain records of equipment repairs.
  • Research part numbers and pricing to determine where to purchase and the cost of repairs.
  • Operate studio, news and control room equipment.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Associates degree in related field or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Generally, 5+ years experience in related field preferred
  • Network certification required (Cisco, CompTIA Network+)
  • SBE certification preferred
  • At least 3 year broadcast operations experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Must have working knowledge of all the following areas, and specialize in at least one of these areas: Broadcast and production systems support and engineering including SDI and IP based technology and workflow Extensive knowledge of computer networking, broadcast automation and workflow systems Transmitter support and engineering
  • Strong understanding and ability to work with IT/cellular systems, servers, and devices, and actively pursue emerging technology in these areas
  • Solid working knowledge of software for server and client operating systems including active directory
  • Working knowledge of Computer Aided Design (CAD)
  • Positive "can do" attitude and willingness to learn and grow with the job
  • Strong interpersonal skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver a high level of customer service
  • Team player
  • Effective communication skills with all level of internal and external customers and partners
  • Ability to resolve complex problems not covered by existing procedures or practices independently often whilst under pressure
  • Knowledge of FCC rules
  • Ability and willingness to learn complex new systems
  • Self-motivated to work independently under timeline to achieve departmental and station goals
  • Ability to comprehend schematics, mechanical drawings and technical manuals
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and work within deadlines
  • Familiarity with various test instruments, alignment apparatuses and knowledge of personal computers
  • Deep operational knowledge of studio, news and control room technology
  • Ability to guide and coach colleagues
  • Must be able to work a flexible schedule including able to work multiple days, holidays, evenings, weekends, and possible overtime hours as needed
  • Availability to travel over multiple days is possible
  • Must be able to work in changing weather conditions
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Salt Lake City is one of America's most livable and fast-growing cities, blending the energy of a thriving metropolitan area with the warmth of a tight-knit community. As Utah's capital and largest city, it sits at over 4,200 feet above sea level along the Wasatch Front, offering residents dramatic mountain views from virtually every neighborhood. From the eclectic boutiques and acclaimed restaurants of the 9th and 9th district to the vibrant, redeveloping Sugar House neighborhood brimming with arts, nightlife, and local eateries, Salt Lake City has a neighborhood and a lifestyle to suit just about everyone.


For outdoor lovers, few cities in the country put so much adventure within such easy reach. The Wasatch Mountains rise sharply just east of the city, delivering year-round recreation including world-class skiing at Alta, Snowbird, Brighton, and Solitude — all within about an hour's drive. When the snow melts, those same mountains transform into hundreds of miles of trails for hiking, mountain biking, and rock climbing. To the northwest, the Great Salt Lake — one of the largest saline lakes in the Western Hemisphere — offers a singular natural landmark unlike anywhere else in the country.


Salt Lake City's sports and culture scene has reached new heights. The Utah Jazz, Real Salt Lake, and the newly minted Utah Hockey Club give fans three major professional teams calling the city home. The Utah Symphony, Utah Opera, and the annual Sundance Film Festival in nearby Park City round out a rich cultural calendar. Meanwhile, the region's booming tech corridor — dubbed "Silicon Slopes" — has attracted top-tier employers and a talented, diverse workforce, making Salt Lake City one of the fastest-growing job markets in the entire country. It's a city on the rise, and there's never been a better time to be part of it.

job.title: Category Growth & Business Development Manager - Remote
job.description:
Are you a category-savvy sales strategist who thrives at the intersection of market intelligence and revenue growth? Operations Shared Services, part of The E.W. Scripps Company, is looking for a Category Growth & Business Development Manager to accelerate revenue across Scripps local television markets by serving as a go-to expert in priority advertising industries.

In this role, you'll partner directly with local sales leadership and account executives across the country, bringing category expertise, hands-on sales support and strategic vision to integrated linear and digital advertising opportunities. Your work will shape how Scripps competes and wins in key categories like automotive, legal and healthcare, making a measurable impact on markets from coast to coast.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Develop and execute division-wide growth strategies for priority business categories, including automotive, legal, healthcare and others identified by the organization.
  • Serve as the subject-matter expert for assigned categories by monitoring advertiser business models, customer-acquisition strategies, consumer behavior, competitive conditions, regulatory considerations, advertising trends and emerging marketing technologies.
  • Partner with local sales managers and account executives to identify high-potential prospects and revenue-growth opportunities across Scripps markets.
  • Participate directly in the sales process by supporting prospecting, discovery, needs analysis, solution development, proposals, presentations and negotiations, and assist in closing new business and expanding existing advertiser relationships through integrated linear and digital solutions.
  • Create scalable, category-specific sales strategies, prospecting approaches, discovery questions, presentations, case studies and other resources for consistent use by local teams.
  • Translate advertiser needs, audience insights, market research, performance data and industry trends into compelling marketing recommendations, and communicate actionable guidance to local sales teams, sales leadership and internal stakeholders.
  • Develop and deliver ongoing training, coaching and sales tactics that improve category knowledge, prospecting effectiveness, advertiser conversations, solution development and closing performance.
  • Join local sales representatives and leaders in advertiser and agency meetings to provide category expertise and advance priority opportunities.
  • Build relationships with key advertisers, agencies, industry associations and strategic partners that generate opportunities across multiple Scripps markets.
  • Collaborate with digital sales, research, marketing, creative, revenue operations and campaign execution teams to ensure solutions are strategically sound, executable, scalable and positioned to produce measurable advertiser outcomes.
  • Support campaign reviews, performance discussions, renewal strategies and upsell recommendations to improve advertiser retention and grow existing business.
  • Maintain accurate opportunity, pipeline, activity, billing and forecast information in applicable CRM and reporting systems.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • BS/BA in related discipline preferred or equivalent years of experience.
  • Generally, 8+ years of experience in related field preferred.
  • Valid driver's license and good driving record required. In addition, proof of insurance and liability coverage may be required.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Demonstrated success developing new business, closing complex opportunities and growing revenue from existing advertiser relationships.
  • Expertise in selling or supporting integrated linear television and digital advertising solutions strongly preferred.
  • Understanding of automotive, legal, healthcare or other high-value local advertising categories preferred.
  • Skilled in supporting sales teams across multiple markets or geographic regions preferred.
  • Adept at delivering sales training, coaching, presentations or category-specific enablement preferred.
  • Strong understanding of category-based selling, consultative sales practices, advertiser needs analysis and solution development.
  • Superior knowledge of linear television advertising and digital marketing products, strategies, performance measures and emerging capabilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence sales outcomes and lead cross-functional initiatives without direct reporting authority.
  • Ability to establish credibility and build productive relationships with local sales leaders, account executives, corporate partners, advertisers and agencies.
  • Strong coaching and facilitation skills, with the ability to improve sales performance through practical guidance, field support and category expertise.
  • Ability to convert industry research, audience insights, performance data and advertiser information into practical sales strategies and compelling proposals.
  • Excellent presentation, negotiation, written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong business and financial acumen, including the ability to manage revenue goals, forecasts, pipelines and performance reporting.
  • Highly organized, self-motivated and goal-focused, with the ability to manage multiple categories, markets and sales opportunities simultaneously.
  • Ability to balance strategic planning with direct, hands-on participation in advertiser opportunities.
  • Proficiency with CRM platforms, sales-reporting tools, Microsoft Office applications and virtual collaboration platforms.

job.title: Community Connections Coordinator, KNXV
job.description:
KNXV | Phoenix, AZ | Full-time | Onsite

What does it take to truly connect a newsroom with the community it serves? At KNXV in Phoenix, AZ, we're looking for a passionate and people-first Community Connections Coordinator to be that essential bridge. In this role, you'll cultivate meaningful relationships with community organizations, residents, and local leaders — surfacing the stories that matter, supporting journalists with trusted voices and timely intelligence, and coordinating the events and conversations that bring our station closer to the people we serve. If you thrive at the intersection of community, journalism, and engagement, this role was made for you.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Build and maintain relationships with community organizations, residents, leaders, and trusted sources to gather community insights and identify emerging issues, events, and story opportunities.
  • Monitor, track, and route audience tips, questions, and leads from community channels, ensuring timely communication and escalation to newsroom teams.
  • Support newsroom listening efforts, community conversations, and source development by connecting journalists with credible and diverse community voices.
  • Assist with breaking and developing news coverage by gathering community context, maintaining source networks, and providing timely intelligence to newsroom staff.
  • Serve as a responsive point of contact for community organizations and residents, fostering positive relationships and trust.
  • Coordinate outreach, maintain partner and contact records, and represent the station at community meetings, events, and activities.
  • Support newsroom talent by coordinating interviews, identifying community contacts, gathering background information, and facilitating community appearances.
  • Coordinate logistics and execution for community conversations, listening sessions, public programs, newsroom events, special coverage initiatives, and station appearances.
  • Manage event-related activities including outreach, scheduling, partner coordination, participant communications, on-site support, and post-event follow-up.
  • Support audience engagement across digital and in-person channels, including live discussions, community groups, neighborhood platforms, and other audience interaction opportunities.
  • Maintain community calendars, project plans, contact databases, and engagement records to support execution of the market community strategy.
  • Track community insights, engagement outcomes, story leads, and best practices, preparing summaries and reports that help inform newsroom and community engagement priorities.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Associates degree in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Generally, 5+ years of experience in journalism, communications, community engagement, nonprofit work, events, public relations or related fields
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Strong listening, relationship-building and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to establish rapport with diverse community members and organizations
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Excellent organization, follow-through and attention to detail
  • Ability to identify and communicate relevant community information quickly and accurately
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with journalists and station teams
  • Comfort working independently in the community and adapting to newsroom needs
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, CRM/contact systems, social platforms and collaboration tools
  • Solid news judgment, comfort with newsroom urgency, ability to verify and relay information quickly, and understanding of how community tips can develop into stories
  • Ability to communicate clearly and accurately across digital platforms, maintain professionalism in public-facing conversations and collaborate closely with reporters, producers, anchors, meteorologists and newsroom leaders

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Phoenix is one of America's most dynamic and fast-growing cities, offering a lifestyle as big and bold as the desert sky. As the capital of Arizona and the fifth-largest city in the country, Phoenix is a hub of culture, cuisine, and outdoor adventure. Explore world-class attractions like the Desert Botanical Garden, the Heard Museum celebrating Native American art and culture, and the Phoenix Art Museum. The city's thriving food scene spans everything from authentic Sonoran cuisine to innovative farm-to-table dining, and the year-round sunshine makes rooftop dining and outdoor festivals a regular pleasure.

Sports fans will feel right at home — Phoenix is a proud major-league city, home to the NBA's Phoenix Suns, the NFL's Arizona Cardinals, the MLB's Arizona Diamondbacks, and the WNBA's Phoenix Mercury. When you're ready to get outside, iconic destinations like Camelback Mountain and South Mountain Park offer hiking and climbing with breathtaking city and desert views just minutes from downtown. For a weekend escape, the red rock formations of Sedona and the grandeur of the Grand Canyon are both within easy driving distance, making every weekend a potential adventure.

job.title: Executive Reporter, KMGH
job.description:
KMGH, The E.W. Scripps Company ABC affiliate in Denver, Colorado, is seeking an Executive Reporter who will lead our mission to enhance storytelling and inspire the next generation of journalists. This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the narrative of our community while mentoring talented reporters and MMJs to reach their full potential.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Lead, develop, and enhance the storytelling skill and abilities of all reporters and MMJs in the station.
  • Collaborate with other newsroom leaders to consistently execute the content strategy through authentic, meaningful storytelling.
  • Oversee the writing of stories for all platforms; provide timely feedback to foster continuous improvement.
  • Develop and supervise effective workflow strategies and procedures for multiple news programs and outlets.
  • Ensure that all content adheres to journalistic standards and ethical guidelines.
  • Deliver a vision and create trust among reporters, photographers and newsroom staff.
  • May provide on-air, multi-platform coverage for breaking news as needed.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • BS/BA in related discipline preferred, or equivalent years of experience
  • Generally, 7+ years of experience in a related field preferred

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Demonstrated expertise in storytelling
  • Knowledge and demonstration of editorial judgment, journalistic ethics, and libel laws
  • Curiosity for the community, city, state, and world we report on daily
  • Deep understanding of content strategy
  • Ability to work a variety of shifts including nights, weekends, early mornings, and holidays

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK AND PLAY:

Denver, Colorado, combines big-market journalism opportunities with an unmatched outdoor lifestyle. As the Mile High City, Denver is one of the fastest-growing and most dynamic metropolitan areas in the country, offering journalists the chance to cover everything from rapid economic growth and innovation to government, transportation, education, public safety, and environmental issues that shape the future of the American West.


Situated at the foot of the Rocky Mountains, Denver provides year-round access to world-class skiing, hiking, mountain biking, camping, and countless outdoor adventures. The city features a thriving arts and culture scene, professional sports teams including the Broncos, Nuggets, Rockies, Avalanche, and Rapids, award-winning restaurants, and vibrant neighborhoods filled with unique stories and diverse perspectives.


KMGH is a trusted news leader serving one of the nation's most competitive and exciting media markets. With breathtaking scenery, an exceptional quality of life, and a community that values strong local journalism, Denver offers a remarkable place to build a meaningful career while making a lasting impact through storytelling.


#LI-SM2

#LI-Onsite

COMPENSATION RANGE:

Annual Salary: $110,000.00 - 117000


 

Pursuant to state and local salary transparency laws, the salary range posted is specific to candidates who will perform this work in Colorado.


 

ADDITIONAL BENEFITS:

  • A career path to grow your professional experiences

job.title: Local Sales Manager, WCPO
job.description:
Are you a proven sales leader who knows how to inspire a team, build winning strategies, and drive real results? WCPO is looking for a Local Sales Manager who thrives at the intersection of media, marketing, and leadership. In this role, you'll guide a talented team of Account Executives to help local businesses grow by connecting them with customers through a powerful suite of multi-platform advertising solutions — from broadcast television to Over The Top (OTT) video, SEO/SEM, social media, digital display, and email targeting. If you're energized by coaching people, developing creative sales strategies, and making a measurable impact in your market, we want to hear from you.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Collaborate with DOS and other sales managers and departments to accomplish the objectives of the station.
  • Organize, direct and manage the execution and performance of a team of local sales Account Executives.
  • Negotiate ratings, rates and budgets.
  • Develop new business for station utilizing and maximizing all station platforms including but not limited to broadcast, digital and mobile.
  • Develop working knowledge of Scripps Sales Process (SSP) and coach Account Executives regarding SSP in the field.
  • Utilize SSP, resources and tools provided to build effective sales strategies.
  • Collaborate with the Director of Sales and Sales Managers to train, develop and motivate the local sales team so that revenue goals are achieved.
  • Collaborate with the Director of Sales and Sales Managers to foster career growth and development of the local sales team so that a pipeline of talent for future Scripps sales management openings is ready.
  • Maintain positive working relationships with outside vendors.
  • Interface with traffic systems and personnel to ensure efficient management of airtime inventory.
  • Oversee accounts receivable and credit policies.
  • Develop and implement pricing and packaging to fill needs of both client and station.
  • Know the strengths and weaknesses of the competing stations, other advertising mediums and position the station accordingly.
  • Effectively forecast sales revenue and manage department expenses so that financial goals are achieved.
  • Other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • Bachelor's degree in business or related field or equivalent experience preferred
  • Generally, 7+ years proven success in media sales
  • Experience in agency and direct strategic account management, broadcast inventory and digital/video capabilities required
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Demonstrated aptitude for informal leadership and mentoring; fosters open dialogue, empowers others, addresses conflict quickly and directly
  • Strong coaching and feedback skills
  • Strong ability to motivate others toward team goals
  • Able to foster an environment that enables creative and innovative thinking
  • Strong influencing, selling and upselling skills
  • Effective teamwork and collaboration skills
  • Very strong analysis and data interpretation - able to help others translate needs and research data into sound marketing proposals
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills
  • Outstanding presentation abilities (in person/virtual, small/large groups, all levels)
  • Strong time management and organization skills
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel and PowerPoint)
  • Working knowledge of Google Office (Sheets, Docs, Slides) and virtual conferencing platforms (E.g. Skype, WebEx, Zoom or MS Teams etc.)
  • Proven ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment
  • May require some travel

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:


Cincinnati is a city that punches well above its weight — a vibrant, welcoming river city with a rich history, world-class culture, and a food scene that has earned national recognition. The Cincinnati Art Museum, the Cincinnati Symphony Orchestra, and the American Sign Museum are just a few of the cultural gems that make the city a destination in its own right. The revitalized Over-the-Rhine neighborhood, with its stunning 19th-century architecture, craft breweries, and acclaimed restaurants, has become one of the most celebrated urban districts in the Midwest.


Sports are a serious way of life here. Cincinnatians are passionate about the Bengals, the Reds, and FC Cincinnati — and attending a game at Paycor Stadium or Great American Ball Park along the Ohio River is an experience unlike any other. Beyond the stadiums, the region offers beautiful parks, miles of trails along the Little Miami Scenic Trail, and easy access to the rolling hills of both Ohio and Northern Kentucky, making it a great place for hikers, cyclists, and outdoor enthusiasts.


Cincinnati is also an incredibly affordable place to live, with a strong job market, diverse and distinct neighborhoods — from Hyde Park and Oakley to Covington just across the river in Kentucky — and a genuine sense of community. Whether you're raising a family, building a career, or simply looking for a city with authentic character and momentum, Cincinnati delivers on all fronts.

job.title: Maintenance Engineer II, WXYZ
job.description:
Are you a technically skilled problem-solver who thrives in a fast-paced broadcast environment? WXYZ in Detroit, MI, is looking for a Broadcast Engineer who will serve as the technical backbone of our operations — from preventive maintenance and emergency repairs to the hands-on support of video, audio, and radio frequency (RF) systems, including satellite and microwave equipment. In this role, you'll keep our broadcast, production, and live-truck technology running flawlessly, partnering closely with news teams and engineering leadership to push our capabilities forward. If you love tackling complex challenges, staying ahead of emerging technology, and making a real impact on what goes on air, this is the opportunity for you.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Provide world-class customer service to all business partners, internal and external to the Scripps organization, with a positive "can-do" attitude.
  • Support, maintain, and install the full range of broadcast, Radio Frequency (RF), and production systems based on both Serial Digital Interface (SDI) and Internet Protocol (IP) based architecture.
  • Set up and enhance software, hardware, server, automation, and workflow systems, projects, and equipment to enable our teams to be both productive and efficient. Ensure all meet current industry standards and comply with Company policies and expectations.
  • Partner with the news department to develop, build, and support content workflow and support systems, including integration and problem-solving software, hardware, networking, and infrastructure. This will include support and integration of audio and video, cameras, editing systems, streaming, content management, and workflow.
  • Use the company purchasing management system to purchase and track assets and services, as well as replacement cycles. This will include contributing to budgeting and planning with the team and Director of Engineering to support business needs.
  • Drive and assist in the operation, support, and maintenance of mobile live trucks, which may involve work in confined spaces and on top of the vehicle with the use of a mobile work platform. Live truck technology may include microwave, satellite, cellular bonding, and video/audio equipment.
  • Resolve complex problems not covered by existing procedures or practices independently, often under pressure.
  • Design improvements to our operation.
  • Maintain logs and reports as per FCC Rules and Regulations.
  • Provide, enhance, and utilize a proactive monitoring system to anticipate technical issues and be able to act accordingly.
  • Update technical plan documentation when installations are completed to include changes that are made.
  • Document and maintain records of equipment repairs.
  • Research part numbers and pricing to determine where to purchase and the cost of repairs.
  • Operate studio, news, and control room equipment.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • Associate's degree in a related field or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Generally, 5+ years' experience in a related field preferred
  • Network certification required (Cisco, CompTIA Network+)
  • SBE certification preferred
  • At least 3 years of broadcast operations experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company's required insurance limits.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Must have working knowledge of all the following areas, and specialize in at least one of these areas: Broadcast and production systems support and engineering, including SDI and IP-based technology and workflow; extensive knowledge of computer networking, broadcast automation, and workflow systems; transmitter support and engineering
  • Strong understanding and ability to work with IT/cellular systems, servers, and devices, and actively pursue emerging technology in these areas
  • Solid working knowledge of software for server and client operating systems, including Active Directory
  • Working knowledge of Computer Aided Design (CAD)
  • Positive "can do" attitude and willingness to learn and grow with the job
  • Strong interpersonal skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver a high level of customer service
  • Team player
  • Effective communication skills with all levels of internal and external customers and partners
  • Ability to resolve complex problems not covered by existing procedures or practices independently, often whilst under pressure
  • Knowledge of FCC rules
  • Ability and willingness to learn complex new systems
  • Self-motivated to work independently under a timeline to achieve departmental and station goals
  • Ability to comprehend schematics, mechanical drawings and technical manuals
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and work within deadlines
  • Familiarity with various test instruments, alignment apparatuses, and knowledge of personal computers
  • Deep operational knowledge of studio, news, and control room technology
  • Ability to guide and coach colleagues
  • Must be able to work a flexible schedule, including able to work multiple days, holidays, evenings, weekends, and possible overtime hours as needed
  • Availability to travel over multiple days is possible
  • Must be able to work in changing weather conditions
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:


Detroit is a city of grit, creativity, and reinvention — and there is no place quite like it. Known worldwide as the Motor City and the birthplace of Motown, Detroit carries a proud heritage in both the automotive industry and American music that you can feel throughout its neighborhoods, museums, and arts venues. The Detroit Institute of Arts ranks among the premier art museums in the country, while Eastern Market — one of the oldest and largest public market districts in the United States — buzzes with energy every weekend, offering local produce, artisan goods and some of the best street art in the Midwest.


Sports fans will feel right at home, with Detroit fielding beloved franchises across all four major professional sports: the Tigers (MLB), Lions (NFL), Red Wings (NHL) and Pistons (NBA). The Detroit Riverfront offers stunning views across the river to Windsor, Ontario, and Belle Isle Park — a 982-acre island state park in the Detroit River — provides a beautiful escape for running, cycling and recreation right in the heart of the metro area.

Detroit's neighborhoods are a draw all their own. Corktown, the city's oldest surviving neighborhood, is a hub of independent restaurants, craft breweries and creative energy. The downtown core has experienced a remarkable revitalization in recent years, bringing new restaurants, entertainment venues and businesses that complement the city's enduring character. With a relatively affordable cost of living compared to other major metros, a passionate community spirit, and a region rich in both culture and natural beauty, Detroit is a remarkable place to build a career and a life.

job.title: Maintenance Engineer III
job.description:
Are you a highly skilled broadcast technician who takes pride in keeping complex systems running at peak performance? KSHB/KMCI in Kansas City, Missouri, is looking for a Maintenance Engineer III to be the technical foundation of our operation — providing preventive maintenance and emergency repairs of video, audio, and radio frequency (RF) systems, including satellite and microwave equipment. Whether you're behind the scenes maintaining our studio gear or out in the field with a satellite IP truck, your expertise directly ensures our content reaches the Kansas City community without interruption. If you're a seasoned, solutions-driven engineer ready to make a real impact, we'd love to have you on our team.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Responsible for preventive maintenance and emergency repairs of video, audio and radio frequency (RF) systems, including satellite and microwave equipment.
  • Drive, set up and operation of a Satellite IP truck.
  • Maintain logs and records as required by laws and per FCC Rules and Regulations.
  • Install and maintain video, audio, RF and computer equipment. These systems include digital transmitter system, microwave systems and of all broadcast equipment including, but are not limited to studio camera and switching systems, video monitors and technical measurement devices, video file servers and automation systems, electronic graphic systems.
  • Install, maintain and operate all studio equipment.
  • Maintain and repair news bureau equipment, ENG equipment, IP truck, satellite dishes and related equipment.
  • Assist in the design of any improvements to our operation.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Associates degree in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Specialized training/certification may be required
  • Generally, 2+ years of experience in related field preferred
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Ability to use a variety of equipment including but not limited to: Ross switchers, Logitek audio consoles, Panasonic cameras, Ross Inception, Ross Xpression, Final Cut editing systems, Harris automation and Nexio video servers. RF and transmitter experience a plus. CAD experience a plus
  • Must be a senior technician or paraprofessional highly experienced with a similar level of responsibility
  • Ability to resolve complex problems not covered by existing procedures or practices independently
  • Must have knowledge of FCC rules. The use of test equipment and soldering skills required.
  • Ability to guide and coach colleagues
  • Ability to effectively communicate with departmental and station personnel as required
  • Ability to work independently under timeline to achieve departmental and station goals
  • Must be able to comprehend schematics, mechanical drawings and technical manuals
  • Ability to prioritize
  • Must be able to work with microwave, transmitters and satellites
  • Ability to effectively work and communicate with others
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule including able to work multiple days, holidays, evenings, weekends, and possible overtime hours as needed. Availability to travel over multiple days is essential
  • Ability to work in changing weather conditions
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Kansas City, Missouri, sits at the confluence of the Missouri and Kansas rivers and punches well above its weight as a cultural, culinary, and sports destination. The city is internationally celebrated for its legendary barbecue — a tradition so serious that it has spawned its own distinct style — alongside a thriving restaurant scene that stretches from the historic River Market district to the lively Crossroads Arts District. World-class museums including the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art and the National WWI Museum anchor a rich cultural landscape, while the 18th & Vine Jazz District pays homage to the city's deep musical roots.

Kansas City is a passionate sports town, home to the Kansas City Chiefs (NFL), the Kansas City Royals (MLB), and Sporting Kansas City (MLS), giving residents an exciting game-day culture across three seasons. The expansive Loose Park, the green trails of the Kaw Point Confluence, and the nearby Swope Park offer ample outdoor recreation in the heart of the metro. With a lower cost of living than many major U.S. cities, well-regarded neighborhoods like Brookside and Waldo, and a genuine Midwestern sense of community, Kansas City is a welcoming place to put down roots and build a career.

job.title: Multimedia Journalist, KERO - Kern River Valley
job.description:
At KERO 23 ABC, we believe every community deserves a journalist who knows its people, understands its challenges, and tells its stories with authenticity. As our Multimedia Journalist serving California's Kern River Valley, you'll be more than a reporter, you'll be the trusted voice covering a region whose stories often go untold by larger markets. This role is designed for someone who thrives working independently, building relationships, and becoming part of the fabric of a close-knit community. Nestled around Lake Isabella and surrounded by some of California's most stunning outdoor recreation, the Kern River Valley offers a unique lifestyle for journalists who value adventure, connection, and meaningful local storytelling. You'll have the opportunity to shine a spotlight on the issues, triumphs, and people that make this region special while ensuring local residents see their communities represented in the news every day.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Develop and pitch original story ideas that are relevant to Kern River Valley communities.
  • Research, write, shoot, and edit daily news stories for multiple platforms.
  • Deliver accurate, engaging live reports from the field.
  • Cultivate sources and build strong relationships with community leaders and residents.
  • Report on breaking news, public safety issues, weather impacts, and community events.
  • Produce compelling digital content, including videos, articles, and social media updates.
  • Work closely with producers, assignment editors, photographers, and newsroom leadership.
  • Generate enterprising story content that reflects the needs and interests of local audiences.
  • Meet daily deadlines while maintaining high journalistic standards.
  • Represent KERO professionally at community events and public appearances.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field preferred.
  • Previous reporting, multimedia journalism, or newsroom experience required.
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and the ability to travel throughout the coverage area.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Strong storytelling, writing, and on-camera presentation skills.
  • Ability to shoot and edit video content independently.
  • Sound news judgment and a commitment to accuracy, fairness, and ethics.
  • Excellent organizational and time-management skills.
  • A passion for community-focused journalism and audience engagement.
  • Confidence working in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
  • Proficiency with digital publishing tools, social media platforms, and mobile journalism techniques.
  • Ability to adapt quickly to breaking news situations and changing priorities.
  • Willingness to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as news coverage requires.
  • Ability to safely lift and carry standard field reporting equipment and work outdoors in varying weather conditions.

OUR TEAM:

The KERO 23 ABC newsroom is made up of dedicated journalists who care deeply about the communities they serve. We're collaborative, innovative, and driven by a shared mission to deliver accurate, impactful local news. Our team brings diverse experiences, perspectives, and talents together to create meaningful journalism that informs, connects, and empowers viewers across Kern County and beyond.


WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Nestled along the scenic Kern River and surrounded by mountains, lakes, and outdoor recreation, the Kern River Valley offers a unique lifestyle for adventurous storytellers. The area is known for its tight-knit communities, stunning natural beauty, and year-round opportunities for hiking, fishing, boating, camping, and exploring the outdoors.

You'll live and work in a region rich with local character and compelling stories, while remaining connected to the broader Bakersfield market. From community celebrations and small-town traditions to important issues affecting local residents, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact through your reporting every day.

job.title: Multimedia Journalist, KNXV
job.description:
We're looking for a storyteller who can do it all — shoot, write, report and most importantly - connect with the community. KNXV, ABC 15 in Phoenix, Arizona, is looking for a talented Multimedia Journalist to join our newsroom. At ABC 15, you'll be more than a journalist — you'll be a one-person powerhouse who brings the stories of the Valley of the Sun to life across television and digital platforms. From breaking news to in-depth community coverage, your work will inform, inspire and make a real difference in the lives of viewers across one of the nation's fastest-growing markets.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Receive assignment or evaluate news leads and news tips to develop story ideas.
  • Gather and verify factual information regarding stories through interview, observation, and research.
  • Organize material, determine slant or emphasis, and write story according to prescribed editorial style and format standards.
  • Shoot video and still photos to illustrate stories.
  • Edit, or assists in editing, videos for all multimedia platforms.
  • Appear on television program when conducting taped interview or narration
  • Give live reports from site of event or mobile broadcast unit.
  • Work cooperatively with photographer assigned to story, if one is assigned.
  • Assist news producer in preparing newscast.
  • Assist online staff in preparing for multi media stories.

 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • BS/BA in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Generally, 3+ years of experience in related field preferred

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Computer literacy required, including newsroom computer systems
  • Videography and non-linear editing experience preferred
  • Knowledge of broadcast quality camera equipment
  • Edit video on Final Cut Pro editing systems, or similar equipment
  • Strong broadcast and AP style writing skills
  • Proficient at posting content to various websites
  • Self-motivated and able to work in a fast-paced deadline-driven environment
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Phoenix is one of America's most exciting and sun-soaked cities, offering an extraordinary quality of life for those who call it home. With more than 300 days of sunshine a year, the Valley of the Sun is a playground for outdoor enthusiasts — whether you're hiking the iconic trails of Camelback Mountain and South Mountain Park, kayaking along the Salt River, or exploring the stunning red rocks just a short drive away in Sedona. The sprawling Sonoran Desert landscape is unlike anywhere else on earth, and it's right at your doorstep.

Beyond the outdoors, the downtown arts district offers a vibrant scene that includes the Phoenix Art Museum, one of the largest in the Southwest, as well as the Musical Instrument Museum — a one-of-a-kind destination that draws visitors from around the globe. The local food scene reflects the city's rich cultural diversity, from authentic Sonoran-style Mexican cuisine and acclaimed farm-to-table restaurants to a thriving craft brewery and coffee culture. The city also hosts beloved annual events like the Barrett-Jackson car auction and the Waste Management Phoenix Open, one of the most attended sporting events in the world.

For sports fans, Phoenix is a major-league city all the way, home to the NFL's Cardinals, the NBA's Suns, the WNBA's Mercury, the NHL's Coyotes, and MLB's Diamondbacks. With a booming economy, a young and diverse population, and world-class amenities at every turn, Phoenix isn't just a great place to work — it's a phenomenal place to build a life.

job.title: Multimedia Journalist, KSTU
job.description:
News is changing, and we’re looking for journalists who want to help shape what comes next. At KSTU Fox 13, an E.W. Scripps station, you’ll do more than report the news. You’ll help reimagine how stories are discovered, told, and experienced across every platform.


As a Multimedia Journalist, you’ll be part of a newsroom that believes local journalism can spark conversation, strengthen communities, and make a real difference. If you’re energized by breaking news, meaningful storytelling, and the opportunity to connect with one of the nation’s rapidly growing communities, this is your chance to be part of something bigger.

  • Receive assignments or evaluate news leads and news tips to develop story ideas.
  • Gather and verify factual information through interviews, observation, and research.
  • Organize materials and write stories according to editorial style and format standards.

  • Proficient at posting content to various websites
  • Self-motivated and able to work in a deadline-driven environment

OUR TEAM:

You’ll join a newsroom filled with curious, creative people who believe great journalism starts with understanding the community we serve. Our team brings different perspectives, backgrounds, interests, and experiences to the table, united by a shared drive to tell stories that matter. Whether you thrive on breaking news, unforgettable characters, accountability reporting, or finding the story everyone else overlooked, there’s room here to make your mark.

Salt Lake City gives you the rare chance to pursue ambitious journalism in a place where adventure is practically part of the commute. The Wasatch Mountains rise just outside the city, putting legendary skiing, hiking, biking, and mountain landscapes within easy reach, while Utah’s red rock country and five national parks make weekend road trips hard to beat.

Beyond the outdoors, Salt Lake City offers a vibrant mix of neighborhoods, restaurants, arts, culture, sports, and a thriving tech scene. job.title: Multimedia Journalist, WEWS
job.description:
WEWS News 5, The E.W. Scripps Company ABC station in Cleveland, Ohio, is looking for a Multimedia Journalist to join our award-winning newsroom. This is not an entry-level position. We are seeking a journalist who can separate us from the competition through exceptional source-building, enterprise reporting, and compelling storytelling. We want someone who knows how to uncover stories that no one else has and deliver them in a way that informs, engages, and serves our community.


Cleveland is a resilient and passionate city with a rich history, diverse neighborhoods, and a strong sense of pride. From the shores of Lake Erie and the vibrant downtown district to world-class healthcare, arts, sports, and cultural institutions, Northeast Ohio offers endless opportunities to tell meaningful stories that impact viewers' lives. WEWS News 5 has a long-standing reputation for trusted journalism, investigative reporting, innovation, and community engagement. Our newsroom is committed to helping journalists grow, develop their skills, and make a difference in the communities they serve. If you're ready to tell stories that matter and be part of a team dedicated to impactful journalism, apply today.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Receive assignments or evaluate news leads and tips to develop original story ideas.
  • Gather and verify factual information through interviews, observation, and research.
  • Organize material, determine story emphasis, and write content according to editorial standards and AP style.
  • Shoot video and still photos to illustrate stories.
  • Edit, or assist in editing, video for television, digital, social, and streaming platforms.
  • Appear on television programs while conducting interviews or providing narration.
  • Deliver live reports from the scene of breaking news and community events.
  • Work collaboratively with photographers and other newsroom staff when assigned.
  • Assist producers in preparing newscasts and coverage plans.
  • Partner with digital teams to create compelling multimedia content for all platforms.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • Bachelor's degree in Broadcast Journalism, Communications, or a related field, or equivalent years of experience
  • Generally, 3+ years of professional reporting experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with company-required limits

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Strong journalism skills, including enterprise reporting, source development, and storytelling
  • Proven ability to develop exclusive stories through relationship-building, public records research, and enterprise reporting that delivers meaningful impact for local communities
  • Computer literacy, including experience with newsroom content management systems
  • Videography and non-linear editing experience preferred
  • Knowledge of broadcast-quality camera equipment
  • Ability to edit video using Final Cut Pro, Adobe Premiere, or similar editing systems
  • Strong broadcast writing and AP style skills
  • Experience publishing content across digital, social, and streaming platforms
  • Self-motivated with the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
  • Strong news judgment and a commitment to accurate, ethical journalism
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK AND PLAY:

Cleveland, Ohio is a city on the rise, blending Midwest charm with big-city energy. Situated on the shores of Lake Erie, Cleveland offers stunning waterfront views, vibrant neighborhoods, and a thriving cultural scene. The city is home to the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, world-renowned Cleveland Orchestra, Cleveland Museum of Art, and championship sports teams including the Guardians, Browns, and Cavaliers. Food lovers will appreciate the city's diverse culinary landscape, from historic West Side Market to innovative farm-to-table restaurants and craft breweries.


Cleveland's affordable cost of living, strong sense of community, and access to outdoor recreation—including Metro Parks, lakefront trails, and nearby Cuyahoga Valley National Park—make it an ideal place to build both your career and your life. With a revitalized downtown, diverse neighborhoods like Tremont, Ohio City, and Little Italy, and a growing tech and healthcare sector, Cleveland offers the perfect balance of professional opportunity and quality of life.

job.title: Multimedia Managing Editor, KJRH
job.description:
KJRH, the NBC affiliate in Tulsa, Oklahoma, owned by The E.W. Scripps Company, is creating a new role for a new era of local news. We're looking for a newsroom leader who understands that today's audience expects news wherever they are, whether that's on a streaming channel, a phone, social media, or television. You'll be at the center of our operation, helping drive a 24/7 news stream while making sure the newsroom stays connected, informed, and focused on the stories that matter most. This role is part coach, part editor, part conductor. You'll help reporters and MMJs tell stronger stories, make smart decisions in the moment, and find creative ways to connect our journalism with the communities we serve.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:


  • Lead the daily execution of KRJH's 24/7 streaming news channel, ensuring a constant flow of relevant, timely, and engaging content.
  • Serve as the central hub for information entering and leaving the newsroom, helping teams stay aligned on priorities and coverage plans.
  • Coach and develop reporters, MMJs, and content creators to elevate storytelling across all platforms.
  • Collaborate with newsroom leadership to execute audience-focused content strategies that deliver meaningful community impact.
  • Oversee story writing, editing, and publishing workflows across broadcast, digital, social, and streaming platforms.
  • Provide timely and constructive feedback that drives continuous growth and stronger journalistic performance.
  • Develop and refine newsroom processes that improve efficiency, communication, and content execution.
  • Ensure all content meets the highest standards of journalistic ethics, editorial judgment, accuracy, and fairness.
  • Inspire trust and collaboration among reporters, photographers, producers, and newsroom staff.
  • Contribute to breaking news coverage and provide multi-platform reporting or on-air support when needed.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:


  • Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Communications, or a related field preferred, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Seven or more years of newsroom, content leadership, digital media, streaming, or related experience preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience leading editorial decision-making and managing content workflows in a fast-paced news environment.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:


  • Deep expertise in digital journalism, streaming content strategy, and audience engagement.
  • Strong understanding of broadcast-style storytelling and how to adapt content across multiple platforms.
  • Exceptional editorial judgment and thorough knowledge of journalistic ethics, media law, and libel considerations.
  • Proven ability to lead through influence, mentor talent, and foster a culture of collaboration and growth.
  • Curiosity about the communities, cities, states, and world we cover every day.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize rapidly changing news situations.
  • A passion for innovation and finding new ways to tell stories that resonate with audiences.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to connect teams around a common vision.
  • Flexibility to work a variety of shifts, including nights, weekends, early mornings, and holidays as newsroom needs require

job.title: Office Services Clerk (TEMP) KRTV
job.description:
Are you someone who takes pride in keeping the office running like a well-oiled machine? KRTV in Great Falls, Montana is looking for an Office Services Clerk (Temp) who thrives on organization, loves helping people, and enjoys wearing many hats throughout the day. From managing correspondence and welcoming visitors to stocking supplies and supporting the team with essential clerical tasks, you'll play a vital behind-the-scenes role in everything we do. If you're detail-oriented, resourceful, and ready to contribute to a fast-moving media environment, we want to hear from you.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Open, sort and distribute incoming correspondence, including faxes and email.
  • Greet visitors and determine whether they should be given access to specific individuals
  • Prepare invoices, reports, memos, letters, other documents, using word processing, spreadsheets, database, and/or presentation software.
  • Perform general office duties such as ordering supplies, maintaining records management systems, and performing basic bookkeeping work.
  • Maintain inventory flow and storage of office supplies
  • Participate in building safety and evacuation team at supervisors direction
  • Perform other duties as needed and as directed by supervisor/management.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • High school diploma or equivalent

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Basic math, reading and computer skills
  • Resourceful, possess excellent communication skills, ability to work with public and with other office personnel in person and by telephone
  • Strong attention to detail
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.

OUR TEAM: We have hikers, rock climbers, mountain bikers, kayakers, runners, skiers, gamers, hunters, fishing enthusiasts, beekeepers, western Montana gardeners, travelers, boaters, community leaders, and every other mixture of diverse backgrounds, passions, and life experiences. We are a community of welcoming, mission-focused, and lively people who continue to grow as we grow our company and rise to our full potential in every aspect of our business.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY: Great Falls, MT, is where outdoor enthusiasts enjoy the big small-town charm and quick access to national parks. Skiing is right outside your door as well as an expansive 40 miles along the River's Edge Trail. Enjoy a picnic at Gibson Park and Giant Springs Heritage State Park or get inspired by the local culture and art at the C.M. Russell Museum. Take a step back in time with The Lewis & Clark Interpretive Center and the First Peoples Buffalo Jump State Park to explore Montana's heritage and history. Whether you want to unplug and get off the grid and onto a hike surrounded by wilderness or enjoy the small-town charm of the local farmers market, restaurants, dog parks, and fly fishing or cultural events and performances at the Mansfield Center for Performing Arts, Great Falls has something for everyone. There are many reasons to claim Great Falls as a great place to live, including the reminder that you are walking in the footsteps of "the greats" from Lewis and Clark, the Blackfeet Indians, and the grizzly bear.

job.title: Ops Engineer II (Temporary, Part Time), WMAR
job.description:
WMAR, The E.W. Scripps Company ABC affiliate in Baltimore, MD, is looking for an Ops Engineer to join our team on a part-time, temporary basis. In this hands-on technical role, you'll set up, operate, and maintain the electronic equipment that keeps our station on the air — from controlling audio levels during live broadcasts to ensuring the integrity of our on-air technical performance. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment and take pride in the behind-the-scenes work that makes great television possible, we want to hear from you.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Perform floor director and teleprompter positions during live and taped productions.
  • Perform video receive and master control duties: monitor and adjust on air material within the automation system.
  • Observes records and operates transmitter power and frequency readings.
  • Set up and operate satellite and ENG receive equipment for recording programs, commercials or other feeds, capturing incoming feeds and other media.
  • Set up and operate Ignite automation system for news and other local material as instructed.
  • Operate camera controls and maintain proper video levels.
  • Mix on air audio for News and other local material.
  • Set up and operate IFB systems.
  • Perform necessary troubleshooting to all equipment including but not limited to News Ticker, Crispin Automation, Ignite, Chyron, lighting board and audio equipment.
  • Perform other duties as directed by manager.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Associates degree in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Specialized training/certification may be required
  • Generally, 2+ years of experience in related field preferred

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Working knowledge of Master Control, video servers, scopes and switcher operation in a broadcast television station
  • Knowledge of transmitter power parameters
  • Strong computer and communication skills
  • Ability to maintain composure and accuracy under deadline
  • Able to write IQT's and manage disaster recovery
  • Must be organized and detailed oriented
  • Able to work weekends, holidays and evenings.
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Baltimore is a city with a character all its own — a proud, working waterfront town where history, culture, and community run deep. The iconic Inner Harbor anchors the city with the world-class National Aquarium, waterfront dining, and stunning views of the Chesapeake Bay region. Fort McHenry, the birthplace of the Star-Spangled Banner, is just minutes away, and neighborhoods like Fells Point and Federal Hill offer a lively mix of historic rowhouses, local taverns, and an ever-growing restaurant and arts scene.


Baltimore is a passionate sports city, home to the NFL's Baltimore Ravens and MLB's Baltimore Orioles, both beloved institutions with dedicated fan bases. Beyond the stadiums, the city's cultural offerings run wide and deep — from the Baltimore Museum of Art (home to one of the largest Matisse collections in the world) to the one-of-a-kind American Visionary Art Museum, to Artscape, the nation's largest free arts festival held every summer. With Johns Hopkins University, the University of Maryland Medical Center, and a thriving tech and biohealth corridor, Baltimore is a city of serious intellectual energy.


Living in Baltimore also means easy access to the broader mid-Atlantic region. Washington, D.C. is less than an hour away by MARC train or car, and the beaches of the Delaware and Maryland shore are a comfortable drive for a weekend escape. With a cost of living well below many comparable East Coast cities and a true sense of neighborhood identity throughout its diverse communities, Baltimore offers an outstanding quality of life for those ready to call Charm City home.

job.title: Producer, KMVT
job.description:
If you’re looking to start or grow your career in local news, KMVT in Twin Falls gives you the opportunity to build real newsroom experience while enjoying a quality of life that can be harder to find in larger markets. You’ll help shape daily newscasts, make real-time editorial decisions and work alongside reporters, anchors and newsroom leaders to tell stories that matter to Southern Idaho. Twin Falls also offers an affordable place to build your career, put down roots and enjoy life outside of work.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Develop and organize newscasts and local programs.
  • Write stories and help determine how they are showcased across platforms.
  • Collaborate with reporters, anchors, news managers and assignment editors to determine daily content needs.
  • Enhance storytelling with graphics, video, research and station branding.
  • Make smart, time-sensitive editorial decisions.
  • Oversee live broadcasts and adjust content as news develops.
  • Perform desktop editing.
  • Publish content to the station’s digital platforms.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Bachelor’s degree in journalism, communications or a related discipline preferred, or equivalent experience.
  • Generally, 2+ years of experience in a related field preferred.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • A passion for local news and an understanding of the stories, events and trends that matter to the community.
  • Strong news judgment and the ability to develop and advance stories.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
  • A passion for writing and creative storytelling, with close attention to grammar, spelling, accuracy and the details that make a story stronger.
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • The ability to adapt quickly in a fast-paced, deadline-driven newsroom.
  • Strong self-motivation.
  • Working knowledge of journalistic ethics and libel laws, along with strong editorial judgment.
  • Familiarity with web analytics.
  • Proficiency with newsroom computer systems; Microsoft Office experience is a plus.
  • Flexibility to work varying hours, including evenings, weekends and holidays.

OUR TEAM:

At KMVT, you’ll be part of a local newsroom focused on serving the Twin Falls community and Southern Idaho. This is an opportunity to learn by doing, take on meaningful responsibility and develop the writing, editorial and production skills that can help build a long-term career in journalism.


WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Twin Falls can be a great place to begin your career without some of the financial pressures that come with starting out in a larger market. It offers a combination of affordability, community and access to the outdoors that makes it possible to build your career while still having a life outside the newsroom.

For someone looking for that first big opportunity in the business, Twin Falls offers the chance to gain hands-on experience, grow your skills and establish yourself in a community where local journalism matters.

job.title: Producer, KNXV
job.description:
KNXV, The E.W. Scripps ABC affiliate in Phoenix, Arizona is looking for a creative, organized Producer who will showcase content for multiple platforms.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Develop and organize newscasts or local programs. 
  • Write story development and showcasing.
  • Collaborate with reporters, anchors, news managers and assignment editors to determine content needs.
  • Enhance content with graphics, video, research, and station branding.
  • Execute time sensitive decisions.
  • Oversee live broadcast and up to the minute editorial decisions.
  • Perform desktop editing.
  • Post content to station's Web sites.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • BS/BA in related discipline preferred or equivalent years of experience
  • Generally, 2+ years of experience  in related field preferred

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Avid local news consumer: knows daily news, events, trends and happenings on a local level
  • Strong vision and ability to advance stories
  • Excellent interpersonal communicator
  • Extraordinarily passionate about writing; courageous and creative storyteller with attention to even tiny details - choosing the perfect words, grammar, spelling
  • Highly organized
  • Highly adaptable - fast paced, deadline driven environment
  • Strong self-motivation
  • Working knowledge of journalistic ethics and libel laws and strong editorial judgement
  • Able to use web analytics
  • Proficient with newsroom computer systems, MS Office a plus 
  • Flexible work hours may be required, including holidays, weekends and evenings

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Phoenix is one of America's most exciting and sun-soaked cities, offering an extraordinary quality of life for those who call it home. With more than 300 days of sunshine a year, the Valley of the Sun is a playground for outdoor enthusiasts — whether you're hiking the iconic trails of Camelback Mountain and South Mountain Park, kayaking along the Salt River, or exploring the stunning red rocks just a short drive away in Sedona. The sprawling Sonoran Desert landscape is unlike anywhere else on earth, and it's right at your doorstep.

Beyond the outdoors, the downtown arts district offers a vibrant scene that includes the Phoenix Art Museum, one of the largest in the Southwest, as well as the Musical Instrument Museum — a one-of-a-kind destination that draws visitors from around the globe. The local food scene reflects the city's rich cultural diversity, from authentic Sonoran-style Mexican cuisine and acclaimed farm-to-table restaurants to a thriving craft brewery and coffee culture. The city also hosts beloved annual events like the Barrett-Jackson car auction and the Waste Management Phoenix Open, one of the most attended sporting events in the world.

For sports fans, Phoenix is a major-league city all the way, home to the NFL's Cardinals, the NBA's Suns, the WNBA's Mercury, the NHL's Coyotes, and MLB's Diamondbacks. With a booming economy, a young and diverse population, and world-class amenities at every turn, Phoenix isn't just a great place to work — it's a phenomenal place to build a life.

job.title: Regional Sr Director Sales
job.description:
Are you a seasoned sales leader ready to make a sweeping impact across multiple markets? We are currently looking for a Regional Sr. Director, Sales to lead our sales organizations and help local and national businesses unlock growth through compelling multi-platform advertising solutions in the Montana Market. In this role, you will provide strategic leadership, revenue oversight, talent development, and operational excellence across a designated geographic zone — partnering cross-functionally to drive consistent revenue growth, maximize inventory performance, and ensure execution of company sales strategies and initiatives. If you thrive on building high-performing teams, forging strong client relationships, and translating strategy into measurable results, this is the opportunity for you.


*Location flexibility is available across our Montana stations, including KBZK, KTVQ, KPAX, KTVH, and KRTV.*

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Partner with market leaders and local sales leadership across multiple markets to establish and achieve revenue, profitability, and strategic objectives.
  • Develop and oversee zonal revenue plans, budgets, forecasts, and performance targets to ensure annual revenue goals are achieved across all assigned markets.
  • Provide strategic direction to market sales leaders while ensuring alignment with company sales strategies, priorities, and performance expectations.
  • Monitor market performance through regular business reviews, identifying opportunities, risks, and corrective actions to optimize results.
  • Drive consistency in inventory management, pricing strategy, and revenue optimization practices across all assigned markets.
  • Collaborate with local sales leaders to maximize broadcast, streaming, and digital revenue opportunities and ensure effective sales execution.
  • Partner with enterprise and national sales leaders to strengthen cross-market selling strategies and maximize revenue opportunities.
  • Meet with key clients, agencies, advertisers, and community stakeholders throughout the zone to strengthen relationships and support business growth.
  • Establish and promote best practices across assigned markets to improve sales effectiveness, productivity, and customer outcomes.
  • Lead and support enterprise, regional, and local revenue initiatives across multiple markets.
  • Build and maintain a strong leadership and talent pipeline across the zone, identifying successors for key sales leadership positions.
  • Collaborate with traffic, finance, and operational teams to optimize inventory utilization and revenue management practices.
  • Ensure compliance with company policies, industry regulations, and political advertising guidelines across all assigned markets.
  • Assess competitive market dynamics across the zone and develop strategies that strengthen market position and revenue growth.
  • Maintain the highest standards of integrity, accountability, and business conduct.
  • Other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, or related field, or equivalent experience preferred
  • Generally, 10+ years of proven success in media sales leadership with significant responsibility for multi-market, regional, or enterprise revenue management
  • Demonstrated success leading sales leaders and sales organizations across multiple locations
  • Advanced experience in inventory management, pricing strategy, political advertising, and revenue forecasting
  • Experience in agency and direct strategic account management, broadcast inventory management, streaming, digital, and video advertising solutions
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Proven ability to lead through influence in a matrixed organizational structure
  • Strong strategic and analytical capabilities with the ability to translate insights into actionable business plans
  • Demonstrated ability to lead geographically dispersed teams and drive organizational alignment
  • Strong executive presence and ability to effectively influence senior leaders and stakeholders
  • Proven leadership skills that foster accountability, collaboration, engagement, and performance
  • Exceptional coaching and talent development capabilities
  • Ability to identify and scale best practices across multiple markets
  • Strong change management and organizational effectiveness skills
  • Effective decision-making abilities in complex and rapidly changing environments
  • Advanced oral, written, and presentation communication skills
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining focus on strategic outcomes
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, CRM platforms, sales analytics tools, and virtual collaboration technologies
  • Frequent travel throughout assigned markets and corporate locations as needed

OUR TEAM:

We have hikers, rock climbers, mountain bikers, kayakers, runners, skiers, fishing enthusiasts, boaters, and every other mixture of diverse backgrounds, passions, and life experiences. We are a community of welcoming, mission-focused, and lively people who continue to grow as we grow our company and rise to our full potential in every aspect of our business.



WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Bozeman, Montana, has a history still alive with the remnants of bygone days and sustains a local heritage that can still be found throughout the community, with nine historical districts and more than 40 individual properties listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The town of Bozeman provides a unique environment for a different kind of lifestyle and often tops lists of best places to live. It is blessed with relatively good weather, outstanding scenery, unparalleled recreational opportunities, world-class fishing, plenty of cultural activities, galleries, museums, and the like. Tech start-up companies are prevalent and growing in the area. The Bozeman area has served as a filming site for a number of films, including The Wildest Dream, A River Runs Through It, A Plumm Summer and Amazing Grace, and Chuck. Bozeman is a short (and beautiful) drive to Yellowstone National Park. Big Sky resort draws the world's wealthiest people as well as A-list celebrities. If you're skiing at Big Sky, you could literally run into your favorite celebrity or professional athlete. Bozeman is also an up-and-coming foodie town. We have very few chain restaurants because people here want the unique experience of dining local, from pizzerias that feature southwest Montana's best home-grown ingredients to steakhouses that showcase local grass-fed and sustainably raised beef.
