job.title: Head of Inclusion Partnerships and Industry Engagement
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

ABOUT WPP

WPP is undergoing its most significant structural transformation in decades. Through Elevate28, we are moving from a holding company model to a single integrated operating company. The EVP WPP is building for the Elevate28 era is anchored on five dimensions – one of which is Inclusion & Belonging. This role ensures WPP shows up in the industry as one company and as a recognised leader in inclusive practice.

Within this transformation, WPP’s Inclusion & Impact (I&I) team is pioneering an innovative, enterprise-wide approach that moves decisively beyond traditional DEI. We treat inclusion as a strategic business enabler—designing and embedding scalable, measurable, and innovative practices directly into our business operations, creative work, client relationships, and workplace culture to shape meaningful behavioral change. This role ensures WPP show up across the creative, marketing, and media ecosystem as one unified company and recognized voice in inclusive practice.

ROLE OVERVIEW

The Head of Inclusion Partnerships & Industry Engagement is an enterprise-wide strategic, advisory, and ambassadorial leader who defines where and how WPP shows up globally for inclusion and impact. This role consolidates historically fragmented decisions into a unified WPP strategy—curating where we invest our brand equity, which strategic partners we ally with, which major industry stages we command, and which recognition benchmarks we pursue.

This is a brand positioning, external engagement, and strategically influential role, centered in inclusion. Operating at the intersection of brand reputation, industry engagement, and modern inclusion, you bring deep agency ecosystem fluency and the presence to build immediate credibility with senior executives, brand marketers, and cultural changemakers. You will establish rigorous investment criteria, steward a dedicated global budget, and serve as an articulate champion for WPP—shaping industry behavior, reinforcing client trust, activating diverse talent pipelines, and earning industry recognition.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  1. Strategic Inclusion Partnership & Investment Strategy (40%)
    Establish a criteria-led, enterprise approach to external alliances and partners.
  • Partnership Strategy: Set the global framework for identifying, assessing, and prioritising external inclusion partners, industry bodies, and community organizations – ensuring alignment to the Inclusion & Impact Strategy.
  • Sponsorship Governance: Build and lead an enterprise intake and evaluation model for global industry partnerships, transitioning legacy, ad-hoc agency investments into a cohesive, high-impact One WPP investment strategy.
  • Investment Allocations: Recommend annual allocations from the dedicated sponsorship budget based on strategic fit, audience, and expected impact. Spend tracking and vendor administration sit with P&C Operations and GBS.
  • Partnership Portfolio Leadership: Direct the overall partnership lifecycle – including renewals, tiering, strategic evolution – with guidance from the Inclusion Partnerships & Client Engagement Lead.

Key KPIs & Objectives:

  • Establish Partnership & Sponsorship Framework, with tiering, selection criteria, and an intake process for event and sponsorship requests.
  • Set an Annual Sponsorship Investment Plan recommended and approved within the allocated budget.
  • Consolidate Legacy agency-level commitments into high-yield, unified enterprise partnerships
  1. Industry Presence & Engagement (35%)
    Positioning WPP as a global growth partner centered on inclusion
  • Event Activation: Lead WPP’s inclusion presence at priority industry moments (e.g., Cannes Lions, Advertising Week, CES, Campaign, Adobe Summit), embedding I&I into mainstage programming, brand roundtables, and other engagements.
  • Frontline Ambassador: Serve as a representative, building relationships with partners, clients, and industry leaders across a range of settings and audiences.
  • Thought Leadership Curation: Translate progressive organizational practices into compelling public narratives; collaborate with Regional Inclusion Directors and MarComms to prepare, position, and amplify diverse executive voices, ERG leaders, and breakthrough creative talent on international stages.

job.title: IAM Engineer - SSO
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

Why we're hiring:

The Senior Identity and Access security Engineer is responsible for governing who, and what, can access DTS systems, data, APIs, tools, workflows and AI-enabled capabilities.

This is a hands-on governance and control role, reporting into the SVP Security and Compliance. The role ensures that access across DTS is appropriate, auditable, reviewed, least-privileged and aligned with security, privacy, compliance and client commitments.

The scope covers traditional human access, external users, privileged access, service accounts, machine identities, API keys, tokens, dataset access, and the emerging governance of AI agents and agentic workflows.

The role will work closely with Architecture, Security, Product, Engineering, Infrastructure, Privacy, Legal/DPO, TechOps, Enterprise Technology and the ISMS and Risk Officer to ensure DTS has a clear and controlled model for access across platforms such as WPP Open, Choreograph, InfoSum, Open Intelligence, Resolve and related DTS capabilities.

 

What you'll be doing:

1. Identity and access governance framework

Define and maintain the access governance framework for DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining access governance standards, processes and control expectations.
  • Establishing how access should be requested, approved, provisioned, reviewed, revoked and evidenced.
  • Ensuring access governance covers internal users, external users, clients, partners, vendors, service accounts, machine identities and AI agents.
  • Aligning identity and access governance with DTS architecture, security, privacy, compliance and data governance requirements.
  • Ensuring access governance is practical for product and engineering teams to implement.

 

2. Access reviews and recertification

Own the process for regular access reviews and recertification across DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining the scope, frequency and evidence requirements for access reviews.
  • Coordinating access reviews for critical DTS systems, production environments, privileged roles, sensitive datasets, client-facing platforms and administrative tools.
  • Ensuring access review outcomes are tracked, remediated and evidenced.
  • Identifying stale, excessive, orphaned or poorly owned access.
  • Escalating overdue, high-risk or unresolved access issues through the appropriate governance channels.

 

3. Privileged access governance

Ensure privileged access across DTS is properly controlled, justified and auditable.

This includes:

  • Reviewing access to production systems, cloud environments, security tools, databases, CI/CD tooling, administrative consoles and sensitive platforms.
  • Supporting least-privilege, just-in-time and time-bound access models where appropriate.
  • Working with Cloud and Platform Security and Infrastructure to improve privileged access controls.
  • Ensuring privileged access risks are visible in the DTS risk register where required.

 

4. External user, client and partner access governance

Govern access for external users, clients, agencies, partners and vendors.

This includes:

  • Defining standards for external user onboarding, approval, permissions, expiry and offboarding.
  • Ensuring external access has a clear business owner and justification.
  • Supporting access governance across client workspaces, agency environments, partner integrations and shared collaboration areas.
  • Working with Product and Engineering to ensure tenant, workspace and client-level isolation is appropriately governed.
  • Tracking risks related to stale accounts, vendor access, partner permissions and external user overprivilege.

 

5. Service account, machine identity and API access governance

Govern non-human access across DTS systems and platforms.

This includes:

  • Defining standards for service accounts, machine identities, automation users, API keys, tokens, secrets and integration credentials.
  • Ensuring non-human access has clear ownership, purpose, scope, rotation, expiry and auditability.
  • Working with Product, Engineering, Cloud Security and Infrastructure to reduce unmanaged credential risk.
  • Ensuring service accounts and machine identities are included in access reviews.
  • Supporting stronger governance of API access, token issuance, credential lifecycle and integration permissions.

 

6. AI and agentic access governance

Define and oversee the governance model for AI agents and agentic workflows across DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining how AI agents are identified, permissioned, monitored, reviewed and revoked.
  • Ensuring agents have clear ownership, scoped permissions and auditable actions.
  • Defining which agent actions require human approval or additional control.
  • Governing agent access to APIs, tools, datasets, workflows, client environments and production capabilities.
  • Ensuring agents act within delegated authority and cannot exceed the permissions of the user, system or business process they represent.
  • Working with Product, Architecture and Security to ensure agentic workflows are designed with clear action boundaries.
  • Working with the Product, Application and Offensive Security Lead to test whether agent permissions and action boundaries can be bypassed.
  • Working with Privacy Engineering to ensure AI access models support permitted use, minimisation and data protection requirements.

7. Data access governance

Govern access to sensitive, client, partner and WPP-owned data across DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining standards for dataset access approval, review, revocation and evidence.
  • Supporting data classification from an access-control and security-governance perspective.
  • Ensuring access to sensitive data is role-based, purpose-based, least-privileged and auditable.
  • Supporting controls for cross-client, cross-market, cross-agency and partner data access.
  • Ensuring data access governance supports InfoSum, Open Intelligence, Resolve, WPP Open and other DTS data collaboration use cases.
  • Working with Privacy Engineering on data minimisation, permitted use, retention and privacy-by-design requirements.
  • Ensuring data access risks are surfaced through the DTS risk process.

 

8. Governance of access to tools, workflows and actions

Ensure access governance extends beyond systems and datasets into tools, workflows and actions.

This includes:

  • Defining governance for access to operational tools, workflow automation, orchestration systems, AI tools and administrative actions.
  • Ensuring high-risk actions are subject to appropriate approval, logging and monitoring.
  • Supporting segregation of duties across sensitive workflows.
  • Ensuring automated workflows and agents have clearly scoped authority.
  • Working with Security Operations to ensure high-risk access and actions are visible in monitoring and detection processes.

 

9. Auditability, evidence and reporting

Maintain clear evidence of access governance and support audit and assurance requirements.

This includes:

  • Producing access governance evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001, client assurance, internal audit and risk reviews.
  • Working with the ISMS and Risk Officer to ensure access controls, reviews, exceptions and remediation actions are documented.
  • Reporting on access review completion, high-risk access, overdue actions and access control gaps.
  • Supporting client and audit questions related to identity, access, privileged roles, service accounts, AI agents and data access.
  • Ensuring access governance is repeatable, measurable and auditable.

 

Who you'll be working with:

The Senior Identity and Access Security Engineer will be accountable for:

  • DTS identity and access governance standards.
  • Regular access reviews and recertification.
  • Privileged access governance.
  • External user, client, partner and vendor access governance.
  • Service account, machine identity, API key and token governance.
  • AI agent identity, permission and action governance.
  • Dataset and sensitive data access governance.
  • Governance of access to tools, workflows and high-risk actions.
  • Access governance evidence for audit, compliance and client assurance.
  • Escalation of material access risks into the DTS risk process.

 

What you'll need:

The successful candidate will have:

  • Experience in identity governance, access management, IAM, security governance, GRC, data access control or platform security.
  • Strong understanding of least privilege, role-based access control, attribute-based access control, access reviews, privileged access and segregation of duties.
  • Experience governing access across SaaS platforms, cloud environments, APIs, data platforms or enterprise technology estates.
  • Knowledge of identity platforms such as Okta, Auth0, Keycloak, Azure AD / Entra ID or similar.
  • Understanding of service accounts, machine identities, API keys, tokens, secrets and non-human access governance.
  • Understanding of AI agents, agentic workflows, delegated authority and tool-access governance would be highly valuable.
  • Understanding of data classification, dataset access governance, privacy-by-design and audit requirements.
  • Ability to work across security, architecture, product, engineering, infrastructure, legal, privacy and compliance teams.
  • Strong organisational skills and ability to coordinate reviews, evidence, remediation and reporting.
  • Ability to translate complex access issues into clear risks, controls and practical actions.

 

Leadership expectations

The Senior Identity and Access Security Engineer is expected to:

  • Be structured, disciplined and pragmatic.
  • Bring clarity to complex access and permission models.
  • Challenge excessive, unclear or poorly governed access.
  • Work constructively with product and engineering teams to design workable controls.
  • Avoid creating unnecessary bureaucracy while ensuring access is properly governed.
  • Treat human, machine and agent access as part of the same control landscape.
  • Escalate material access risks clearly and early.
  • Support DTS in building a secure, auditable and scalable access governance model.

 

Success measures

Success in the role will be measured by:

  • DTS having clear identity, access and data access governance standards.
  • Regular access reviews completed on schedule with evidence.
  • Reduction in stale, excessive, orphaned or poorly owned access.
  • Stronger governance of privileged access and production access.
  • Clear ownership and review of service accounts, machine identities, API keys and tokens.
  • Defined governance for AI agent identities, permissions and actions.
  • Improved auditability of access to data, APIs, tools, workflows and production systems.
  • Better alignment between identity, security, privacy, architecture, product and engineering teams.
  • Material access risks being visible through the DTS risk register and Risk Review Board.
  • Increased confidence that DTS can answer: who or what has access to what, why, and when was it last reviewed?

WPP Open is our AI platform for marketing, connecting marketing professionals, data, tools and AI in one place. It is the simplest, safest and fastest way to realize the benefits of AI at scale—delivering better-informed creative ideas faster, at greater scale and lower cost. Our proprietary, opt-in media solutions give clients access to unique advantages and cutting-edge capabilities through a single point of access to addressable media, combining premium inventory with universal customer signals. They enable cross-channel storytelling, cross-platform AI optimisation and robust measurement of business impact to maximise campaign effectiveness.

About the team:


Strategic Initiatives & Applied Research works at the intersection of emerging technology, client
demand and WPP’s product strategy. We build production-lite solutions to test strategically
important opportunities, prove their technical and commercial value, and turn successful work
into reusable capabilities for Product and Engineering.


Our first major programme is agentic media buying, but our remit is broader: applied AI,
agent-to-agent workflows, new platform connections and other emerging opportunities to help
shape the future of WPP’s products. We want generalists who are happy to move onto the next
frontier problem once this one is proven.


The role


Forward Deployed Engineers are hands-on product engineers who work close to clients,
publishers and the market. You will combine technical depth with commercial understanding and
consultancy-style problem solving: helping to define a problem, building the solution, testing it in
a real setting and translating what works into reusable technical capability.
This is neither isolated prototyping nor slide-led consulting. You will be accountable from
discovery through implementation, field validation and handover.


What you'll do


- Build and ship working systems fast - agentic workflows, data pipelines, interfaces and
integrations. All centered on answering a commercial question, not a technical one.
- Work directly with external partners, clients, internal operational and commercial teams
to translate ambiguous problems into deliverable technical outcomes.


- Build at production-lite quality: moving quickly while incorporating observability,
validation, sensible testing and graceful failure rather than creating either disposable
prototypes or prematurely over-engineered systems.


- Build the business case alongside the build: what it's worth, who pays for it, what it costs
to scale.


What you’ll bring


- experience in software engineering, data science or a related field, with a track record of
getting things into real use.

- Strong Python and hands-on cloud experience


- Demonstrable experience building agentic/LLM systems - tool and structured calling
orchestration, evaluation, and a realistic view of what breaks when you try to get
production value out of them.


- Consultancy-style experience gained through consulting, professional services, solutions
engineering, forward deployment or an internal business-transformation function.


- Strong product and commercial judgement, with the ability to communicate technical
choices and business implications to technical and non-technical stakeholders.


- Comfort operating in ambiguity, learning unfamiliar domains quickly and balancing speed
with operational credibility.


- Willingness to travel internationally several times a year and develop a strong working
knowledge of media and advertising technology.


Nice to have


- Exposure to ad tech or media: ad servers, SSPs/DSPs, programmatic, or order
management systems


- Front-end or dashboarding skills for building demonstrable interfaces

We believe the best work happens when we're together, fostering creativity, collaboration, and connection. That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. If you require accommodations or flexibility, please discuss this with the hiring team during the interview process.

job.title: Lead Software Engineer
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

 

Title: Lead Software Engineer

Level: Lead Engineer, Data & Technology Solutions

Location: Copenhagen

Reporting to: Director of Engineering

About Open Intelligence:

We are the Activation arm of WPP Open Intelligence. Our team builds the foundational data infrastructure and high-performance edge services that power WPP’s position in the market. With approximately one-third of all global media spend flowing through WPP, our platform operates at the core of this massive network-deeply integrated and adopted by the largest supply-side partners in the AdTech industry. Operating at our scale presents unique engineering challenges. Our edge services currently handle over 60,000 classification requests per second, while our contextual classification pipelines process 10,000 requests per second. With operations spanning the US, UK, and ongoing expansion into EMEA and APAC, our infrastructure continuously interacts with up to 98% of the population in our active markets. We are an engineering-led team focused on building robust, scalable, and highly reliable systems.

 

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for a Lead Software Engineer who thrives on owning backend systems end to end — architecture, delivery, and the people who build them. You care more about sound software design, reliable APIs, and clear ownership than about any single framework or language.

You are comfortable setting technical direction for a squad, mentoring engineers, and turning product roadmap into shippable, versioned contracts. Hands-on when it matters, you design and operate services, partner integrations, and orchestration components in production — authentication, retries, idempotency, rate limiting, and the operational discipline that keeps live systems healthy. You are likely highly proficient in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Java/Kotlin, and experienced with cloud platforms, containers/Kubernetes, CI/CD, and production observability. Interest in infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform), durable workflows, and AI coding assistants is a plus when it helps the team ship faster without lowering the quality bar.

Beyond the technical craft, you are a strong communicator who can explain trade-offs to engineers, Product, and non-technical stakeholders, and align sibling teams on interfaces. You take ownership of reliability and technical debt for the systems your squad runs, escalate blockers early with clear options, and are motivated by growing both the platform and the engineers who build it.

 

WHY ARE WE HIRING We are at a critical inflection point in our growth and need to scale our engineering team to tackle an expanding set of complex challenges. As the digital ecosystem evolves, we are actively developing and releasing a new catalog of privacy-preserving data products. These solutions are designed to scale advanced targeting capabilities while remaining uncompromising on our promise to protect user privacy.

To support this product evolution, our infrastructure is undergoing massive global expansion. By the end of this year, we will be fully operational across the rest of the EMEA and APAC regions. Concurrently, we are deepening our integrations to support even more of the largest supply-side partners in the AdTech industry. We are hiring because we need strong engineering talent to help us architect for this next order of magnitude in scale-ensuring our systems remain resilient, performant, and compliant as our global footprint and feature set rapidly expand.

 

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

· Lead an engineering squad: set technical direction, prioritize delivery, run design and code reviews, and grow engineers through mentoring and clear ownership.

· Own the architecture and health of activation and orchestration services — API, databases, partner gateways, internal integrations, MCP and agentic integrations.

· Partner with Product and sibling teams to turn roadmap phases into shippable, versioned contracts — not ad hoc

integrations.

· Drive API integration engineering: authentication, rate limiting, idempotency, retries, partial-update patterns, and runbooks as partner APIs evolve.

· Establish and uphold production standards — CI/CD, testing, observability, auditability, and safe release practices.

· Keep an end-to-end overview of how data flow through activation — what is live, what is in progress, and where dependencies or technical debt block the next phase.

· Contribute hands-on where it matters: critical paths, new gateways, framework foundations (e.g. tool registry, workflow runtime, guardrails hooks).

· Identify and address technical debt deliberately; balance speed with reliability for systems that support live campaigns.

· Share knowledge in design reviews, stand-ups, and cross-team forums; escalate blockers early with clear options.

· Stay curious about agentic orchestration, durable workflows, and AI coding assistants to improve how the team designs and ships software.

 

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

· Strong communication — you explain trade-offs to engineers, product, and non-technical stakeholders and align multiple teams on interfaces.

· 6+ years in software engineering with 2+ years leading engineers or owning a significant technical area (team lead, staff, or equivalent).

· Proven delivery of backend and API-centric systems in production — services, integrations, or platforms at meaningful scale.

· Solid experience building and operating REST/HTTP APIs and event- or workflow-driven systems (durable state, async jobs, or orchestration).

· Comfort owning third-party integrations — auth, errors, versioning, operational monitoring, and partner-driven change.

· Strong proficiency in at least one backend language (e.g. Python, Go, or Java/Kotlin) and sound software design (patterns, testing, code review).

· Experience with CI/CD, Git, and testing — unit, integration, and boundary/contract tests where APIs matter.

· Experience with cloud platforms (GCP, AWS, or Azure) and deploying services with containers and Kubernetes.

· Familiarity with infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform) and production observability (metrics, logs, tracing).

· A track record of technical debt and reliability ownership — incidents, postmortems, and systemic fixes, not one-off firefighting.

· Interest in leveraging AI coding assistants and prompt engineering to improve team productivity without lowering the production bar.

 

NICE TO HAVE

· Experience leading delivery of orchestration, workflow, or agentic systems (tool registries, policy/guardrails, human-in-the-loop flows).

· Full-stack exposure — internal UIs or ops tools (e.g. change logs, escalations) backed by the same APIs you own.

· Familiarity with AdTech / MarTech — SSPs, DSPs, deals, audiences, or campaign activation terminology.

· Experience in a monorepo or large shared codebase with many integration surfaces.

· Awareness of data privacy and safe handling of sensitive data in distributed deployments.

· Prior work on audit trails or decision logs for high-trust or automated systems.

If you are ready to be at the forefront of the AdTech industry, shaping its future, and driving success for both our clients, we encourage you to apply and join our team.

job.title: Manager, Data Revenue Operations
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

About Data & Technology Solutions

WPP’s Data & Technology Solutions is WPP’s unified global data and technology team. We work with our agencies and clients to build data-driven solutions and technology that power marketing transformation.

WPP Open is our AI platform for marketing. It connects marketing professionals, data, tools and AI in a single place. WPP Open is the simplest, safest and fastest way to realize the benefits of scaled AI—delivering better-informed creative ideas faster, at scale and at lower cost.

We’re endlessly curious and our team of thinkers, builders, creators and problem solvers are over 2,000 strong, across 20 markets around the world.

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are seeking a commercially minded and analytically strong Manager, Data Revenue Operations to own revenue and usage reporting across WPP’s data distribution ecosystem.

Reporting to the Director of Platform Data Strategy, this role will ensure revenue generated through platform and distribution partners is reported completely, accurately and on time. The Manager will proactively manage partner reporting, validate and reconcile revenue and usage, investigate discrepancies and potential revenue leakage, and provide clear visibility into the performance of the platform data business.

Beyond reporting, this role will turn platform revenue and usage data into actionable business intelligence—identifying what is driving performance, where demand is emerging and where opportunities exist to grow the business.

You are:

  • Analytically minded, with the ability to identify patterns, anomalies and opportunities across complex datasets

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Revenue Analysis and Business Insights: Analyze revenue and usage across platforms, buyers, audiences and data offerings to understand performance drivers, identify emerging trends and surface high-growth or underpenetrated areas of the business.

Growth Opportunity Identification: Translate revenue and usage trends into actionable recommendations, identifying emerging demand, new buyers and use cases, underpenetrated areas and opportunities to increase adoption and revenue.

Finance and Commercial Partnership: Partner closely with Finance to support monthly revenue processing, accruals, reconciliation, forecasting and revenue recognition, while providing Data Strategy and commercial stakeholders with clear visibility into business performance.

Reporting and Business Reviews: Develop recurring reporting and business reviews that clearly communicate revenue performance, key drivers, risks, anomalies and growth opportunities.

Process Improvement and Automation: Standardize reporting and reconciliation processes across platforms and identify opportunities to automate report collection, ingestion, validation and analysis to improve accuracy and scalability.

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

  • 5+ years of experience in revenue operations, data operations, business operations, revenue analytics or a related function
  • Experience within digital advertising, AdTech, programmatic media, audience data or data marketplaces strongly preferred
  • Understanding of DSPs, SSPs, publishers, data marketplaces and data distribution platforms
  • Experience working with usage-based revenue models, CPM pricing, revenue-share arrangements or similar commercial structures
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with experience working across disparate datasets
  • Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills; SQL and experience with BI/reporting tools are highly desirable
  • Strong attention to detail and demonstrated ability to identify and investigate reporting discrepancies
  • Ability to move beyond reporting what happened to understand why it happened, what it means and what opportunities it creates for the business
  • Highly organized, proactive and comfortable operating in both structured and ambiguous environments

BURSON BUCHANAN

MANAGING DIRECTOR

JOB PURPOSE

As a Managing Director at Burson Buchanan, you will be a principal growth engine, client counsellor, and key leader within our premier strategic advisory boutique. Burson Buchanan delivers high-level advisory and communications support to clients on major capital markets events, ongoing financial communications, high-profile litigation and government investigations, crises and other reputation-defining events. Backed by Burson’s global network and market-leading data, analytics and AI tools, Burson Buchanan is defining strategic communications advisory for the intelligence era.

As a business generator, you will leverage your deep network of relationships within the advisory community—including leading investment banks, law firms and other advisory firms—and in the executive ranks and boardrooms of leading companies to help originate new business leads and opportunities. As a strategic senior counsellor, you will oversee accounts and lead teams in responding to the market-shaping events faced by Burson Buchanan clients, ensuring we consistently deliver excellent client work while driving sustainable account growth and long-term client retention.

As a member of the Burson Buchanan Senior Leadership Team (SLT), you will help shape the strategic direction of the firm. Leading by example, you will set the tone for a team culture that is built on high performance, teamwork, and open and respectful feedback to continue to elevate the value we bring to clients.

CLIENT & STRATEGIC ADVISORY

  • Advise and lead: serve as a trusted, high-level strategic advisor at the C-suite and Board level, delivering peer-to-peer counsel on complex capital markets activity (e.g., M&A, IPOs, shareholder activism situations) as well as high-stakes reputational issues (e.g., crisis/issues management and litigation).
  • Innovate: Position Burson Buchanan as the UK’s premier strategic comms advisory by seamlessly blending deep capital markets acumen with Burson’s state-of-the-art AI technology suite. Leverage Burson’s global network to support clients across multi-jurisdictional financial and corporate communications challenges.
  • Market leader: Maintain a comprehensive, forward-looking understanding of global capital markets, macroeconomic drivers, regulatory shifts, and competitive dynamics to add transformative value to client mandates.
  • Client service leader: Lead complex client accounts and major transaction mandates, ensuring flawless execution, game-changing strategic positioning, and the highest standards of quality control across all deliverables.
  • Lead by example: Operate with a true “player-coach” mindset—demonstrating the agility to transition seamlessly from board-level counsel to rolling up your sleeves on core deliverables, taking proactive ownership to solve both client and firm-wide challenges.

 

COMMERCIAL & BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT

  • Origination & growth: act as a primary business generator for Burson Buchanan. Proactively identify, target, and convert high-value new business opportunities that advance the firm’s commercial priorities.
  • Network & brand ambassador: serve as a prominent external ambassador for Burson Buchanan through market commentary, event participation, and senior industry networking to enhance agency profile and lead pipeline.
  • Cross-agency opportunities: proactively identify cross-selling opportunities across the broader Burson and WPP networks, bringing multi-disciplinary capability to capital markets clients.

LEADERSHIP, PEOPLE & CULTURE

  • Senior Leadership Team: serve as an active member of the SLT, contributing directly to agency-wide strategy, operational excellence, talent strategy, and long-term positioning.
  • High-performance culture: model leadership behaviours, setting a benchmark for ambition, strategic depth, and commercial urgency across a high-functioning team of advisors—while helping to build a culture that fosters connection and respect.
  • Talent development & mentorship: line manage, mentor, and inspire talent, fostering career growth and retention within the financial comms practice.
  • AI & innovation leadership: lead by example in the adoption of innovative solutions for our clients, including AI-driven communications tools, ensuring team adherence to WPP tools, ethical frameworks, and best practices.

job.title: OKTA Engineer - SSO
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

Why we're hiring:

The Senior Identity and Access security Engineer is responsible for governing who, and what, can access DTS systems, data, APIs, tools, workflows and AI-enabled capabilities.

This is a hands-on governance and control role, reporting into the SVP Security and Compliance. The role ensures that access across DTS is appropriate, auditable, reviewed, least-privileged and aligned with security, privacy, compliance and client commitments.

The scope covers traditional human access, external users, privileged access, service accounts, machine identities, API keys, tokens, dataset access, and the emerging governance of AI agents and agentic workflows.

The role will work closely with Architecture, Security, Product, Engineering, Infrastructure, Privacy, Legal/DPO, TechOps, Enterprise Technology and the ISMS and Risk Officer to ensure DTS has a clear and controlled model for access across platforms such as WPP Open, Choreograph, InfoSum, Open Intelligence, Resolve and related DTS capabilities.

 

What you'll be doing:

1. Identity and access governance framework

Define and maintain the access governance framework for DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining access governance standards, processes and control expectations.
  • Establishing how access should be requested, approved, provisioned, reviewed, revoked and evidenced.
  • Ensuring access governance covers internal users, external users, clients, partners, vendors, service accounts, machine identities and AI agents.
  • Aligning identity and access governance with DTS architecture, security, privacy, compliance and data governance requirements.
  • Ensuring access governance is practical for product and engineering teams to implement.

 

2. Access reviews and recertification

Own the process for regular access reviews and recertification across DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining the scope, frequency and evidence requirements for access reviews.
  • Coordinating access reviews for critical DTS systems, production environments, privileged roles, sensitive datasets, client-facing platforms and administrative tools.
  • Ensuring access review outcomes are tracked, remediated and evidenced.
  • Identifying stale, excessive, orphaned or poorly owned access.
  • Escalating overdue, high-risk or unresolved access issues through the appropriate governance channels.

 

3. Privileged access governance

Ensure privileged access across DTS is properly controlled, justified and auditable.

This includes:

  • Reviewing access to production systems, cloud environments, security tools, databases, CI/CD tooling, administrative consoles and sensitive platforms.
  • Supporting least-privilege, just-in-time and time-bound access models where appropriate.
  • Working with Cloud and Platform Security and Infrastructure to improve privileged access controls.
  • Ensuring privileged access risks are visible in the DTS risk register where required.

 

4. External user, client and partner access governance

Govern access for external users, clients, agencies, partners and vendors.

This includes:

  • Defining standards for external user onboarding, approval, permissions, expiry and offboarding.
  • Ensuring external access has a clear business owner and justification.
  • Supporting access governance across client workspaces, agency environments, partner integrations and shared collaboration areas.
  • Working with Product and Engineering to ensure tenant, workspace and client-level isolation is appropriately governed.
  • Tracking risks related to stale accounts, vendor access, partner permissions and external user overprivilege.

 

5. Service account, machine identity and API access governance

Govern non-human access across DTS systems and platforms.

This includes:

  • Defining standards for service accounts, machine identities, automation users, API keys, tokens, secrets and integration credentials.
  • Ensuring non-human access has clear ownership, purpose, scope, rotation, expiry and auditability.
  • Working with Product, Engineering, Cloud Security and Infrastructure to reduce unmanaged credential risk.
  • Ensuring service accounts and machine identities are included in access reviews.
  • Supporting stronger governance of API access, token issuance, credential lifecycle and integration permissions.

 

6. AI and agentic access governance

Define and oversee the governance model for AI agents and agentic workflows across DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining how AI agents are identified, permissioned, monitored, reviewed and revoked.
  • Ensuring agents have clear ownership, scoped permissions and auditable actions.
  • Defining which agent actions require human approval or additional control.
  • Governing agent access to APIs, tools, datasets, workflows, client environments and production capabilities.
  • Ensuring agents act within delegated authority and cannot exceed the permissions of the user, system or business process they represent.
  • Working with Product, Architecture and Security to ensure agentic workflows are designed with clear action boundaries.
  • Working with the Product, Application and Offensive Security Lead to test whether agent permissions and action boundaries can be bypassed.
  • Working with Privacy Engineering to ensure AI access models support permitted use, minimisation and data protection requirements.

7. Data access governance

Govern access to sensitive, client, partner and WPP-owned data across DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining standards for dataset access approval, review, revocation and evidence.
  • Supporting data classification from an access-control and security-governance perspective.
  • Ensuring access to sensitive data is role-based, purpose-based, least-privileged and auditable.
  • Supporting controls for cross-client, cross-market, cross-agency and partner data access.
  • Ensuring data access governance supports InfoSum, Open Intelligence, Resolve, WPP Open and other DTS data collaboration use cases.
  • Working with Privacy Engineering on data minimisation, permitted use, retention and privacy-by-design requirements.
  • Ensuring data access risks are surfaced through the DTS risk process.

 

8. Governance of access to tools, workflows and actions

Ensure access governance extends beyond systems and datasets into tools, workflows and actions.

This includes:

  • Defining governance for access to operational tools, workflow automation, orchestration systems, AI tools and administrative actions.
  • Ensuring high-risk actions are subject to appropriate approval, logging and monitoring.
  • Supporting segregation of duties across sensitive workflows.
  • Ensuring automated workflows and agents have clearly scoped authority.
  • Working with Security Operations to ensure high-risk access and actions are visible in monitoring and detection processes.

 

9. Auditability, evidence and reporting

Maintain clear evidence of access governance and support audit and assurance requirements.

This includes:

  • Producing access governance evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001, client assurance, internal audit and risk reviews.
  • Working with the ISMS and Risk Officer to ensure access controls, reviews, exceptions and remediation actions are documented.
  • Reporting on access review completion, high-risk access, overdue actions and access control gaps.
  • Supporting client and audit questions related to identity, access, privileged roles, service accounts, AI agents and data access.
  • Ensuring access governance is repeatable, measurable and auditable.

 

Who you'll be working with:

The Senior Identity and Access Security Engineer will be accountable for:

  • DTS identity and access governance standards.
  • Regular access reviews and recertification.
  • Privileged access governance.
  • External user, client, partner and vendor access governance.
  • Service account, machine identity, API key and token governance.
  • AI agent identity, permission and action governance.
  • Dataset and sensitive data access governance.
  • Governance of access to tools, workflows and high-risk actions.
  • Access governance evidence for audit, compliance and client assurance.
  • Escalation of material access risks into the DTS risk process.

 

What you'll need:

The successful candidate will have:

  • Experience in identity governance, access management, IAM, security governance, GRC, data access control or platform security.
  • Strong understanding of least privilege, role-based access control, attribute-based access control, access reviews, privileged access and segregation of duties.
  • Experience governing access across SaaS platforms, cloud environments, APIs, data platforms or enterprise technology estates.
  • Knowledge of identity platforms such as Okta, Auth0, Keycloak, Azure AD / Entra ID or similar.
  • Understanding of service accounts, machine identities, API keys, tokens, secrets and non-human access governance.
  • Understanding of AI agents, agentic workflows, delegated authority and tool-access governance would be highly valuable.
  • Understanding of data classification, dataset access governance, privacy-by-design and audit requirements.
  • Ability to work across security, architecture, product, engineering, infrastructure, legal, privacy and compliance teams.
  • Strong organisational skills and ability to coordinate reviews, evidence, remediation and reporting.
  • Ability to translate complex access issues into clear risks, controls and practical actions.

 

Leadership expectations

The Senior Identity and Access Security Engineer is expected to:

  • Be structured, disciplined and pragmatic.
  • Bring clarity to complex access and permission models.
  • Challenge excessive, unclear or poorly governed access.
  • Work constructively with product and engineering teams to design workable controls.
  • Avoid creating unnecessary bureaucracy while ensuring access is properly governed.
  • Treat human, machine and agent access as part of the same control landscape.
  • Escalate material access risks clearly and early.
  • Support DTS in building a secure, auditable and scalable access governance model.

 

Success measures

Success in the role will be measured by:

  • DTS having clear identity, access and data access governance standards.
  • Regular access reviews completed on schedule with evidence.
  • Reduction in stale, excessive, orphaned or poorly owned access.
  • Stronger governance of privileged access and production access.
  • Clear ownership and review of service accounts, machine identities, API keys and tokens.
  • Defined governance for AI agent identities, permissions and actions.
  • Improved auditability of access to data, APIs, tools, workflows and production systems.
  • Better alignment between identity, security, privacy, architecture, product and engineering teams.
  • Material access risks being visible through the DTS risk register and Risk Review Board.
  • Increased confidence that DTS can answer: who or what has access to what, why, and when was it last reviewed?

Who you are:

You're open: We are inclusive and collaborative; we encourage the free exchange of ideas; we respect and celebrate diverse views. We are open-minded: to new ideas, new partnerships, new ways of working.

You're optimistic: We believe in the power of creativity, technology and talent to create brighter futures or our people, our clients and our communities. We approach all that we do with conviction: to try the new and to seek the unexpected.

You're extraordinary: we are stronger together: through collaboration we achieve the amazing. We are creative leaders and pioneers of our industry; we provide extraordinary every day.

 

What we'll give you:

Passionate, inspired people – We aim to create a culture in which people can do extraordinary work.

Scale and opportunity – We offer the opportunity to create, influence and complete projects at a scale that is unparalleled in the industry.

Challenging and stimulating work – Unique work and the opportunity to join a group of creative problem solvers. Are you up for the challenge?

#LI-Hybrid

That's why we’ve adopted a hybrid approach, with teams in the office around four days a week. Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

Why we're hiring:

The Senior Identity and Access security Engineer is responsible for governing who, and what, can access DTS systems, data, APIs, tools, workflows and AI-enabled capabilities.

This is a hands-on governance and control role, reporting into the SVP Security and Compliance. The role ensures that access across DTS is appropriate, auditable, reviewed, least-privileged and aligned with security, privacy, compliance and client commitments.

The scope covers traditional human access, external users, privileged access, service accounts, machine identities, API keys, tokens, dataset access, and the emerging governance of AI agents and agentic workflows.

The role will work closely with Architecture, Security, Product, Engineering, Infrastructure, Privacy, Legal/DPO, TechOps, Enterprise Technology and the ISMS and Risk Officer to ensure DTS has a clear and controlled model for access across platforms such as WPP Open, Choreograph, InfoSum, Open Intelligence, Resolve and related DTS capabilities.

 

What you'll be doing:

1. Identity and access governance framework

Define and maintain the access governance framework for DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining access governance standards, processes and control expectations.
  • Establishing how access should be requested, approved, provisioned, reviewed, revoked and evidenced.
  • Ensuring access governance covers internal users, external users, clients, partners, vendors, service accounts, machine identities and AI agents.
  • Aligning identity and access governance with DTS architecture, security, privacy, compliance and data governance requirements.
  • Ensuring access governance is practical for product and engineering teams to implement.

 

2. Access reviews and recertification

Own the process for regular access reviews and recertification across DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining the scope, frequency and evidence requirements for access reviews.
  • Coordinating access reviews for critical DTS systems, production environments, privileged roles, sensitive datasets, client-facing platforms and administrative tools.
  • Ensuring access review outcomes are tracked, remediated and evidenced.
  • Identifying stale, excessive, orphaned or poorly owned access.
  • Escalating overdue, high-risk or unresolved access issues through the appropriate governance channels.

 

3. Privileged access governance

Ensure privileged access across DTS is properly controlled, justified and auditable.

This includes:

  • Reviewing access to production systems, cloud environments, security tools, databases, CI/CD tooling, administrative consoles and sensitive platforms.
  • Supporting least-privilege, just-in-time and time-bound access models where appropriate.
  • Working with Cloud and Platform Security and Infrastructure to improve privileged access controls.
  • Ensuring privileged access risks are visible in the DTS risk register where required.

 

4. External user, client and partner access governance

Govern access for external users, clients, agencies, partners and vendors.

This includes:

  • Defining standards for external user onboarding, approval, permissions, expiry and offboarding.
  • Ensuring external access has a clear business owner and justification.
  • Supporting access governance across client workspaces, agency environments, partner integrations and shared collaboration areas.
  • Working with Product and Engineering to ensure tenant, workspace and client-level isolation is appropriately governed.
  • Tracking risks related to stale accounts, vendor access, partner permissions and external user overprivilege.

 

5. Service account, machine identity and API access governance

Govern non-human access across DTS systems and platforms.

This includes:

  • Defining standards for service accounts, machine identities, automation users, API keys, tokens, secrets and integration credentials.
  • Ensuring non-human access has clear ownership, purpose, scope, rotation, expiry and auditability.
  • Working with Product, Engineering, Cloud Security and Infrastructure to reduce unmanaged credential risk.
  • Ensuring service accounts and machine identities are included in access reviews.
  • Supporting stronger governance of API access, token issuance, credential lifecycle and integration permissions.

 

6. AI and agentic access governance

Define and oversee the governance model for AI agents and agentic workflows across DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining how AI agents are identified, permissioned, monitored, reviewed and revoked.
  • Ensuring agents have clear ownership, scoped permissions and auditable actions.
  • Defining which agent actions require human approval or additional control.
  • Governing agent access to APIs, tools, datasets, workflows, client environments and production capabilities.
  • Ensuring agents act within delegated authority and cannot exceed the permissions of the user, system or business process they represent.
  • Working with Product, Architecture and Security to ensure agentic workflows are designed with clear action boundaries.
  • Working with the Product, Application and Offensive Security Lead to test whether agent permissions and action boundaries can be bypassed.
  • Working with Privacy Engineering to ensure AI access models support permitted use, minimisation and data protection requirements.

7. Data access governance

Govern access to sensitive, client, partner and WPP-owned data across DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining standards for dataset access approval, review, revocation and evidence.
  • Supporting data classification from an access-control and security-governance perspective.
  • Ensuring access to sensitive data is role-based, purpose-based, least-privileged and auditable.
  • Supporting controls for cross-client, cross-market, cross-agency and partner data access.
  • Ensuring data access governance supports InfoSum, Open Intelligence, Resolve, WPP Open and other DTS data collaboration use cases.
  • Working with Privacy Engineering on data minimisation, permitted use, retention and privacy-by-design requirements.
  • Ensuring data access risks are surfaced through the DTS risk process.

 

8. Governance of access to tools, workflows and actions

Ensure access governance extends beyond systems and datasets into tools, workflows and actions.

This includes:

  • Defining governance for access to operational tools, workflow automation, orchestration systems, AI tools and administrative actions.
  • Ensuring high-risk actions are subject to appropriate approval, logging and monitoring.
  • Supporting segregation of duties across sensitive workflows.
  • Ensuring automated workflows and agents have clearly scoped authority.
  • Working with Security Operations to ensure high-risk access and actions are visible in monitoring and detection processes.

 

9. Auditability, evidence and reporting

Maintain clear evidence of access governance and support audit and assurance requirements.

This includes:

  • Producing access governance evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001, client assurance, internal audit and risk reviews.
  • Working with the ISMS and Risk Officer to ensure access controls, reviews, exceptions and remediation actions are documented.
  • Reporting on access review completion, high-risk access, overdue actions and access control gaps.
  • Supporting client and audit questions related to identity, access, privileged roles, service accounts, AI agents and data access.
  • Ensuring access governance is repeatable, measurable and auditable.

 

Who you'll be working with:

The Senior Identity and Access Security Engineer will be accountable for:

  • DTS identity and access governance standards.
  • Regular access reviews and recertification.
  • Privileged access governance.
  • External user, client, partner and vendor access governance.
  • Service account, machine identity, API key and token governance.
  • AI agent identity, permission and action governance.
  • Dataset and sensitive data access governance.
  • Governance of access to tools, workflows and high-risk actions.
  • Access governance evidence for audit, compliance and client assurance.
  • Escalation of material access risks into the DTS risk process.

 

What you'll need:

The successful candidate will have:

  • Experience in identity governance, access management, IAM, security governance, GRC, data access control or platform security.
  • Strong understanding of least privilege, role-based access control, attribute-based access control, access reviews, privileged access and segregation of duties.
  • Experience governing access across SaaS platforms, cloud environments, APIs, data platforms or enterprise technology estates.
  • Knowledge of identity platforms such as Okta, Auth0, Keycloak, Azure AD / Entra ID or similar.
  • Understanding of service accounts, machine identities, API keys, tokens, secrets and non-human access governance.
  • Understanding of AI agents, agentic workflows, delegated authority and tool-access governance would be highly valuable.
  • Understanding of data classification, dataset access governance, privacy-by-design and audit requirements.
  • Ability to work across security, architecture, product, engineering, infrastructure, legal, privacy and compliance teams.
  • Strong organisational skills and ability to coordinate reviews, evidence, remediation and reporting.
  • Ability to translate complex access issues into clear risks, controls and practical actions.

 

Leadership expectations

The Senior Identity and Access Security Engineer is expected to:

  • Be structured, disciplined and pragmatic.
  • Bring clarity to complex access and permission models.
  • Challenge excessive, unclear or poorly governed access.
  • Work constructively with product and engineering teams to design workable controls.
  • Avoid creating unnecessary bureaucracy while ensuring access is properly governed.
  • Treat human, machine and agent access as part of the same control landscape.
  • Escalate material access risks clearly and early.
  • Support DTS in building a secure, auditable and scalable access governance model.

 

Success measures

Success in the role will be measured by:

  • DTS having clear identity, access and data access governance standards.
  • Regular access reviews completed on schedule with evidence.
  • Reduction in stale, excessive, orphaned or poorly owned access.
  • Stronger governance of privileged access and production access.
  • Clear ownership and review of service accounts, machine identities, API keys and tokens.
  • Defined governance for AI agent identities, permissions and actions.
  • Improved auditability of access to data, APIs, tools, workflows and production systems.
  • Better alignment between identity, security, privacy, architecture, product and engineering teams.
  • Material access risks being visible through the DTS risk register and Risk Review Board.
  • Increased confidence that DTS can answer: who or what has access to what, why, and when was it last reviewed?

job.title: Security Threat Hunting Specialist
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

Why we're hiring:

The Threat Hunter is responsible for proactively identifying advanced threats that evade traditional security controls. This role involves hypothesis-driven investigations, leveraging threat intelligence, and analyzing telemetry across endpoints, networks, and cloud environments to uncover stealthy adversary activity. The Threat Hunter plays a critical role in reducing dwell time and strengthening organizational resilience under the Autonomic Security Operations model.

What you'll be doing:

Proactive Threat Hunting

  • Execute hypothesis-driven hunts based on adversary TTPs and threat intelligence.
  • Analyze telemetry from SIEM, EDR/XDR, NDR, and cloud-native platforms to identify anomalies.
  • Develop and maintain hunting queries and scripts for automation and repeatability.
  • Validate detection coverage through purple team exercises and adversary emulation.

Threat Intelligence Integration

  • Incorporate emerging threat intelligence into hunting hypotheses and detection pipelines.
  • Maintain awareness of global threat actor tactics, techniques, and procedures (MITRE ATT&CK).

Continuous Improvement

  • Document hunt findings and feed insights into detection engineering and SOC workflows.
  • Maintain a backlog of hunting hypotheses and visibility gaps for remediation.
  • Contribute to automation of hunting workflows using scripting and SOAR platforms.

Strategic Alignment to GCAT SOC10x

  • 10X People: Continuous learning and knowledge sharing within the team.
  • 10X Process: Embed agile, hypothesis-driven hunting workflows.
  • 10X Technology: Leverage AI/ML analytics for anomaly detection and hunt acceleration.
  • 10X Visibility: Ensure comprehensive telemetry ingestion across hybrid environments.
  • 10X Speed: Reduce dwell time and accelerate detection-to-response cycles.

 

What you'll need:

Technical Expertise

  • Strong knowledge of threat hunting methodologies and frameworks (MITRE ATT&CK, TaHiTI).
  • Proficiency in SIEM, EDR/XDR, and log aggregation tools across hybrid infrastructure.
  • Scripting skills (Python, PowerShell) for automation and data analysis.
  • Familiarity with threat intelligence integration and behavioral analytics.

Collaboration & Communication

  • Ability to work closely with SOC, IR, and engineering teams.
  • Skilled in documenting hunt outcomes and communicating findings effectively.

Certifications (Preferred)

  • GIAC GCTI, GCIH, or equivalent advanced security certifications.

Key Attributes

  • Automation-first mindset with focus on scalability and resilience.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

job.title: Senior Associate, Audience Solutions
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

About Data & Technology Solutions

WPP’s Data & Technology Solutions is WPP’s unified global data and technology team. We work with our agencies and clients to build data-driven solutions and technology that power marketing transformation.

WPP Open is our AI platform for marketing. It connects marketing professionals, data, tools and AI in a single place. WPP Open is the simplest, safest and fastest way to realize the benefits of scaled AI—delivering better-informed creative ideas faster, at scale and at lower cost.

We’re endlessly curious and our team of thinkers, builders, creators and problem solvers are over 2,000 strong, across 20 markets around the world.

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are seeking a solutions-driven Senior Associate, Audience Solutions to support audience creation and delivery across WPP’s activation ecosystem.

This role will serve as a key audience-building resource for Activation teams, translating campaign and audience requirements into executable audience builds within WPP’s audience tools.

The Senior Associate will manage audience requests from intake through delivery, identifying appropriate data and audience attributes, constructing audiences according to campaign requirements, conducting quality assurance, and ensuring audiences are available for activation.

The ideal candidate understands audience data and digital media activation, enjoys working hands-on within platforms, and can translate a business or campaign need into a well-constructed audience solution.

You are:

  • An audience data or AdTech professional with hands-on experience building audiences for digital media activation
  • Familiar with audience segmentation, Boolean logic, taxonomy, data marketplaces and audience activation workflows
  • Able to translate campaign requirements into clear and executable audience builds
  • Comfortable working directly with Activation teams and managing multiple audience requests simultaneously
  • Organized and responsive, with the ability to manage requests through established workflows and timelines
  • Familiar with workflow and ticketing systems such as Zendesk or Jira

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Audience Request Intake and Management: Manage audience requests from Activation teams, ensuring campaign objectives, audience requirements, timelines and activation destinations are clearly understood before audiences are built.

Audience Creation and Configuration: Translate audience requirements into executable builds within WPP’s audience tools, selecting appropriate audience attributes and applying segmentation and Boolean logic to create audiences that meet campaign needs.

Audience Recommendations: Help Activation teams navigate available audience options and identify appropriate data and segments based on the requirements provided, particularly where dedicated Data Strategy support is not available.

Quality Assurance: Review audience builds for accuracy, including segment selection, inclusion and exclusion logic, taxonomy, naming conventions, pricing and activation requirements before audiences are released for use.

Audience Delivery and Activation Readiness: Ensure completed audiences are correctly configured and available within the appropriate activation platforms and destinations.

Troubleshooting and Issue Resolution: Investigate audience availability, configuration, syndication and activation issues and drive issues through resolution.

Audience Documentation and Governance: Maintain accurate records of audience requests, builds, definitions, naming conventions and delivery status to support consistency, transparency and reuse.

Workflow and Process Management: Manage audience requests through established ticketing and workflow systems, maintaining accurate status, ownership and documentation and ensuring requests are completed within established timelines.

Workflow and Process Improvement: Identify recurring audience requests, operational challenges and opportunities to improve audience-building workflows, documentation and turnaround times.

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

  • 3+ years of experience in audience strategy, audience operations, data operations, programmatic media, AdTech or a related field
  • Hands-on experience creating or managing audiences for digital media activation
  • Understanding of audience segmentation, Boolean logic, demographic, behavioral and purchase-based data
  • Familiarity with DSPs, SSPs, DMPs, CDPs, audience marketplaces and other audience activation and distribution platforms
  • Understanding of how audiences move from data platforms into media activation environments
  • Experience with ticketing and workflow management tools such as Zendesk or Jira
  • Strong organizational and project-management skills with the ability to manage multiple requests and deadlines
  • Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Collaborative, proactive and comfortable working in both structured and ambiguous environments

If you are ready to be at the forefront of the AdTech industry, shaping its future, and driving success for both our clients, we encourage you to apply and join our team.

job.description:

The Team

The Global Commercial Finance team develops and embeds commercial best practice across WPP, supporting major global client relationships and working across agencies, markets and disciplines. The team provides commercial analysis, strengthens financial performance and helps ensure consistent approaches to scopes, pricing, reporting, working capital and contractual obligations.

We are seeking a Senior Commercial Analyst to join the Global Commercial team and provide dedicated commercial operations and financial support across a portfolio of key accounts. The role will own and coordinate core reporting, billing, forecasting, scope-management and financial processes, enabling senior team members to focus on strategic commercial priorities, negotiations and procurement relationships.

What you'll be doing

You will work as an integral member of the Global Commercial team, coordinating commercial information from multiple agencies, regions and markets. You will produce accurate, timely and decision-ready analysis, maintain disciplined commercial processes and build effective relationships across WPP Finance, Commercial and Operations teams. This role offers a unique opportunity to gain exposure across WPP’s broad capabilities, from Creative and Media to the wider network, while working across a diverse portfolio of clients. You will join an experienced commercial team that plays a key role in enabling new business, supporting growth and navigating complex commercial, operational and contractual matters.

Commercial and Financial Analysis

  • Consolidate and independently analyze financial and commercial analysis across a portfolio of global accounts.
  • Analyze financial performance, including, revenue, margin, forecasts, scopes, pricing, investment and other key commercial measures.
  • Coordinate and evalutate budget and quarterly reforecast analysis, including variance commentary and network follow-ups.
  • Independently produce global and regional reporting, identifying trends, risks, anomalies and required actions.
  • Work with agency Finance teams to investigate discrepancies and improve data accuracy and completeness.
  • Support finance, procurement and compliance requirements, including savings reporting, audits, rebate, spend analysis and supporting documentation.

Pricing, pitches and RFP support

  • Support pricing exercises, pitches and RFPs across existing and prospective accounts.
  • Coordinate and make recommendations on rates, staffing assumptions and pricing inputs from WPP agencies and markets.
  • Consolidate multi-agency pricing submissions and review them for completeness and consistency with scope requirements.
  • Support the development of staffing plans, fee models and associated commercial analysis.
  • Prepare benchmarking analysis on proposals

On-going Commercial Support

  • Act as a key Finance and Commercial point of contact across the WPP network for assigned accounts for day-to-day queries
  • Help implement consistent commercial processes and identify opportunities to simplify or automate recurring reporting.
  • Analyze financial performance, identify opportunities for optimization, and provide insightful reporting to key internal stakeholders.
  • Support contract-compliance monitoring, particularly payment terms and financial obligations.
  • Provide ad hoc commercial analysis and project support as required.
  • Develop and maintain commercial process documentation, guidance, FAQs and onboarding materials to support consistency across the WPP network.

 

Billing, working capital and scope management

  • Coordinate central billing processes, including billing status, purchase-order tracking and escalation of outstanding issues.
  • Monitor payment terms and support the resolution of working-capital and contract-compliance issues.
  • Oversee scope-management platforms and maintain accurate records of scopes, fees and commercial commitments.
  • Coordinate with agencies to ensure scope and billing information is complete, current and supported by appropriate documentation.
  • Support annual scope, resourcing and fee-planning processes.

Client Reporting

  • Lead recurring procurement reporting, including scopes, savings, performance measures and agreed commercial commitments Independently identify issues requiring management attention.
  • Manage data collection across agencies and markets, reviewing submissions for completeness and consistency.
  • Prepare clear, client-ready analysis and reporting for Commercial Directors.
  • Support commercial governance meetings and track actions through to completion.

Confident communicating with client and internal stakeholders, including navigating challenging commercial and procurement conversations.

What you'll need

  • Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in commercial finance, client finance, financial analysis or business operations.
  • Strong understanding of revenue, margin, forecasting, billing, accruals and working-capital principles.
  • Experience consolidating and analysing financial data across business units, markets or systems.
  • Experience supporting scopes of work, staffing plans, pricing or client financial reporting.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills
  • Excellent attention to detail, analytical judgement and commitment to data accuracy.
  • Strong organisation and project-coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple deadlines.
  • Confidence working with Finance and Commercial stakeholders across agencies, markets and levels of seniority.
